trait.en: Jesus forgives and heals
trait.af: Jesus vergewe en genees

en.title: Faith Through the Roof
story: News had spread that Jesus was back in Capernaum, and so many people crowded into the house where He was staying that there was no room left, not even outside the door. Jesus was teaching them God’s Word.
Four men arrived carrying a friend who was paralysed. He couldn’t walk or even move much. They had probably carried him a long way. But the crowd blocked every entrance.

Most people would have given up. These friends didn’t. Houses in Capernaum had flat roofs made of beams covered with branches and packed clay, with an outside staircase. So they climbed up, dug through the roof right above Jesus, and lowered their friend down on his mat.
Mark says, ‘When Jesus saw their faith…’ Notice that it was the friends’ faith He saw. Then He said something no one expected: ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’
Some teachers of the law sitting there thought, ‘He’s blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?’ They were right that only God can forgive sins. What they missed was who Jesus is.

Jesus knew their thoughts. He asked, ‘Which is easier: to say “Your sins are forgiven,” or to say “Get up, take your mat and walk”? But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.’ Then He turned to the man: ‘Get up, take your mat and go home.’
The man stood up, took his mat and walked out in full view of them all. Everyone was amazed and praised God: ‘We have never seen anything like this!’
Jesus heals bodies, but His greatest gift is forgiveness. And He sees the faith of friends who refuse to give up.

verse.text: Praise the Lord… who forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases.

lessons: Jesus has authority to forgive sins, because He is God’s Son.
Jesus heals, and His greatest gift is forgiveness.
Faithful friends don’t give up on bringing others to Jesus.
questions: What obstacles did the four friends face? How did they overcome them?
Why did Jesus forgive the man’s sins first?
Who is a friend you could ‘carry’ to Jesus in prayer?
en.listen: Be still and ask: ‘Lord, who do you want me to carry to you in prayer?’ Write down the names that come to mind, and pray for each one.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you forgive all my sins.
Thank you that you heal. I pray for…
Make me a friend who brings others to you.

mission.text: This week, choose one friend who needs Jesus and pray for them every day. Look for a way to help them.

en.journal: Draw the four friends on the roof. Write the names of four people you will ‘carry’ to Jesus in prayer this week.

af.title: Geloof deur die Dak
story: Die nuus het versprei dat Jesus terug was in Kapernaum, en so baie mense het in die huis waar Hy gebly het ingedruk dat daar geen plek oor was nie, nie eers buite die deur nie. Jesus het hulle God se Woord geleer.
Vier mans het aangekom en ’n vriend gedra wat verlam was. Hy kon nie loop of selfs veel beweeg nie. Hulle het hom seker ’n lang pad gedra. Maar die skare het elke ingang versper.

Die meeste mense sou moed opgegee het. Hierdie vriende het nie. Huise in Kapernaum het plat dakke gehad wat van balke gemaak is, bedek met takke en vasgedrukte klei, met ’n buitetrap. Toe het hulle opgeklim, deur die dak reg bo Jesus gegrawe, en hulle vriend op sy matjie laat afsak.
Markus sê: ‘Toe Jesus hulle geloof sien…’ Let op dat dit die vriende se geloof was wat Hy gesien het. Toe het Hy iets gesê wat niemand verwag het nie: ‘Seun, jou sondes is vergewe.’
Party wetsgeleerdes wat daar gesit het, het gedink: ‘Hy laster God! Wie kan sondes vergewe behalwe God alleen?’ Hulle was reg dat net God sondes kan vergewe. Wat hulle gemis het, was wie Jesus is.

Jesus het hulle gedagtes geken. Hy het gevra: ‘Wat is makliker: om te sê “Jou sondes is vergewe,” of om te sê “Staan op, vat jou matjie en loop”? Maar Ek wil hê julle moet weet dat die Seun van die mens gesag op aarde het om sondes te vergewe.’ Toe draai Hy na die man: ‘Staan op, vat jou matjie en gaan huis toe.’
Die man het opgestaan, sy matjie gevat en voor almal se oë uitgeloop. Almal was verbaas en het God geprys: ‘Ons het nog nooit so iets gesien nie!’
Jesus genees liggame, maar sy grootste geskenk is vergifnis. En Hy sien die geloof van vriende wat weier om moed op te gee.

verse.text: Prys die Here… wat al jou sondes vergewe en al jou siektes genees.

lessons: Jesus het gesag om sondes te vergewe, want Hy is God se Seun.
Jesus genees, en sy grootste geskenk is vergifnis.
Getroue vriende gee nie moed op om ander na Jesus te bring nie.
questions: Watter struikelblokke het die vier vriende gehad? Hoe het hulle dit oorkom?
Hoekom het Jesus eers die man se sondes vergewe?
Wie is ’n vriend wat jy in gebed na Jesus kan ‘dra’?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra: ‘Here, wie wil U hê moet ek in gebed na U dra?’ Skryf die name neer wat in jou gedagtes opkom, en bid vir elkeen.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U al my sondes vergewe.
Dankie dat U genees. Ek bid vir…
Maak my ’n vriend wat ander na U bring.

mission.text: Kies hierdie week een vriend wat Jesus nodig het en bid elke dag vir hulle. Soek ’n manier om hulle te help.

af.journal: Teken die vier vriende op die dak. Skryf die name van vier mense neer wat jy hierdie week in gebed na Jesus sal ‘dra’.

en.title: Who Can Forgive Sins?
story: Mark 2 is a story about a hole in a roof, but underneath it is a question about the identity of Jesus. It is the first of five conflict stories in Mark, in which Jesus’ authority is challenged.

The scene is crowded and dramatic. People pack the house so tightly that four men carrying a paralysed friend can’t get near. Their solution is bold, even destructive: they climb up, remove part of the roof (somebody’s roof!) and lower their friend into the middle of Jesus’ teaching. This is faith with sweat, dirt and determination.

Then Jesus surprises everyone. Instead of healing the man immediately, He says, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’ Why? Jesus isn’t saying the man’s paralysis was caused by a particular sin. Rather, Jesus addresses his deepest need first. A man can walk and still be far from God. Forgiveness is the greater healing.

The teachers of the law react inwardly: ‘Who can forgive sins but God alone?’ Theologically, they are correct. You can forgive someone who wrongs you, but only God can forgive sins against God. So by declaring forgiveness on His own authority, Jesus is claiming to do what only God does.

Jesus then reads their thoughts (something else only God can do) and asks a clever question: ‘Which is easier to say?’ Anyone can say ‘Your sins are forgiven’, because no one can see whether it happened. But saying ‘Get up and walk’ can be checked immediately. So Jesus does the visible miracle to prove the invisible one: ‘that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins’.

‘Son of Man’ was Jesus’ favourite title for Himself. It comes from Daniel 7, where ‘one like a son of man’ receives authority, glory and an everlasting kingdom from God. Jesus is quietly claiming to be that divine figure.

Psalm 103 praises the Lord ‘who forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases’. In Capernaum, Jesus did both, because He is the Lord. He is the same today: the One who forgives completely, who still heals, and who honours the faith of those who bring others to Him.

verse.text: But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.

lessons: By forgiving sins, Jesus claimed to do what only God can do.
Forgiveness is our deepest need and Jesus’ greatest gift.
Jesus still forgives and heals today, and honours persistent faith.
questions: Why were the teachers of the law right that only God can forgive sins? What did they miss?
How did the visible healing prove the invisible forgiveness?
What does it mean to you personally that Jesus has authority to forgive your sins?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Bring Jesus anything you need forgiveness for. Hear Him say, ‘Your sins are forgiven.’ Then ask whom He wants you to bring to Him. Write it down.
prayer: Jesus, Son of Man, you have authority to forgive sins.
Thank you for forgiving me for…
Give me persistent faith for my friend…

mission.text: This week, take a practical step to ‘bring a friend to Jesus’: invite them to church or youth group, or share what Jesus means to you.

en.journal: Read Daniel 7:13–14. Write what it tells you about the ‘Son of Man’ and why Jesus might have chosen that title.

af.title: Wie Kan Sondes Vergewe?
story: Markus 2 is ’n storie oor ’n gat in ’n dak, maar daaronder lê ’n vraag oor wie Jesus is. Dit is die eerste van vyf konflikstories in Markus, waarin Jesus se gesag uitgedaag word.

Die toneel is stampvol en dramaties. Mense druk so styf in die huis dat vier mans wat ’n verlamde vriend dra, nie naby kan kom nie. Hulle oplossing is dapper, selfs vernietigend: hulle klim op, verwyder ’n deel van die dak (iemand se dak!) en laat hulle vriend in die middel van Jesus se leer afsak. Dit is geloof met sweet, stof en vasberadenheid.

Dan verras Jesus almal. In plaas daarvan om die man dadelik te genees, sê Hy: ‘Seun, jou sondes is vergewe.’ Hoekom? Jesus sê nie die man se verlamming is deur ’n spesifieke sonde veroorsaak nie. Eerder spreek Jesus eers sy diepste behoefte aan. ’n Man kan loop en steeds ver van God af wees. Vergifnis is die groter genesing.

Die wetsgeleerdes reageer binne-in hulleself: ‘Wie kan sondes vergewe behalwe God alleen?’ Teologies is hulle reg. Jy kan iemand vergewe wat jou verontreg, maar net God kan sondes teen God vergewe. Deur vergifnis op sy eie gesag te verklaar, beweer Jesus dus dat Hy doen wat net God doen.

Jesus lees dan hulle gedagtes (nog iets wat net God kan doen) en vra ’n slim vraag: ‘Wat is makliker om te sê?’ Enigiemand kan sê ‘Jou sondes is vergewe’, want niemand kan sien of dit gebeur het nie. Maar om te sê ‘Staan op en loop’ kan dadelik getoets word. So doen Jesus die sigbare wonderwerk om die onsigbare een te bewys: ‘sodat julle kan weet dat die Seun van die mens gesag op aarde het om sondes te vergewe’.

‘Seun van die mens’ was Jesus se gunsteling-titel vir Homself. Dit kom uit Daniël 7, waar ‘een soos ’n mensekind’ gesag, heerlikheid en ’n ewige koninkryk van God ontvang. Jesus beweer stilweg dat Hy daardie goddelike figuur is.

Psalm 103 prys die Here ‘wat al jou sondes vergewe en al jou siektes genees’. In Kapernaum het Jesus albei gedoen, want Hy is die Here. Hy is vandag dieselfde: die Een wat heeltemal vergewe, wat nog genees, en wat die geloof eer van die wat ander na Hom bring.

verse.text: Maar Ek wil hê julle moet weet dat die Seun van die mens gesag op aarde het om sondes te vergewe.

lessons: Deur sondes te vergewe, het Jesus beweer dat Hy doen wat net God kan doen.
Vergifnis is ons diepste behoefte en Jesus se grootste geskenk.
Jesus vergewe en genees vandag nog, en eer volhardende geloof.
questions: Hoekom was die wetsgeleerdes reg dat net God sondes kan vergewe? Wat het hulle gemis?
Hoe het die sigbare genesing die onsigbare vergifnis bewys?
Wat beteken dit vir jou persoonlik dat Jesus gesag het om jou sondes te vergewe?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Bring vir Jesus enigiets waarvoor jy vergifnis nodig het. Hoor Hom sê: ‘Jou sondes is vergewe.’ Vra dan wie Hy wil hê jy na Hom moet bring. Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Jesus, Seun van die mens, U het gesag om sondes te vergewe.
Dankie dat U my vergewe vir…
Gee my volhardende geloof vir my vriend…

mission.text: Neem hierdie week ’n praktiese tree om ‘’n vriend na Jesus te bring’: nooi hulle na die kerk of jeug, of vertel wat Jesus vir jou beteken.

af.journal: Lees Daniël 7:13–14. Skryf wat dit jou vertel oor die ‘Seun van die mens’ en hoekom Jesus dalk daardie titel gekies het.

en.title: Friends Who Help
story: A man couldn’t walk.
His four friends carried him on a mat to see Jesus.
The house was too full! So they made a hole in the roof.
Down, down, down went the man, right in front of Jesus!
Jesus forgave him and made him well. He jumped up and walked!

verse.text: Jesus forgives and heals.

en.action: Lie down flat like the man on his mat, then jump up and walk around!
lessons: Jesus forgives me and makes me well.
questions: Can you jump up like the man?
prayer: Thank you, Jesus,
for forgiving me and helping me. Amen.

af.title: Maats wat Help
story: ’n Man kon nie loop nie.
Sy vier maats het hom op ’n matjie na Jesus gedra.
Die huis was te vol! Toe maak hulle ’n gat in die dak.
Af, af, af het die man gegaan, reg voor Jesus!
Jesus het hom vergewe en gesond gemaak. Hy het opgespring en geloop!

verse.text: Jesus vergewe en genees.

af.action: Lê plat soos die man op sy matjie, spring dan op en loop rond!
lessons: Jesus vergewe my en maak my gesond.
questions: Kan jy opspring soos die man?
prayer: Dankie, Jesus,
dat U my vergewe en help. Amen.

en.title: A Hole in the Roof
story: Jesus was teaching in a house in Capernaum. So many people came to hear Him that the house was packed. There wasn’t even room at the door!
Four friends arrived, carrying a man on a mat. Their friend couldn’t walk, and they were sure Jesus could help him. But they couldn’t get in. What would you do?

These friends didn’t give up. They climbed up onto the flat roof, dug a big hole in it, and carefully lowered their friend down on his mat, right in front of Jesus! Bits of roof must have been falling on everyone’s heads!

Jesus saw how much faith the friends had. He looked at the man kindly and said, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’ Some teachers grumbled, ‘Only God can forgive sins!’ They were right, and Jesus is God’s Son!

So Jesus said, ‘I want you to know that I have power to forgive sins.’ Then He said to the man, ‘Get up, take your mat and go home.’ And the man jumped up, picked up his mat and walked out in front of everyone!
The people were amazed. ‘We have never seen anything like this!’ they said, and they praised God.
Jesus forgives and heals. And good friends bring each other to Jesus.

verse.text: He forgives all your sins and heals all your sicknesses.

lessons: Jesus forgives and heals.
Good friends help each other come to Jesus.
Don’t give up when it’s hard to get to Jesus.
questions: What did the friends do when they couldn’t get in?
Who is a friend you could pray for or bring to Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that you forgive me and heal me.
Please help my friend…
and help me be a friend who brings people to you. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, pray for a friend who needs help, and do something kind for them.

af.title: ’n Gat in die Dak
story: Jesus was besig om in ’n huis in Kapernaum te leer. So baie mense het gekom om Hom te hoor dat die huis stampvol was. Daar was nie eers plek by die deur nie!
Vier maats het aangekom en ’n man op ’n matjie gedra. Hulle maat kon nie loop nie, en hulle was seker Jesus kon hom help. Maar hulle kon nie inkom nie. Wat sou jy doen?

Hierdie maats het nie moed opgegee nie. Hulle het op die plat dak geklim, ’n groot gat daarin gegrawe, en hulle maat versigtig op sy matjie laat sak, reg voor Jesus! Stukkies dak het seker op almal se koppe geval!

Jesus het gesien hoeveel geloof die maats gehad het. Hy het die man vriendelik aangekyk en gesê: ‘Seun, jou sondes is vergewe.’ Party leraars het gekla: ‘Net God kan sondes vergewe!’ Hulle was reg, en Jesus is God se Seun!

Toe sê Jesus: ‘Ek wil hê julle moet weet dat Ek mag het om sondes te vergewe.’ Toe sê Hy vir die man: ‘Staan op, vat jou matjie en gaan huis toe.’ En die man het opgespring, sy matjie opgetel en voor almal uitgeloop!
Die mense was verbaas. ‘Ons het nog nooit so iets gesien nie!’ het hulle gesê, en hulle het God geprys.
Jesus vergewe en genees. En goeie maats bring mekaar na Jesus.

verse.text: Hy vergewe al jou sondes en genees al jou siektes.

lessons: Jesus vergewe en genees.
Goeie maats help mekaar om na Jesus te kom.
Moenie moed opgee as dit moeilik is om by Jesus uit te kom nie.
questions: Wat het die maats gedoen toe hulle nie kon inkom nie?
Wie is ’n maat vir wie jy kan bid of na Jesus kan bring?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U my vergewe en genees.
Help asseblief my maat…
en help my om ’n maat te wees wat mense na U bring. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre vir ’n maat wat hulp nodig het, en doen iets gaafs vir hulle.

en.title: A Hole in the Roof
story: Jesus was teaching in a house in Capernaum. So many people came to hear Him that the house was packed. There wasn’t even room at the door!
Four friends arrived, carrying a man on a mat. Their friend couldn’t walk, and they were sure Jesus could help him. But they couldn’t get in. What would you do?

These friends didn’t give up. They climbed up onto the flat roof, dug a big hole in it, and carefully lowered their friend down on his mat, right in front of Jesus! Bits of roof must have been falling on everyone’s heads!

Jesus saw how much faith the friends had. He looked at the man kindly and said, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’ Some teachers grumbled, ‘Only God can forgive sins!’ They were right, and Jesus is God’s Son!

So Jesus said, ‘I want you to know that I have power to forgive sins.’ Then He said to the man, ‘Get up, take your mat and go home.’ And the man jumped up, picked up his mat and walked out in front of everyone!
The people were amazed. ‘We have never seen anything like this!’ they said, and they praised God.
Jesus forgives and heals. And good friends bring each other to Jesus.

verse.text: He forgives all your sins and heals all your sicknesses.

lessons: Jesus forgives and heals.
Good friends help each other come to Jesus.
Don’t give up when it’s hard to get to Jesus.
questions: What did the friends do when they couldn’t get in?
Who is a friend you could pray for or bring to Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that you forgive me and heal me.
Please help my friend…
and help me be a friend who brings people to you. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, pray for a friend who needs help, and do something kind for them.

en.fact: In Bible times, many houses had flat roofs made of wooden beams, branches and dried mud. People used them like an extra room, and you could climb up by an outside staircase.
en.deeper: Why do you think Jesus forgave the man before He healed his legs?
en.journal: Draw a house with a hole in the roof and four friends at the top. Write: ‘Friends bring friends to Jesus.’

af.title: ’n Gat in die Dak
story: Jesus was besig om in ’n huis in Kapernaum te leer. So baie mense het gekom om Hom te hoor dat die huis stampvol was. Daar was nie eers plek by die deur nie!
Vier maats het aangekom en ’n man op ’n matjie gedra. Hulle maat kon nie loop nie, en hulle was seker Jesus kon hom help. Maar hulle kon nie inkom nie. Wat sou jy doen?

Hierdie maats het nie moed opgegee nie. Hulle het op die plat dak geklim, ’n groot gat daarin gegrawe, en hulle maat versigtig op sy matjie laat sak, reg voor Jesus! Stukkies dak het seker op almal se koppe geval!

Jesus het gesien hoeveel geloof die maats gehad het. Hy het die man vriendelik aangekyk en gesê: ‘Seun, jou sondes is vergewe.’ Party leraars het gekla: ‘Net God kan sondes vergewe!’ Hulle was reg, en Jesus is God se Seun!

Toe sê Jesus: ‘Ek wil hê julle moet weet dat Ek mag het om sondes te vergewe.’ Toe sê Hy vir die man: ‘Staan op, vat jou matjie en gaan huis toe.’ En die man het opgespring, sy matjie opgetel en voor almal uitgeloop!
Die mense was verbaas. ‘Ons het nog nooit so iets gesien nie!’ het hulle gesê, en hulle het God geprys.
Jesus vergewe en genees. En goeie maats bring mekaar na Jesus.

verse.text: Hy vergewe al jou sondes en genees al jou siektes.

lessons: Jesus vergewe en genees.
Goeie maats help mekaar om na Jesus te kom.
Moenie moed opgee as dit moeilik is om by Jesus uit te kom nie.
questions: Wat het die maats gedoen toe hulle nie kon inkom nie?
Wie is ’n maat vir wie jy kan bid of na Jesus kan bring?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U my vergewe en genees.
Help asseblief my maat…
en help my om ’n maat te wees wat mense na U bring. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre vir ’n maat wat hulp nodig het, en doen iets gaafs vir hulle.

af.fact: In Bybeltye het baie huise plat dakke gehad wat van houtbalke, takke en gedroogde modder gemaak is. Mense het dit soos ’n ekstra kamer gebruik, en jy kon met ’n buitetrap opklim.
af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy het Jesus die man vergewe voordat Hy sy bene gesond gemaak het?
af.journal: Teken ’n huis met ’n gat in die dak en vier maats bo-op. Skryf: ‘Maats bring maats na Jesus.’

trait.en: Jesus notices me in the crowd
trait.af: Jesus sien my raak in die skare

en.title: Who Touched Me?
story: Jesus was on His way to Jairus’ house to heal his dying daughter, and a large crowd pressed around Him on every side. Hidden in that crowd was a woman with a desperate secret.

For twelve years she had suffered from bleeding that wouldn’t stop. Under the law of Moses, this made her ‘unclean’. She wasn’t allowed to go to the temple, and anyone she touched would become ceremonially unclean too. For twelve years she had been weak, isolated and probably very lonely. She had spent all her money on doctors, but instead of getting better, she grew worse.
She had heard about Jesus. She thought, ‘If I just touch His clothes, I will be healed.’ She didn’t want to be noticed. She just wanted to slip in, touch Him and slip away.
So she pushed through the crowd and touched His cloak. Immediately the bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was free from her suffering.

Jesus stopped. He knew that power had gone out from Him. ‘Who touched my clothes?’ His disciples were puzzled: ‘You see the people crowding against you, and yet you ask who touched you?’ But Jesus kept looking around.

Trembling with fear, the woman came and fell at His feet and told Him the whole truth. Why did Jesus insist on finding her? Because He didn’t just want to heal her body. He wanted to restore her completely. In front of everyone, He said, ‘Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be freed from your suffering.’
With one word, ‘Daughter’, Jesus gave her back her dignity and her place in the community. She was no longer an outcast hiding in a crowd. She was a beloved daughter.
Jesus never sees you as just a face in the crowd. He knows you, and He calls you His own.

verse.text: Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace.

lessons: Jesus notices individuals, even in a crowd.
Jesus heals not only bodies, but restores dignity and belonging.
We can reach out to Jesus in faith, however long we have suffered.
questions: Why did the woman want to stay hidden?
Why do you think Jesus insisted on finding her?
What does the word ‘Daughter’ tell us about how Jesus sees us?
en.listen: Be still and imagine reaching out to touch Jesus’ cloak. What do you need from Him? Ask: ‘Jesus, what do you call me?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you notice me in the crowd.
I reach out to you for…
Thank you that I belong to you.

mission.text: This week, notice someone who is often ignored or left out, and include them.

en.journal: Write about a time when you felt invisible or left out. Then write what Jesus says to you about it.

af.title: Wie Het aan My Geraak?
story: Jesus was op pad na Jaïrus se huis om sy sterwende dogter gesond te maak, en ’n groot skare het van alle kante teen Hom gedruk. Versteek in daardie skare was ’n vrou met ’n desperate geheim.

Twaalf jaar lank het sy gely aan bloeding wat nie wou ophou nie. Volgens die wet van Moses het dit haar ‘onrein’ gemaak. Sy mag nie na die tempel gaan nie, en enigiemand aan wie sy raak, sou ook seremonieel onrein word. Twaalf jaar lank was sy swak, afgesonder en waarskynlik baie eensaam. Sy het al haar geld aan dokters uitgegee, maar in plaas daarvan om beter te word, het sy slegter geword.
Sy het van Jesus gehoor. Sy het gedink: ‘As ek net aan sy klere raak, sal ek genees word.’ Sy wou nie opgemerk word nie. Sy wou net insluip, aan Hom raak en wegglip.
Toe het sy deur die skare gedruk en aan sy mantel geraak. Dadelik het die bloeding opgehou, en sy het in haar liggaam gevoel dat sy vry was van haar lyding.

Jesus het gaan staan. Hy het geweet dat krag van Hom uitgegaan het. ‘Wie het aan my klere geraak?’ Sy dissipels was verbaas: ‘U sien hoe die mense teen U druk, en tog vra U wie aan U geraak het?’ Maar Jesus het aangehou rondkyk.

Bewend van vrees het die vrou gekom, voor sy voete neergeval en Hom die hele waarheid vertel. Hoekom het Jesus daarop aangedring om haar te kry? Omdat Hy nie net haar liggaam wou genees nie. Hy wou haar heeltemal herstel. Voor almal het Hy gesê: ‘Dogter, jou geloof het jou gesond gemaak. Gaan in vrede en wees vry van jou lyding.’
Met een woord, ‘Dogter’, het Jesus haar haar waardigheid en haar plek in die gemeenskap teruggegee. Sy was nie meer ’n uitgeworpene wat in ’n skare wegkruip nie. Sy was ’n geliefde dogter.
Jesus sien jou nooit net as ’n gesig in die skare nie. Hy ken jou, en Hy noem jou syne.

verse.text: Dogter, jou geloof het jou gesond gemaak. Gaan in vrede.

lessons: Jesus sien individue raak, selfs in ’n skare.
Jesus genees nie net liggame nie, maar herstel waardigheid en die gevoel om te behoort.
Ons kan met geloof na Jesus uitreik, hoe lank ons ook al gely het.
questions: Hoekom wou die vrou versteek bly?
Hoekom dink jy het Jesus daarop aangedring om haar te kry?
Wat sê die woord ‘Dogter’ vir ons oor hoe Jesus ons sien?
af.listen: Wees stil en stel jou voor jy reik uit om aan Jesus se mantel te raak. Wat het jy van Hom nodig? Vra: ‘Jesus, wat noem U my?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U my in die skare raaksien.
Ek reik na U uit vir…
Dankie dat ek aan U behoort.

mission.text: Sien hierdie week iemand raak wat dikwels geïgnoreer of uitgelos word, en sluit hulle in.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n keer toe jy onsigbaar of uitgelos gevoel het. Skryf dan wat Jesus vir jou daaroor sê.

en.title: Clean, Whole and Called ‘Daughter’
story: Mark 5 weaves two stories together, a technique scholars call a ‘sandwich’. Jesus sets out to heal Jairus’ daughter, is interrupted by a woman in the crowd, then continues to Jairus’ house. The two stories interpret each other: both involve a ‘daughter’, both involve the number twelve, and both involve someone ‘unclean’ being touched and restored.

Consider the woman’s situation in light of Leviticus 15. A woman with ongoing bleeding was ceremonially unclean for as long as it lasted, and anything or anyone she touched became unclean too. For twelve years she had been excluded from worship at the temple and probably from much of normal social life. Mark adds a painful detail: she had ‘suffered a great deal under the care of many doctors and had spent all she had, yet instead of getting better she grew worse’. She was physically weak, socially isolated, financially ruined and religiously excluded.

So when she touches Jesus, she is breaking a rule. By the law, her touch should make Him unclean. Instead, the opposite happens: His holiness flows into her and makes her clean. This is the pattern of Jesus’ whole ministry. Uncleanness doesn’t contaminate Jesus; His purity and life overcome it.

Jesus’ question, ‘Who touched my clothes?’, isn’t because He doesn’t know. He wants a public encounter. A secret healing would have fixed her body but left her shame and exclusion in place. By calling her forward and declaring her healed in front of everyone, Jesus restores her publicly. And He gives her a title: ‘Daughter.’ It is the only time in the Gospels that Jesus addresses someone this way.

He also says, ‘Your faith has healed you.’ Her faith wasn’t perfect. It may even have been a little superstitious. But it reached out to the right Person. Faith is not about the strength of the one believing, but about the One in whom we believe.
Meanwhile, Jairus is waiting, watching precious minutes slip away. The interruption that seemed a disaster was about to become the setting for an even greater miracle.

verse.text: Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be freed from your suffering.

lessons: Jesus’ holiness overcomes uncleanness; it isn’t contaminated by it.
Jesus heals the whole person, including shame and exclusion.
Faith is about the One we trust, not about how strong our faith feels.
questions: Why was it so significant that the woman touched Jesus, according to the law?
Why did Jesus make the healing public instead of letting her slip away?
What does it mean that faith depends on the One we believe in, not on the strength of our belief?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Is there anything that makes you feel ‘unclean’, ashamed or on the outside? Bring it to Jesus. Ask Him what He calls you. Write it down.
prayer: Jesus, your holiness makes me clean.
I bring you the shame I feel about…
Thank you that you call me your own, and that I belong in your family.

mission.text: This week, reach out to someone who might feel excluded (at school, online, or in your community), and treat them with dignity.

en.journal: Compare the woman before and after meeting Jesus: physically, socially and spiritually. What does that show about how Jesus heals?

af.title: Rein, Heel en ‘Dogter’ Genoem
story: Markus 5 vleg twee stories inmekaar, ’n tegniek wat geleerdes ’n ‘toebroodjie’ noem. Jesus vertrek om Jaïrus se dogter te genees, word onderbreek deur ’n vrou in die skare, en gaan dan verder na Jaïrus se huis. Die twee stories verklaar mekaar: albei gaan oor ’n ‘dogter’, albei het die getal twaalf, en albei gaan oor iemand ‘onreins’ wat aangeraak en herstel word.

Dink aan die vrou se situasie in die lig van Levitikus 15. ’n Vrou met aanhoudende bloeding was seremonieel onrein solank dit geduur het, en enigiets of enigiemand aan wie sy raak, het ook onrein geword. Twaalf jaar lank was sy uitgesluit van aanbidding by die tempel en waarskynlik van baie van die normale sosiale lewe. Markus voeg ’n pynlike besonderheid by: sy het ‘baie gely onder die sorg van baie dokters en alles uitgegee wat sy gehad het, maar in plaas daarvan om beter te word, het sy slegter geword’. Sy was liggaamlik swak, sosiaal afgesonder, finansieel geruïneer en godsdienstig uitgesluit.

So wanneer sy aan Jesus raak, oortree sy ’n reël. Volgens die wet moet haar aanraking Hom onrein maak. In plaas daarvan gebeur die teenoorgestelde: sy heiligheid vloei na haar toe en maak haar rein. Dit is die patroon van Jesus se hele bediening. Onreinheid besoedel nie Jesus nie; sy reinheid en lewe oorwin dit.

Jesus se vraag, ‘Wie het aan my klere geraak?’, is nie omdat Hy nie weet nie. Hy wil ’n openbare ontmoeting hê. ’n Geheime genesing sou haar liggaam reggemaak het, maar haar skaamte en uitsluiting laat bly het. Deur haar vorentoe te roep en voor almal te verklaar dat sy genees is, herstel Jesus haar in die openbaar. En Hy gee haar ’n titel: ‘Dogter.’ Dit is die enigste keer in die Evangelies dat Jesus iemand so aanspreek.

Hy sê ook: ‘Jou geloof het jou gesond gemaak.’ Haar geloof was nie volmaak nie. Dit was dalk selfs ’n bietjie bygelowig. Maar dit het na die regte Persoon uitgereik. Geloof gaan nie oor die krag van die een wat glo nie, maar oor die Een in wie ons glo.
Intussen wag Jaïrus, en kyk hoe kosbare minute verbygaan. Die onderbreking wat soos ’n ramp gelyk het, was op die punt om die toneel te word vir ’n nog groter wonderwerk.

verse.text: Dogter, jou geloof het jou gesond gemaak. Gaan in vrede en wees vry van jou lyding.

lessons: Jesus se heiligheid oorwin onreinheid; dit word nie daardeur besoedel nie.
Jesus genees die hele mens, ook skaamte en uitsluiting.
Geloof gaan oor die Een wat ons vertrou, nie oor hoe sterk ons geloof voel nie.
questions: Hoekom was dit volgens die wet so betekenisvol dat die vrou aan Jesus geraak het?
Hoekom het Jesus die genesing openbaar gemaak in plaas daarvan om haar te laat wegglip?
Wat beteken dit dat geloof afhang van die Een in wie ons glo, en nie van die krag van ons geloof nie?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Is daar iets wat jou ‘onrein’, skaam of buite laat voel? Bring dit na Jesus. Vra Hom wat Hy jou noem. Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Jesus, u heiligheid maak my rein.
Ek bring vir U die skaamte wat ek voel oor…
Dankie dat U my u eie noem, en dat ek in u familie behoort.

mission.text: Reik hierdie week uit na iemand wat dalk uitgesluit voel (by die skool, aanlyn of in jou gemeenskap), en behandel hulle met waardigheid.

af.journal: Vergelyk die vrou voor en nadat sy Jesus ontmoet het: liggaamlik, sosiaal en geestelik. Wat wys dit oor hoe Jesus genees?

en.title: Jesus Notices Me
story: Lots and lots of people were pushing around Jesus.
A sick lady thought, ‘If I just touch His clothes, I will be well.’
She reached out and touched His cloak. She was healed!
Jesus stopped. ‘Who touched me?’ He asked.
Jesus saw her and was kind to her. Jesus notices me too!

verse.text: Jesus is the same yesterday, today and forever.

en.action: Reach out your hand gently, like the lady touching Jesus’ cloak.
lessons: Jesus notices me, even in a crowd.
questions: Can you reach out your hand like the lady?
prayer: Thank you, Jesus,
that you notice me. Amen.

af.title: Jesus Sien My Raak
story: Baie, baie mense het om Jesus gedruk.
’n Siek vrou het gedink: ‘As ek net aan sy klere raak, sal ek gesond word.’
Sy het haar hand uitgesteek en aan sy mantel geraak. Sy is genees!
Jesus het gaan staan. ‘Wie het aan My geraak?’ het Hy gevra.
Jesus het haar gesien en was goed vir haar. Jesus sien my ook raak!

verse.text: Jesus is gister, vandag en vir altyd dieselfde.

af.action: Steek jou hand saggies uit, soos die vrou wat aan Jesus se mantel raak.
lessons: Jesus sien my raak, selfs in ’n skare.
questions: Kan jy jou hand uitsteek soos die vrou?
prayer: Dankie, Jesus,
dat U my raaksien. Amen.

en.title: A Touch in the Crowd
story: Jesus was walking through a town, and a huge crowd was squashing all around Him. Everyone wanted to be close to Him.

In the crowd was a woman who had been sick for twelve long years. She had gone to many doctors and spent all her money, but instead of getting better, she got worse. Because of her sickness, people kept away from her. She felt very alone.
She had heard about Jesus. She thought, ‘If I just touch His clothes, I will be healed.’ So she pushed her way through the crowd, reached out a trembling hand and touched the edge of His cloak.
Straight away, she felt in her body that she was healed!
Jesus stopped. ‘Who touched my clothes?’ He asked. His disciples laughed. ‘Everyone is pushing against you!’ But Jesus knew that healing power had gone out from Him. He kept looking around.

The woman came forward, shaking, and fell at His feet. She told Him the whole story. Jesus didn’t scold her. He said gently, ‘Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace.’ He called her ‘Daughter’! She wasn’t alone any more. She was part of God’s family.
Jesus notices you too, even in a big crowd. You are never just one of many to Him.

verse.text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

lessons: Jesus notices me, even in a crowd.
I can reach out to Jesus with faith.
Jesus welcomes me into God’s family.
questions: Why do you think Jesus stopped to find the woman, instead of just walking on?
How does it feel to know Jesus notices you?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that you notice me.
I reach out to you tonight with…
Thank you that I am part of God’s family. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, notice someone who might feel alone in a crowd, and say something kind to them.

af.title: ’n Aanraking in die Skare
story: Jesus het deur ’n dorp geloop, en ’n groot skare het rondom Hom gedruk. Almal wou naby Hom wees.

In die skare was ’n vrou wat twaalf lang jare siek was. Sy het na baie dokters gegaan en al haar geld uitgegee, maar in plaas daarvan om beter te word, het sy slegter geword. Weens haar siekte het mense van haar af weggebly. Sy het baie alleen gevoel.
Sy het van Jesus gehoor. Sy het gedink: ‘As ek net aan sy klere raak, sal ek genees word.’ Toe het sy deur die skare gedruk, ’n bewende hand uitgesteek en aan die soom van sy mantel geraak.
Dadelik het sy in haar liggaam gevoel dat sy genees is!

Jesus het gaan staan. ‘Wie het aan my klere geraak?’ het Hy gevra. Sy dissipels het gelag. ‘Almal druk teen U!’ Maar Jesus het geweet dat genesende krag van Hom uitgegaan het. Hy het aangehou rondkyk.

Die vrou het bewend vorentoe gekom en voor sy voete neergeval. Sy het Hom die hele storie vertel. Jesus het haar nie uitgetrap nie. Hy het sag gesê: ‘Dogter, jou geloof het jou gesond gemaak. Gaan in vrede.’ Hy het haar ‘Dogter’ genoem! Sy was nie meer alleen nie. Sy was deel van God se familie.
Jesus sien jou ook raak, selfs in ’n groot skare. Vir Hom is jy nooit net een van baie nie.

verse.text: Jesus Christus is gister en vandag dieselfde, en tot in ewigheid.

lessons: Jesus sien my raak, selfs in ’n skare.
Ek kan met geloof na Jesus uitreik.
Jesus verwelkom my in God se familie.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Jesus gaan staan om die vrou te soek, in plaas daarvan om net aan te loop?
Hoe voel dit om te weet Jesus sien jou raak?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U my raaksien.
Ek reik vanaand na U uit met…
Dankie dat ek deel van God se familie is. Amen.

mission.text: Sien môre iemand raak wat dalk alleen in ’n skare voel, en sê iets gaafs vir hulle.

af.fact: In Bybeltye het Joodse mans dikwels ’n mantel met tossels aan die hoeke gedra, om hulle aan God se gebooie te herinner. Die vrou het dalk aan een van hierdie tossels geraak.
af.deeper: Jesus het die vrou ‘Dogter’ genoem. Hoekom dink jy het daardie woord so baie vir haar beteken?
af.journal: Trek jou hand af en skryf daarin: ‘Jesus sien my raak.’

trait.en: Jesus says: don’t be afraid, just believe
trait.af: Jesus sê: moenie bang wees nie, glo net

en.title: Don’t Be Afraid; Just Believe
story: Jairus was a leader of the local synagogue, a respected man in Capernaum. Many religious leaders were suspicious of Jesus, but when your child is dying, pride doesn’t matter any more. Jairus pushed through the crowd and fell at Jesus’ feet. ‘My little daughter is dying. Please come and put your hands on her so that she will be healed and live.’
Jesus went with him immediately. But the crowd slowed them down, and then Jesus stopped completely to talk to the woman who had touched His cloak. Imagine how Jairus felt as the minutes ticked by.
While Jesus was still speaking, messengers arrived from Jairus’ house. ‘Your daughter is dead. Why bother the teacher anymore?’
Overhearing it, Jesus turned to Jairus and said seven words that have comforted millions since: ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’

At the house, there was a commotion of people crying and wailing loudly. Jesus said, ‘Why all this commotion and wailing? The child is not dead but asleep.’ They laughed at Him. They knew she was dead. But for Jesus, death was no more permanent than sleep.

Jesus put everyone out except the girl’s parents and three disciples: Peter, James and John. He took her by the hand and said, ‘Talitha koum!’ (‘Little girl, I say to you, get up!’). Immediately she stood up and began to walk around. Everyone was completely astonished.
Then Jesus did something tender and practical: He told them to give her something to eat.
Sometimes, like Jairus, we hear news that makes us afraid. Things seem too late or too hopeless. In those moments, Jesus says the same words to us: ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’

verse.text: Don’t be afraid; just believe.

lessons: Jesus says to us in frightening moments: ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’
Nothing is too late for Jesus, not even death.
Jesus is both powerful and tender.
questions: How do you think Jairus felt when Jesus stopped for the woman?
Why did Jesus say the girl was ‘asleep’?
What news or situation makes you afraid? How can Jesus’ words help?
en.listen: Be still and bring Jesus something that makes you afraid. Imagine Him saying to you, ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’ Ask what He wants you to believe about Him. Write it down.
prayer: Jesus, nothing is too late for you.
I feel afraid about…
Help me not to be afraid, but to believe.

mission.text: Write ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe’ on a card and keep it with you this week. Read it whenever you feel anxious.

en.journal: Write about a situation that feels too late or hopeless. Then write a prayer of faith, using Jesus’ words.

af.title: Moenie Bang Wees Nie; Glo Net
story: Jaïrus was ’n leier van die plaaslike sinagoge, ’n gerespekteerde man in Kapernaum. Baie godsdienstige leiers was agterdogtig oor Jesus, maar as jou kind besig is om te sterf, maak trots nie meer saak nie. Jaïrus het deur die skare gedruk en voor Jesus se voete neergeval. ‘My dogtertjie is besig om te sterf. Kom sit asseblief u hande op haar sodat sy genees word en lewe.’

Jesus het dadelik saam met hom gegaan. Maar die skare het hulle vertraag, en toe het Jesus heeltemal gaan staan om met die vrou te praat wat aan sy mantel geraak het. Stel jou voor hoe Jaïrus gevoel het terwyl die minute verbytik.
Terwyl Jesus nog praat, het boodskappers van Jaïrus se huis aangekom. ‘Jou dogter is dood. Hoekom pla jy die leermeester nog?’
Jesus het dit gehoor, na Jaïrus gedraai en ’n paar woorde gesê wat sedertdien miljoene mense getroos het: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’

By die huis was daar ’n lawaai van mense wat hard huil en weeklaag. Jesus het gesê: ‘Hoekom al hierdie lawaai en geween? Die kind is nie dood nie, sy slaap.’ Hulle het vir Hom gelag. Hulle het geweet sy is dood. Maar vir Jesus was die dood nie meer permanent as slaap nie.

Jesus het almal uitgestuur behalwe die meisie se ouers en drie dissipels: Petrus, Jakobus en Johannes. Hy het haar hand gevat en gesê: ‘Talita koemi!’ (‘Dogtertjie, Ek sê vir jou, staan op!’). Dadelik het sy opgestaan en begin rondloop. Almal was heeltemal verstom.
Toe het Jesus iets teers en prakties gedoen: Hy het hulle gesê om vir haar iets te ete te gee.
Soms hoor ons, soos Jaïrus, nuus wat ons bang maak. Dinge lyk te laat of te hopeloos. Op daardie oomblikke sê Jesus dieselfde woorde vir ons: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’

verse.text: Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.

lessons: Jesus sê vir ons op skrikwekkende oomblikke: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’
Niks is te laat vir Jesus nie, nie eers die dood nie.
Jesus is magtig sowel as teer.
questions: Hoe dink jy het Jaïrus gevoel toe Jesus vir die vrou gaan staan het?
Hoekom het Jesus gesê die meisie ‘slaap’?
Watter nuus of situasie maak jou bang? Hoe kan Jesus se woorde help?
af.listen: Wees stil en bring vir Jesus iets wat jou bang maak. Stel jou voor Hy sê vir jou: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’ Vra wat Hy wil hê jy oor Hom moet glo. Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Jesus, niks is vir U te laat nie.
Ek voel bang oor…
Help my om nie bang te wees nie, maar te glo.

mission.text: Skryf ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net’ op ’n kaartjie en hou dit hierdie week by jou. Lees dit elke keer as jy angstig voel.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n situasie wat te laat of hopeloos voel. Skryf dan ’n gebed van geloof, met Jesus se woorde.

en.title: When Jesus Is Late
story: Jairus’ story raises a question every believer faces at some point: what do you do when Jesus seems to be late?

Jairus did everything right. He humbled himself, a synagogue leader falling at the feet of a controversial rabbi. He asked in faith: ‘Put your hands on her so that she will be healed and live.’ Jesus agreed and set out with him. Then came the delay: the crowd, the woman, the conversation. And then the worst possible news: ‘Your daughter is dead. Why bother the teacher anymore?’
Notice the message’s logic: if she is dead, Jesus is no longer relevant. The messengers believed Jesus could help the sick, but not the dead. Their faith had a ceiling.

Jesus ‘ignored’ (or ‘overheard’) what they said. The word can mean both. He refused to let their limited view define the situation. To Jairus He said, ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’ The tense in Greek suggests ‘keep on believing’. Jairus’ faith had brought him to Jesus. Now he needed to keep holding on when everything looked lost.

At the house, the mourners laughed when Jesus said the child was only asleep. Jesus wasn’t denying her death; He was redefining it. For the Lord of life, death is like sleep, something from which He can wake us. Paul later describes believers who have died as having ‘fallen asleep’, waiting for the resurrection.

Jesus took only five witnesses into the room, perhaps to protect the family’s privacy and the girl’s dignity. He took her hand, spoke Aramaic words a mother might use to wake her child in the morning, and she rose. Then, wonderfully ordinary: ‘Give her something to eat.’

John 11 tells a similar story. Jesus deliberately waited two days before going to Lazarus, ‘so that God’s Son may be glorified’. Jesus’ delays are not denials. Sometimes He waits because He intends to do something greater than we asked.
Not every prayer is answered the way Jairus’ was. But Jesus’ words remain the same: ‘Don’t be afraid; keep on believing.’ He is never late for His purposes.

verse.text: Don’t be afraid; just believe.

lessons: Jesus’ delays are not denials; He is never late for His purposes.
We must not let others’ limited faith define what Jesus can do.
Faith that brings us to Jesus must keep holding on when things look lost.
questions: What did the messengers believe about Jesus? Where was the ‘ceiling’ in their faith?
What does it mean that Jesus redefined death as sleep?
How do you respond when God seems to be late in answering your prayers?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Bring Jesus a prayer that seems to be taking a long time to be answered. Ask: ‘What do you want me to keep believing?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, you are never late for your purposes.
I have been waiting for… and sometimes I feel like giving up.
Help me not to be afraid, but to keep on believing.

mission.text: This week, keep praying for one long-standing request, and each time add: ‘I will keep on believing.’

en.journal: Write a list of ‘ceilings’ people sometimes put on what Jesus can do. Next to each one, write a Bible truth that breaks through it.

af.title: As Jesus Laat Is
story: Jaïrus se storie bring ’n vraag na vore wat elke gelowige op ’n stadium het: wat doen jy as dit lyk of Jesus laat is?

Jaïrus het alles reg gedoen. Hy het homself verneder, ’n sinagogeleier wat voor die voete van ’n omstrede rabbi neerval. Hy het in geloof gevra: ‘Sit u hande op haar sodat sy genees word en lewe.’ Jesus het ingestem en saam met hom vertrek. Toe kom die vertraging: die skare, die vrou, die gesprek. En toe die ergste moontlike nuus: ‘Jou dogter is dood. Hoekom pla jy die leermeester nog?’
Let op die boodskap se logika: as sy dood is, is Jesus nie meer relevant nie. Die boodskappers het geglo Jesus kan die siekes help, maar nie die dooies nie. Hulle geloof het ’n plafon gehad.

Jesus het ‘nie gesteur nie aan’ (of ‘afgeluister’) wat hulle gesê het. Die woord kan albei beteken. Hy het geweier om hulle beperkte siening die situasie te laat bepaal. Vir Jaïrus het Hy gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’ Die tyd in Grieks dui aan ‘hou aan glo’. Jaïrus se geloof het hom na Jesus gebring. Nou moes hy aanhou vasklou toe alles verlore gelyk het.

By die huis het die treurders gelag toe Jesus sê die kind slaap net. Jesus het nie haar dood ontken nie; Hy het dit herdefinieer. Vir die Here van die lewe is die dood soos slaap, iets waaruit Hy ons kan wakker maak. Paulus beskryf later gelowiges wat gesterf het as die wat ‘ontslaap’ het, en wag vir die opstanding.

Jesus het net vyf getuies in die kamer ingeneem, dalk om die familie se privaatheid en die meisie se waardigheid te beskerm. Hy het haar hand gevat, Aramese woorde gesê wat ’n ma sou gebruik om haar kind soggens wakker te maak, en sy het opgestaan. Toe, wonderlik gewoon: ‘Gee haar iets om te eet.’

Johannes 11 vertel ’n soortgelyke storie. Jesus het doelbewus twee dae gewag voordat Hy na Lasarus gegaan het, ‘sodat die Seun van God verheerlik kan word’. Jesus se vertragings is nie weierings nie. Soms wag Hy omdat Hy van plan is om iets groters te doen as waarvoor ons gevra het.
Nie elke gebed word beantwoord soos Jaïrus s’n nie. Maar Jesus se woorde bly dieselfde: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; hou aan glo.’ Hy is nooit laat vir sy doel nie.

verse.text: Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.

lessons: Jesus se vertragings is nie weierings nie; Hy is nooit laat vir sy doel nie.
Ons moenie ander se beperkte geloof laat bepaal wat Jesus kan doen nie.
Geloof wat ons na Jesus bring, moet aanhou vasklou as dinge verlore lyk.
questions: Wat het die boodskappers oor Jesus geglo? Waar was die ‘plafon’ in hulle geloof?
Wat beteken dit dat Jesus die dood as slaap herdefinieer het?
Hoe reageer jy as dit lyk of God laat is om jou gebede te beantwoord?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Bring vir Jesus ’n gebed wat lank neem om beantwoord te word. Vra: ‘Wat wil U hê moet ek aanhou glo?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, U is nooit laat vir u doel nie.
Ek wag al vir… en soms voel ek lus om op te gee.
Help my om nie bang te wees nie, maar aan te hou glo.

mission.text: Hou hierdie week aan bid vir een versoek wat al lank uitstaan, en voeg elke keer by: ‘Ek sal aanhou glo.’

af.journal: Skryf ’n lys van ‘plafonne’ wat mense soms plaas op wat Jesus kan doen. Skryf langs elkeen ’n Bybelwaarheid wat daardeur breek.

en.title: Just Believe
story: Jairus had a little girl who was very sick.
He ran to Jesus. ‘Please come and help her!’
Then someone said, ‘It’s too late.’
But Jesus said, ‘Don’t be afraid. Just believe.’
Jesus held her hand and said, ‘Little girl, get up!’ And she did!

verse.text: Don’t be afraid. Just believe.

en.action: Lie down and pretend to sleep. When someone says, ‘Little girl (or boy), get up!’, jump up!
lessons: Jesus says: don’t be afraid, just believe.
questions: Can you jump up when Jesus calls?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
help me not to be afraid. I believe you! Amen.

af.title: Glo Net
story: Jaïrus het ’n dogtertjie gehad wat baie siek was.
Hy het na Jesus gehardloop. ‘Kom help haar asseblief!’
Toe het iemand gesê: ‘Dis te laat.’
Maar Jesus het gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie. Glo net.’
Jesus het haar hand vasgehou en gesê: ‘Dogtertjie, staan op!’ En sy het!

verse.text: Moenie bang wees nie. Glo net.

af.action: Lê en maak of jy slaap. As iemand sê: ‘Dogtertjie (of seuntjie), staan op!’, spring op!
lessons: Jesus sê: moenie bang wees nie, glo net.
questions: Kan jy opspring as Jesus roep?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
help my om nie bang te wees nie. Ek glo U! Amen.

en.title: Little Girl, Get Up!
story: Jairus was an important man who looked after the synagogue, the meeting place where people learned about God. But today he didn’t feel important. His twelve-year-old daughter was very sick, and she was dying.
Jairus ran to Jesus and fell at His feet. ‘Please come and put your hands on her so that she will be healed and live!’ he begged. Jesus went with him straight away.
But on the way, Jesus stopped to help the woman who had touched His cloak. Jairus must have been so worried. Hurry, Jesus!
Then some men came from Jairus’ house with terrible news: ‘Your daughter is dead. Why bother the teacher any more?’
Jesus heard them. He turned to Jairus and said, ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’

At the house, people were crying loudly. Jesus said, ‘Why are you crying? The child is not dead but asleep.’ They laughed at Him. But Jesus sent them outside and went in with the girl’s mother and father and three disciples.

Jesus took the girl by the hand and said, ‘Talitha koum!’ which means, ‘Little girl, get up!’ Immediately she stood up and walked around! Her parents were completely amazed. Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
When everything seems hopeless, Jesus says to you too: ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’

verse.text: Don’t be afraid; just believe.

lessons: Jesus says: don’t be afraid, just believe.
Nothing is too late for Jesus.
Jesus is kind and gentle with children.
questions: How do you think Jairus felt when the men said it was too late?
When do you need to remember: ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe’?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
when I feel afraid,
help me to remember your words:
‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’ Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you feel worried, say Jesus’ words out loud: ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’

af.title: Dogtertjie, Staan Op!
story: Jaïrus was ’n belangrike man wat na die sinagoge gekyk het, die vergaderplek waar mense van God geleer het. Maar vandag het hy nie belangrik gevoel nie. Sy twaalfjarige dogter was baie siek, en sy was besig om te sterf.
Jaïrus het na Jesus gehardloop en voor sy voete neergeval. ‘Kom sit asseblief u hande op haar sodat sy gesond word en lewe!’ het hy gesmeek. Jesus het dadelik saam met hom gegaan.
Maar op pad het Jesus gaan staan om die vrou te help wat aan sy mantel geraak het. Jaïrus was seker so bekommerd. Maak gou, Jesus!
Toe kom party mans van Jaïrus se huis met verskriklike nuus: ‘Jou dogter is dood. Hoekom pla jy die leermeester nog?’
Jesus het hulle gehoor. Hy het na Jaïrus gedraai en gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’

By die huis het mense hard gehuil. Jesus het gesê: ‘Hoekom huil julle? Die kind is nie dood nie, sy slaap.’ Hulle het vir Hom gelag. Maar Jesus het hulle uitgestuur en saam met die meisie se ma en pa en drie dissipels ingegaan.

Jesus het die meisie se hand gevat en gesê: ‘Talita koemi!’ wat beteken: ‘Dogtertjie, staan op!’ Dadelik het sy opgestaan en rondgeloop! Haar ouers was heeltemal verstom. Jesus het hulle gesê om vir haar iets te ete te gee.
As alles hopeloos lyk, sê Jesus ook vir jou: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’

verse.text: Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.

lessons: Jesus sê: moenie bang wees nie, glo net.
Niks is te laat vir Jesus nie.
Jesus is goed en sag met kinders.
questions: Hoe dink jy het Jaïrus gevoel toe die mans sê dit is te laat?
Wanneer moet jy onthou: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net’?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
as ek bang voel,
help my om u woorde te onthou:
‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’ Amen.

mission.text: As jy môre bekommerd voel, sê Jesus se woorde hardop: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’

en.deeper: Why do you think Jesus took the girl by the hand?
en.journal: Draw Jesus holding the girl’s hand. Write: ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe.’

af.fact: ‘Talita koemi’ is Aramees, die alledaagse taal wat Jesus gepraat het. Markus het Jesus se presiese woorde bewaar, dalk omdat Petrus, wat daar was, dit nooit vergeet het nie.
af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy het Jesus die meisie se hand gevat?
af.journal: Teken Jesus wat die meisie se hand vashou. Skryf: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net.’

trait.en: Jesus teaches me to love everyone
trait.af: Jesus leer my om almal lief te hê

en.title: Who Is My Neighbour?
story: An expert in the law of Moses stood up to test Jesus. ‘Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?’ Jesus asked him what the law said. The man answered well: ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart… and love your neighbour as yourself.’ ‘Correct,’ said Jesus. ‘Do this and you will live.’
But the man wanted to justify himself, so he asked, ‘And who is my neighbour?’ He was really asking: who can I leave out?
Jesus answered with a story. A man travelling the dangerous road from Jerusalem down to Jericho was attacked by robbers. They stripped him, beat him and left him half dead.

A priest happened to come down the same road. When he saw the man, he passed by on the other side. A Levite, a temple worker, did the same. Maybe they were in a hurry. Maybe they were afraid the robbers were still nearby, or worried about becoming ceremonially unclean if the man had died. Whatever their reasons, they walked away.

Then a Samaritan came along. Jews and Samaritans had hated each other for centuries. Jesus’ listeners would have expected the Samaritan to be the villain. Instead, ‘when he saw him, he took pity on him’. He bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine, put him on his own donkey, took him to an inn and cared for him. The next day he gave the innkeeper two silver coins, about two days’ wages, and promised to pay any extra.

Then Jesus turned the question around: ‘Which of these three do you think was a neighbour to the man?’ The expert couldn’t even bring himself to say ‘the Samaritan’. He said, ‘The one who had mercy on him.’ Jesus told him, ‘Go and do likewise.’
The question isn’t ‘Who is my neighbour?’ but ‘Am I being a neighbour?’ Love doesn’t look for limits. It looks for people in need.

verse.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart… and love your neighbour as yourself.

lessons: Love doesn’t look for limits; it looks for people in need.
Being religious isn’t the same as being loving.
God calls us to show mercy, even to people who are different from us.
questions: What was the expert in the law really asking?
Why was it so surprising that the hero was a Samaritan?
Who might be the ‘hurt person on the road’ in your life?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Who do you want me to be a neighbour to this week?’ Write down the name or picture that comes to mind.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for showing mercy to me.
Help me not to walk past… on the other side.
Make me a good neighbour to everyone.

mission.text: This week, do one ‘Good Samaritan’ act: help someone in need, especially someone outside your usual group.

en.journal: Rewrite Jesus’ story set in your own school or neighbourhood today. Who walks past? Who stops to help?

af.title: Wie Is My Naaste?
story: ’n Kenner van die wet van Moses het opgestaan om Jesus te toets. ‘Leermeester, wat moet ek doen om die ewige lewe te beërf?’ Jesus het hom gevra wat die wet sê. Die man het goed geantwoord: ‘Jy moet die Here jou God liefhê met jou hele hart… en jou naaste soos jouself.’ ‘Reg,’ het Jesus gesê. ‘Doen dit en jy sal lewe.’
Maar die man wou homself regverdig, toe vra hy: ‘En wie is my naaste?’ Hy het eintlik gevra: wie kan ek uitlos?
Jesus het met ’n storie geantwoord. ’n Man wat die gevaarlike pad van Jerusalem af na Jerigo gereis het, is deur rowers aangeval. Hulle het hom uitgetrek, geslaan en halfdood gelos.

’n Priester het toevallig met dieselfde pad af gekom. Toe hy die man sien, het hy aan die ander kant verbygegaan. ’n Leviet, ’n tempelwerker, het dieselfde gedoen. Dalk was hulle haastig. Dalk was hulle bang die rowers was nog naby, of bekommerd dat hulle seremonieel onrein sou word as die man dood is. Wat hulle redes ook al was, hulle het weggestap.

Toe het ’n Samaritaan daar aangekom. Jode en Samaritane het mekaar eeue lank gehaat. Jesus se luisteraars sou verwag het die Samaritaan is die skurk. In plaas daarvan, ‘toe hy hom sien, het hy hom jammer gekry’. Hy het sy wonde verbind, met olie en wyn daarop, hom op sy eie donkie gesit, na ’n herberg geneem en vir hom gesorg. Die volgende dag het hy die herbergier twee silwermuntstukke gegee, omtrent twee dae se loon, en belowe om enige ekstra te betaal.

Toe het Jesus die vraag omgedraai: ‘Watter een van hierdie drie dink jy was ’n naaste vir die man?’ Die kenner kon homself nie eers kry om ‘die Samaritaan’ te sê nie. Hy het gesê: ‘Die een wat hom barmhartigheid bewys het.’ Jesus het vir hom gesê: ‘Gaan en doen dieselfde.’
Die vraag is nie ‘Wie is my naaste?’ nie, maar ‘Is ek ’n naaste?’ Liefde soek nie grense nie. Dit soek mense in nood.

verse.text: Jy moet die Here jou God liefhê met jou hele hart… en jou naaste soos jouself.

lessons: Liefde soek nie grense nie; dit soek mense in nood.
Om godsdienstig te wees, is nie dieselfde as om liefdevol te wees nie.
God roep ons om barmhartigheid te bewys, selfs aan mense wat anders is as ons.
questions: Wat het die kenner van die wet eintlik gevra?
Hoekom was dit so verrassend dat die held ’n Samaritaan was?
Wie is dalk die ‘persoon wat langs die pad seergekry het’ in jou lewe?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Vir wie wil U hê moet ek hierdie week ’n naaste wees?’ Skryf die naam of prentjie neer wat in jou gedagtes opkom.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U barmhartigheid aan my bewys het.
Help my om nie aan die ander kant by… verby te loop nie.
Maak my ’n goeie naaste vir almal.

mission.text: Doen hierdie week een ‘Barmhartige Samaritaan’-daad: help iemand in nood, veral iemand buite jou gewone groep.

af.journal: Skryf Jesus se storie oor, afspeel in jou eie skool of buurt vandag. Wie loop verby? Wie gaan staan om te help?

en.title: Go and Do Likewise
story: The parable of the Good Samaritan is so familiar that it is easy to miss how shocking it was. To feel its force, we need to see the conversation that prompted it.

A lawyer, an expert in the law of Moses, asks Jesus how to inherit eternal life. Jesus turns the question back, and the lawyer summarises the law beautifully: love God completely and love your neighbour as yourself. Jesus agrees: ‘Do this and you will live.’

Then comes the revealing follow-up: ‘wanting to justify himself, he asked, “And who is my neighbour?”’ The lawyer wants a definition with boundaries. If ‘neighbour’ means fellow Jews, or good people, then he can love them and feel righteous, while ignoring everyone else.

Jesus answers with a story that destroys the boundaries. The two religious professionals, a priest and a Levite, see the wounded man and deliberately cross to the other side. They may even have had religious reasons: touching a dead body would make a priest unclean. Their religion had become a reason not to love.

Then Jesus introduces a Samaritan. To Jesus’ Jewish audience this was outrageous. Samaritans were regarded as heretics and enemies, a mixed people with a corrupted temple and false worship. Just a chapter earlier, a Samaritan village had refused to welcome Jesus, and James and John wanted to call down fire on it! Yet the Samaritan is the one moved with compassion. He gives his time, his oil and wine, his donkey, his money and his promise.

Finally Jesus flips the lawyer’s question. He asked, ‘Who is my neighbour?’ (whom must I love?). Jesus asks, ‘Who was a neighbour?’ (who showed love?). The question isn’t who deserves my love; it is whether I will love whoever is in need in front of me.

There is something deeper here too. Many early Christians saw Jesus Himself in the Samaritan: the despised outsider who finds us wounded and helpless, binds our wounds and pays the full cost of our healing. We love because He first loved us.
Relationship with God and love for others can’t be separated. John writes: ‘Whoever does not love their brother and sister, whom they have seen, cannot love God, whom they have not seen.’

verse.text: We love because He first loved us… Anyone who loves God must also love their brother and sister.

lessons: Love doesn’t ask ‘Who deserves it?’ but ‘Who needs it?’
Religion can become an excuse not to love; true faith shows itself in mercy.
Jesus is our Good Samaritan, and His love makes us loving.
questions: Why did the lawyer want to define ‘neighbour’?
How might religion become a reason not to love? Can you think of examples today?
Who are the ‘Samaritans’ in your world: people you might be tempted to look down on?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Is there anyone I have been “crossing to the other side” to avoid?’ Write down what you sense, and one step of mercy you can take.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for being my Good Samaritan.
Forgive me for walking past people in need, like…
Fill me with your compassion so that I love without limits.

mission.text: This week, show practical mercy to someone in need, giving time, help or money, and don’t tell anyone about it.

en.journal: Write about the difference between asking ‘Who is my neighbour?’ and ‘Who was a neighbour?’. How could that change the way you live this week?

af.title: Gaan en Doen Dieselfde
story: Die gelykenis van die Barmhartige Samaritaan is so bekend dat dit maklik is om te mis hoe skokkend dit was. Om die krag daarvan te voel, moet ons die gesprek sien wat dit uitgelok het.

’n Wetsgeleerde, ’n kenner van die wet van Moses, vra Jesus hoe om die ewige lewe te beërf. Jesus draai die vraag terug, en die wetsgeleerde som die wet pragtig op: het God volkome lief en het jou naaste lief soos jouself. Jesus stem saam: ‘Doen dit en jy sal lewe.’

Dan kom die opvolgvraag wat alles verklap: ‘omdat hy homself wou regverdig, het hy gevra: “En wie is my naaste?”’ Die wetsgeleerde wil ’n definisie met grense hê. As ‘naaste’ mede-Jode beteken, of goeie mense, dan kan hy hulle liefhê en regverdig voel, terwyl hy almal anders ignoreer.

Jesus antwoord met ’n storie wat die grense vernietig. Die twee godsdienstige beroepslui, ’n priester en ’n Leviet, sien die gewonde man en stap doelbewus na die ander kant. Hulle het dalk selfs godsdienstige redes gehad: om aan ’n lyk te raak, sou ’n priester onrein maak. Hulle godsdiens het ’n rede geword om nie lief te hê nie.

Dan bring Jesus ’n Samaritaan in. Vir Jesus se Joodse gehoor was dit skandalig. Samaritane is as ketters en vyande beskou, ’n gemengde volk met ’n besoedelde tempel en vals aanbidding. Net ’n hoofstuk vroeër het ’n Samaritaanse dorp geweier om Jesus te verwelkom, en Jakobus en Johannes wou vuur daarop laat neerdaal! Tog is die Samaritaan die een wat met innige jammerte beweeg word. Hy gee sy tyd, sy olie en wyn, sy donkie, sy geld en sy belofte.

Laastens draai Jesus die wetsgeleerde se vraag om. Hy het gevra: ‘Wie is my naaste?’ (wie moet ek liefhê?). Jesus vra: ‘Wie was ’n naaste?’ (wie het liefde gewys?). Die vraag is nie wie my liefde verdien nie; dit is of ek enigiemand wat voor my in nood is, sal liefhê.

Daar is ook iets dieper hier. Baie vroeë Christene het Jesus self in die Samaritaan gesien: die veragte buitestaander wat ons gewond en hulpeloos kry, ons wonde verbind en die volle prys vir ons genesing betaal. Ons het lief omdat Hy ons eerste liefgehad het.
Verhouding met God en liefde vir ander kan nie geskei word nie. Johannes skryf: ‘Wie sy broer en suster wat hy gesien het nie liefhet nie, kan God wat hy nie gesien het nie, nie liefhê nie.’

verse.text: Ons het lief omdat Hy ons eerste liefgehad het… Wie God liefhet, moet ook sy broer en suster liefhê.

lessons: Liefde vra nie ‘Wie verdien dit?’ nie, maar ‘Wie het dit nodig?’
Godsdiens kan ’n verskoning word om nie lief te hê nie; ware geloof wys homself in barmhartigheid.
Jesus is ons Barmhartige Samaritaan, en sy liefde maak ons liefdevol.
questions: Hoekom wou die wetsgeleerde ‘naaste’ definieer?
Hoe kan godsdiens ’n rede word om nie lief te hê nie? Kan jy aan voorbeelde vandag dink?
Wie is die ‘Samaritane’ in jou wêreld: mense op wie jy dalk in die versoeking kom om neer te sien?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Is daar iemand wat ek vermy deur “na die ander kant oor te stap”?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel, en een tree van barmhartigheid wat jy kan neem.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U my Barmhartige Samaritaan is.
Vergewe my dat ek verbyloop by mense in nood, soos…
Vul my met u medelye sodat ek sonder grense liefhet.

mission.text: Bewys hierdie week praktiese barmhartigheid aan iemand in nood, deur tyd, hulp of geld te gee, en moenie vir enigiemand daarvan vertel nie.

af.journal: Skryf oor die verskil tussen om te vra ‘Wie is my naaste?’ en ‘Wie was ’n naaste?’. Hoe kan dit verander hoe jy hierdie week lewe?

en.title: Be a Good Neighbour
story: A man was hurt on the road. Ouch!
Two people saw him, but they walked past.
Then a kind man stopped.
He put on plasters, gave him a ride on his donkey and took care of him.
Jesus says: be kind to everyone!

verse.text: Love your neighbour as yourself.

en.action: Pretend to put a plaster on someone’s arm and give them a gentle hug.
lessons: Jesus wants me to be kind to everyone.
questions: Who can you be kind to tomorrow?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
help me to be kind to everyone. Amen.

af.title: Wees ’n Goeie Naaste
story: ’n Man het op die pad seergekry. Eina!
Twee mense het hom gesien, maar hulle het verbygeloop.
Toe het ’n gawe man stilgehou.
Hy het pleisters opgesit, hom op sy donkie laat ry en vir hom gesorg.
Jesus sê: wees gaaf met almal!

verse.text: Jy moet jou naaste liefhê soos jouself.

af.action: Maak of jy ’n pleister op iemand se arm sit en gee hulle ’n sagte drukkie.
lessons: Jesus wil hê ek moet gaaf wees met almal.
questions: Met wie kan jy môre gaaf wees?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
help my om gaaf te wees met almal. Amen.

en.title: The Kind Stranger
story: One day a man asked Jesus, ‘God says I must love my neighbour. But who is my neighbour?’ So Jesus told a story.
A man was walking along a lonely road from Jerusalem to Jericho. Suddenly robbers jumped out! They took his clothes and his money, hurt him badly and left him lying by the road.

After a while a priest came walking by. He saw the hurt man, but he crossed to the other side of the road and kept going. Then a temple helper came by. He also looked, and he also walked past on the other side.
Then a Samaritan came along on his donkey. Now, Jewish people and Samaritans usually didn’t like each other at all. But when the Samaritan saw the hurt man, his heart was full of kindness.

He knelt down, cleaned the man’s wounds and bandaged them. He lifted him onto his own donkey and took him to an inn. He looked after him all night. In the morning he paid the innkeeper and said, ‘Take care of him. If it costs more, I’ll pay you when I come back.’
Jesus asked, ‘Which of the three was a good neighbour to the hurt man?’ The man answered, ‘The one who was kind to him.’ Jesus said, ‘Go and do the same.’
Your neighbour is anyone who needs your help, even someone who is different from you.

verse.text: Love your neighbour as yourself.

lessons: Jesus teaches me to love everyone, not just my friends.
My neighbour is anyone who needs help.
Love is something I do, not just something I feel.
questions: Why do you think the first two men walked past?
Who is someone different from you that you could be kind to?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you for being so kind to me.
Help me to notice people who need help,
and to be a good neighbour to everyone. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, be a ‘good neighbour’: help someone who needs it, especially someone you don’t usually play with.

af.title: Die Gawe Vreemdeling
story: Eendag het ’n man vir Jesus gevra: ‘God sê ek moet my naaste liefhê. Maar wie is my naaste?’ Toe het Jesus ’n storie vertel.
’n Man het op ’n eensame pad van Jerusalem na Jerigo geloop. Skielik het rowers uitgespring! Hulle het sy klere en sy geld gevat, hom erg seergemaak en hom langs die pad laat lê.

Ná ’n ruk het ’n priester verbygeloop. Hy het die man gesien wat seergekry het, maar hy het oorgestap na die ander kant van die pad en aangeloop. Toe het ’n tempelhelper verbygekom. Hy het ook gekyk, en hy het ook aan die ander kant verbygeloop.

Toe het ’n Samaritaan op sy donkie aangekom. Nou, Joodse mense en Samaritane het gewoonlik glad nie van mekaar gehou nie. Maar toe die Samaritaan die man sien wat seergekry het, was sy hart vol goedheid.

Hy het neergekniel, die man se wonde skoongemaak en verbind. Hy het hom op sy eie donkie gelig en na ’n herberg geneem. Hy het die hele nag vir hom gesorg. Die oggend het hy die herbergier betaal en gesê: ‘Sorg vir hom. As dit meer kos, sal ek jou betaal as ek terugkom.’
Jesus het gevra: ‘Watter een van die drie was ’n goeie naaste vir die man wat seergekry het?’ Die man het geantwoord: ‘Die een wat goed was vir hom.’ Jesus het gesê: ‘Gaan en doen dieselfde.’
Jou naaste is enigiemand wat jou hulp nodig het, selfs iemand wat anders is as jy.

verse.text: Jy moet jou naaste liefhê soos jouself.

lessons: Jesus leer my om almal lief te hê, nie net my maats nie.
My naaste is enigiemand wat hulp nodig het.
Liefde is iets wat ek doen, nie net iets wat ek voel nie.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het die eerste twee mans verbygeloop?
Wie is iemand wat anders is as jy met wie jy gaaf kan wees?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U so goed is vir my.
Help my om mense raak te sien wat hulp nodig het,
en ’n goeie naaste vir almal te wees. Amen.

mission.text: Wees môre ’n ‘goeie naaste’: help iemand wat dit nodig het, veral iemand met wie jy nie gewoonlik speel nie.

en.fact: The road from Jerusalem to Jericho was about 27 kilometres long and went steeply downhill through rocky desert. It was known as a dangerous road where robbers hid.
en.deeper: Why is it surprising that the hero of Jesus’ story was a Samaritan?
en.journal: Draw the kind Samaritan helping the hurt man. Write: ‘Go and do the same.’
