af.deeper: Hoekom is dit verrassend dat die held van Jesus se storie ’n Samaritaan was?
af.journal: Teken die gawe Samaritaan wat die man help wat seergekry het. Skryf: ‘Gaan en doen dieselfde.’

trait.en: God is our Father who loves to hear us
trait.af: God is ons Vader wat ons graag hoor

en.title: Lord, Teach Us to Pray
story: The disciples had watched Jesus pray many times. He got up early in the morning to pray, prayed alone on mountainsides and sometimes prayed all night. They could see that prayer was the source of His strength and closeness to the Father. So one day they asked, ‘Lord, teach us to pray.’

Jesus gave them a pattern we now call the Lord’s Prayer. It begins, ‘Our Father in heaven.’ Many people in Jesus’ time felt they had to approach God with long, formal titles. Jesus invites us to call Him Father, because through Jesus we are God’s children.

‘Hallowed be your name’ means: may your name be honoured as holy. ‘Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven’ means: may your rule and your good plans fill the earth, starting with me. Before asking for anything for ourselves, we put God first.

Then we bring our needs: ‘Give us today our daily bread’ (what we need for today). ‘Forgive us our sins, as we also forgive everyone who sins against us’ (we receive forgiveness and pass it on). ‘Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one’ (keep us close to you and protect us).

Jesus then told a funny story about a man who knocked on his friend’s door at midnight to borrow bread. The friend didn’t want to get up, but because the man kept knocking, he eventually did. Jesus said, ‘Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.’
And then the best part: ‘If you then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!’
Prayer isn’t a performance. It is a child talking with a loving Father who is delighted to listen and to give good gifts.

verse.text: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.

lessons: Through Jesus, we can call God ‘Father’.
The Lord’s Prayer teaches us to put God first, then bring our needs.
Our Father loves to give good gifts, especially the Holy Spirit.
questions: Why did the disciples want Jesus to teach them to pray?
What does each part of the Lord’s Prayer ask for?
What do you think it means to keep asking, seeking and knocking?
en.listen: Pray the Lord’s Prayer slowly, pausing after each line. Ask: ‘Father, which line do you want me to think about today?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Our Father in heaven, I want to honour your name.
Your kingdom come in my life, especially in…
Thank you that you love to give me good gifts.

mission.text: This week, pray the Lord’s Prayer each day, and add your own words after each line.

en.journal: Write the Lord’s Prayer in your own words, as if you were talking to a loving father.

af.title: Here, Leer Ons Bid
story: Die dissipels het baie keer gesien hoe Jesus bid. Hy het vroeg in die oggend opgestaan om te bid, alleen op berghange gebid en soms die hele nag gebid. Hulle kon sien dat gebed die bron van sy krag en nabyheid aan die Vader was. Toe vra hulle eendag: ‘Here, leer ons bid.’

Jesus het hulle ’n patroon gegee wat ons nou die Onse Vader noem. Dit begin: ‘Ons Vader in die hemel.’ Baie mense in Jesus se tyd het gevoel hulle moet God met lang, formele titels nader. Jesus nooi ons om Hom Vader te noem, want deur Jesus is ons God se kinders.

‘Laat u Naam geheilig word’ beteken: mag u Naam as heilig geëer word. ‘Laat u koninkryk kom, laat u wil geskied, soos in die hemel net so ook op die aarde’ beteken: mag u heerskappy en u goeie planne die aarde vul, en by my begin. Voordat ons vir onsself vra, stel ons God eerste.

Dan bring ons ons behoeftes: ‘Gee ons vandag ons daaglikse brood’ (wat ons vir vandag nodig het). ‘Vergeef ons ons sondes, soos ons ook almal vergewe wat teen ons sondig’ (ons ontvang vergifnis en gee dit aan). ‘Lei ons nie in versoeking nie, maar verlos ons van die Bose’ (hou ons naby U en beskerm ons).

Jesus het toe ’n snaakse storie vertel van ’n man wat middernag aan sy vriend se deur geklop het om brood te leen. Die vriend wou nie opstaan nie, maar omdat die man aangehou klop het, het hy op die ou end. Jesus het gesê: ‘Vra en vir julle sal gegee word; soek en julle sal kry; klop en vir julle sal oopgemaak word.’
En dan die beste deel: ‘As julle dan, al is julle sleg, weet om goeie gawes aan julle kinders te gee, hoeveel te meer sal julle Vader in die hemel die Heilige Gees gee aan die wat Hom vra!’
Gebed is nie ’n vertoning nie. Dit is ’n kind wat praat met ’n liefdevolle Vader wat dit geniet om te luister en goeie gawes te gee.

verse.text: Vra en vir julle sal gegee word; soek en julle sal kry; klop en vir julle sal oopgemaak word.

lessons: Deur Jesus kan ons God ‘Vader’ noem.
Die Onse Vader leer ons om God eerste te stel, en dan ons behoeftes te bring.
Ons Vader gee graag goeie gawes, veral die Heilige Gees.
questions: Hoekom wou die dissipels hê Jesus moet hulle leer bid?
Waarvoor vra elke deel van die Onse Vader?
Wat dink jy beteken dit om aan te hou vra, soek en klop?
af.listen: Bid die Onse Vader stadig, en wag ná elke reël. Vra: ‘Vader, oor watter reël wil U hê moet ek vandag dink?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Ons Vader in die hemel, ek wil u Naam eer.
Laat u koninkryk in my lewe kom, veral in…
Dankie dat U my graag goeie gawes gee.

mission.text: Bid hierdie week elke dag die Onse Vader, en voeg ná elke reël jou eie woorde by.

af.journal: Skryf die Onse Vader in jou eie woorde, asof jy met ’n liefdevolle vader praat.

en.title: Abba, Father
story: In Matthew 6, Jesus teaches about prayer in the Sermon on the Mount. Before giving His model prayer, He warns against two wrong ways of praying. The first is praying to be seen, like the hypocrites who ‘love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by others’. Prayer is not a performance for an audience. The second is ‘babbling like pagans’, who think they will be heard ‘because of their many words’. Prayer is not a technique to manipulate God. ‘Your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.’

So why pray? Because prayer is relationship. Jesus begins with two words that changed everything: ‘Our Father.’ In Mark 14 Jesus prays ‘Abba, Father’, using the Aramaic word a child would use for their dad. It is warm, close and trusting. Astonishingly, Paul tells us that the Holy Spirit in us cries out the same word: ‘The Spirit you received brought about your adoption to sonship. And by Him we cry, “Abba, Father.”’ Through Jesus, we are not just servants of God. We are His children.

Look at the structure of the prayer. The first half is about God: His name honoured, His kingdom coming, His will done. The second half is about us: daily provision, forgiveness and protection. Putting God first doesn’t make our needs unimportant. It puts them in the right place.

One line gets special emphasis. Right after the prayer, Jesus adds, ‘If you forgive other people when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.’ This doesn’t mean we earn forgiveness by forgiving. It means a heart that has truly received God’s mercy will become merciful. Refusing to forgive blocks the flow of grace in our own lives.
In Luke 11 Jesus adds two encouragements: keep asking, seeking and knocking (persistence), and trust that your Father gives good gifts, above all the Holy Spirit.

This prayer isn’t meant only to be recited, though reciting it together is beautiful. It is a pattern, a map for a conversation with your Father. You can pray it word for word, and you can use each line as a starting point for your own words.

verse.text: The Spirit you received brought about your adoption… And by Him we cry, ‘Abba, Father.’

lessons: Prayer is relationship, not performance or technique.
Through Jesus and by the Spirit, we can call God ‘Abba, Father’.
The Lord’s Prayer puts God first and our needs in the right place.
questions: What two wrong ways of praying does Jesus warn against?
What does it mean to you that you can call God ‘Abba’?
Why do you think Jesus linked receiving forgiveness so closely with forgiving others?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Use the Lord’s Prayer as a map: pause at each line and add your own words. At the end, sit quietly and ask your Father what He wants to say. Write it down.
prayer: Abba, Father, thank you that I am your child.
Your kingdom come and your will be done in…
Help me to forgive… as you have forgiven me.

mission.text: This week, spend one prayer time each day using the Lord’s Prayer as a map, adding your own words to each line.

en.journal: Write a personal version of the Lord’s Prayer, with one paragraph for each line, about your life right now.

af.title: Abba, Vader
story: In Matteus 6 leer Jesus oor gebed in die Bergpredikasie. Voordat Hy sy voorbeeldgebed gee, waarsku Hy teen twee verkeerde maniere van bid. Die eerste is om te bid om gesien te word, soos die skynheiliges wat ‘graag in die sinagoges en op die straathoeke staan en bid sodat ander hulle kan sien’. Gebed is nie ’n vertoning vir ’n gehoor nie. Die tweede is om ‘aan te babbel soos die heidene’, wat dink hulle sal gehoor word ‘oor hulle baie woorde’. Gebed is nie ’n tegniek om God te manipuleer nie. ‘Julle Vader weet wat julle nodig het voordat julle Hom vra.’

Hoekom bid ons dan? Omdat gebed verhouding is. Jesus begin met twee woorde wat alles verander het: ‘Ons Vader.’ In Markus 14 bid Jesus ‘Abba, Vader’, en gebruik die Aramese woord wat ’n kind vir sy pa sou gebruik. Dit is warm, naby en vol vertroue. Verbasend genoeg vertel Paulus ons dat die Heilige Gees in ons dieselfde woord uitroep: ‘Die Gees wat julle ontvang het, het julle as kinders aangeneem. En deur Hom roep ons: “Abba, Vader.”’ Deur Jesus is ons nie net diensknegte van God nie. Ons is sy kinders.

Kyk na die struktuur van die gebed. Die eerste helfte gaan oor God: sy Naam geëer, sy koninkryk wat kom, sy wil wat geskied. Die tweede helfte gaan oor ons: daaglikse voorsiening, vergifnis en beskerming. Om God eerste te stel, maak nie ons behoeftes onbelangrik nie. Dit plaas hulle op die regte plek.

Een reël kry spesiale klem. Net ná die gebed voeg Jesus by: ‘As julle ander mense vergewe wanneer hulle teen julle sondig, sal julle hemelse Vader julle ook vergewe.’ Dit beteken nie ons verdien vergifnis deur te vergewe nie. Dit beteken ’n hart wat God se genade regtig ontvang het, sal genadig word. Om te weier om te vergewe, blokkeer die vloei van genade in ons eie lewe.
In Lukas 11 voeg Jesus twee bemoedigings by: hou aan vra, soek en klop (volharding), en vertrou dat jou Vader goeie gawes gee, bo alles die Heilige Gees.

Hierdie gebed is nie net bedoel om opgesê te word nie, al is dit pragtig om dit saam op te sê. Dit is ’n patroon, ’n kaart vir ’n gesprek met jou Vader. Jy kan dit woord vir woord bid, en jy kan elke reël as ’n beginpunt vir jou eie woorde gebruik.

verse.text: Die Gees wat julle ontvang het, het julle as kinders aangeneem… En deur Hom roep ons: ‘Abba, Vader.’

lessons: Gebed is verhouding, nie ’n vertoning of tegniek nie.
Deur Jesus en deur die Gees kan ons God ‘Abba, Vader’ noem.
Die Onse Vader stel God eerste en plaas ons behoeftes op die regte plek.
questions: Teen watter twee verkeerde maniere van bid waarsku Jesus?
Wat beteken dit vir jou dat jy God ‘Abba’ kan noem?
Hoekom dink jy het Jesus die ontvang van vergifnis so nou verbind met om ander te vergewe?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Gebruik die Onse Vader as ’n kaart: wag by elke reël en voeg jou eie woorde by. Sit aan die einde stil en vra jou Vader wat Hy wil sê. Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Abba, Vader, dankie dat ek u kind is.
Laat u koninkryk kom en u wil geskied in…
Help my om… te vergewe soos U my vergewe het.

mission.text: Gebruik hierdie week elke dag een gebedstyd die Onse Vader as ’n kaart, en voeg by elke reël jou eie woorde by.

af.journal: Skryf ’n persoonlike weergawe van die Onse Vader, met een paragraaf vir elke reël, oor jou lewe op die oomblik.

en.title: Our Father
story: Jesus’ friends said, ‘Please teach us to pray.’
Jesus said, ‘Talk to God like a loving Father.’
‘Say: Our Father in heaven, your name is special.’
‘Please give us food, forgive us, and keep us safe.’
God is our Father, and He loves to hear us.

verse.text: Our Father in heaven, your name is holy.

en.action: Fold your hands and say with a grown-up: ‘Our Father in heaven…’
lessons: God is my Father who loves to hear me.
questions: What would you like to say to Father God?
prayer: Dear Father in heaven,
thank you for loving me. Amen.

af.title: Ons Vader
story: Jesus se vriende het gesê: ‘Leer ons asseblief om te bid.’
Jesus het gesê: ‘Praat met God soos met ’n liefdevolle Vader.’
‘Sê: Ons Vader in die hemel, u Naam is spesiaal.’
‘Gee ons asseblief kos, vergewe ons, en hou ons veilig.’
God is ons Vader, en Hy hoor ons graag.

verse.text: Ons Vader in die hemel, laat u Naam geheilig word.

af.action: Vou jou hande en sê saam met ’n grootmens: ‘Ons Vader in die hemel…’
lessons: God is my Vader wat my graag hoor.
questions: Wat wil jy vir Vader God sê?
prayer: Liewe Vader in die hemel,
dankie dat U my liefhet. Amen.

en.title: Teach Us to Pray
story: Jesus often went off by Himself to pray. Sometimes He prayed all night! His disciples watched Him, and one day they said, ‘Lord, teach us to pray.’
So Jesus taught them a prayer. It starts like this: ‘Our Father in heaven.’ Jesus wanted us to know that we can talk to God like a child talks to a loving dad.

Then Jesus showed us what to pray about. ‘Hallowed be your name’ means: God, you are wonderful and holy. ‘Your kingdom come, your will be done’ means: God, please make things on earth good, the way they are in heaven.

‘Give us today our daily bread’ means: please give us what we need. ‘Forgive us our sins, as we forgive others’ means: please forgive me, and help me forgive people who hurt me. ‘Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil’ means: please help me choose what is right, and keep me safe.

Then Jesus told a little story. ‘If your child asks for bread, would you give them a stone? If they ask for a fish, would you give them a snake?’ Of course not! ‘If you know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!’
God isn’t far away or too busy. He is your Father, and He loves to hear from you.

verse.text: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.

lessons: God is our Father who loves to hear us.
Jesus taught us what to pray about.
Our Father loves to give good gifts to His children.
questions: What does it mean that we can call God ‘Father’?
Which part of the Lord’s Prayer do you like best?
prayer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
Your kingdom come, your will be done.
Give us our daily bread, forgive us as we forgive,
and keep us safe. Amen.

mission.text: This week, say the Lord’s Prayer together each night and talk about one line.

af.title: Leer Ons Bid
story: Jesus het dikwels alleen weggegaan om te bid. Soms het Hy die hele nag gebid! Sy dissipels het Hom dopgehou, en eendag het hulle gesê: ‘Here, leer ons bid.’
Toe het Jesus hulle ’n gebed geleer. Dit begin so: ‘Ons Vader in die hemel.’ Jesus wou hê ons moet weet dat ons met God kan praat soos ’n kind met ’n liefdevolle pa praat.

Toe het Jesus ons gewys waaroor om te bid. ‘Laat u Naam geheilig word’ beteken: God, U is wonderlik en heilig. ‘Laat u koninkryk kom, laat u wil geskied’ beteken: God, maak asseblief dinge op aarde goed, soos dit in die hemel is.

‘Gee ons vandag ons daaglikse brood’ beteken: gee ons asseblief wat ons nodig het. ‘Vergeef ons ons sondes, soos ons ander vergewe’ beteken: vergewe my asseblief, en help my om mense te vergewe wat my seermaak. ‘Lei ons nie in versoeking nie, maar verlos ons van die Bose’ beteken: help my asseblief om te kies wat reg is, en hou my veilig.

Toe het Jesus ’n storietjie vertel. ‘As jou kind vir brood vra, sal jy vir hulle ’n klip gee? As hulle vir ’n vis vra, sal jy vir hulle ’n slang gee?’ Natuurlik nie! ‘As julle weet hoe om goeie geskenke aan julle kinders te gee, hoeveel te meer sal julle Vader in die hemel goeie dinge gee aan die wat Hom vra!’
God is nie ver weg of te besig nie. Hy is jou Vader, en Hy hou daarvan om van jou te hoor.

verse.text: Ons Vader in die hemel, laat u Naam geheilig word.

lessons: God is ons Vader wat ons graag hoor.
Jesus het ons geleer waaroor om te bid.
Ons Vader hou daarvan om goeie geskenke aan sy kinders te gee.
questions: Wat beteken dit dat ons God ‘Vader’ kan noem?
Van watter deel van die Onse Vader hou jy die meeste?
prayer: Ons Vader in die hemel, laat u Naam geheilig word.
Laat u koninkryk kom, laat u wil geskied.
Gee ons ons daaglikse brood, vergeef ons soos ons vergewe,
en hou ons veilig. Amen.

mission.text: Bid hierdie week elke aand saam die Onse Vader en gesels oor een reël.

en.title: Campfire Night: Jesus the Healer
story: Welcome to the fourth campfire of the Trail of the Living Water! This week you walked with Jesus: at a wedding where water became the best wine; in a crowded house where four friends opened a roof; in a crowd where a trembling woman touched His cloak and was called ‘Daughter’; at Jairus’ house, where Jesus said, ‘Don’t be afraid; just believe’; on a dangerous road in a story about a kind Samaritan; and on a hillside where Jesus taught His friends to pray ‘Our Father’. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever. He still brings joy, forgives, heals, notices, raises hope and teaches us to love and pray.
en.game: Healer’s bag: put six objects in a bag (a cup, a small mat or cloth, a scarf, a sock ‘doll’, a plaster, a piece of bread). Take turns pulling one out and telling which story it belongs to and what it shows about Jesus.
questions: Which story about Jesus this week touched your heart most?
How has Jesus helped you be a neighbour or a praying friend this week?
What have you sensed God saying in your Listening times?
prayer: Jesus, you are the same yesterday, today and forever.
Thank you that you notice me, forgive me and help me believe.
Teach me to love like you and to pray to our Father.

mission.text: Learn Hebrews 13:8 by heart this week, and say the Lord’s Prayer together as a family.

en.journal: Write a thank-you letter to Jesus for one thing He did in this week’s stories, and one thing He has done in your life.

af.title: Kampvuuraand: Jesus die Geneser
story: Welkom by die vierde kampvuur van Die Pad van die Lewende Water! Hierdie week het jy saam met Jesus geloop: by ’n troue waar water die beste wyn geword het; in ’n stampvol huis waar vier vriende ’n dak oopgemaak het; in ’n skare waar ’n bewende vrou aan sy mantel geraak en ‘Dogter’ genoem is; by Jaïrus se huis, waar Jesus gesê het: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; glo net’; op ’n gevaarlike pad in ’n storie oor ’n gawe Samaritaan; en op ’n heuwel waar Jesus sy vriende geleer het om ‘Ons Vader’ te bid. Jesus Christus is gister en vandag dieselfde, en tot in ewigheid. Hy bring nog steeds vreugde, vergewe, genees, sien raak, wek hoop en leer ons om lief te hê en te bid.
af.game: Geneser se sak: sit ses voorwerpe in ’n sak (’n beker, ’n klein matjie of lap, ’n serp, ’n kous-‘pop’, ’n pleister, ’n stuk brood). Haal om die beurt een uit en sê by watter storie dit hoort en wat dit oor Jesus wys.
questions: Watter storie oor Jesus hierdie week het jou hart die meeste geraak?
Hoe het Jesus jou hierdie week gehelp om ’n naaste of ’n biddende vriend te wees?
Wat het jy aangevoel God sê in jou Luistertye?
prayer: Jesus, U is gister en vandag dieselfde, en tot in ewigheid.
Dankie dat U my raaksien, my vergewe en my help om te glo.
Leer my om lief te hê soos U en tot ons Vader te bid.

mission.text: Leer hierdie week Hebreërs 13:8 uit jou kop, en bid saam as familie die Onse Vader.

af.journal: Skryf ’n dankiebrief aan Jesus vir een ding wat Hy in hierdie week se stories gedoen het, en een ding wat Hy in jou lewe gedoen het.

en.title: Campfire Night: Jesus the Healer
story: This week you saw Jesus reveal His glory through signs: joy overflowing at a wedding, sins forgiven with the authority of God, an outcast made clean and called ‘Daughter’, death redefined as sleep, love that refuses to set limits, and prayer that begins with ‘Abba, Father’. Each story answers the question the crowds kept asking: ‘Who is this?’ He is the Messiah, the Son of Man, the Lord who forgives and heals, and the Good Samaritan who finds us on the road. And because He is the same yesterday, today and forever, the Jesus of these stories is the Jesus you can meet tonight.

Elke storie beantwoord die vraag wat die skares aanhou vra het: ‘Wie is Hy?’ Hy is die Messias, die Seun van die mens, die Here wat vergewe en genees, en die Barmhartige Samaritaan wat ons op die pad kry. Hierdie week het ek geleer dat U…

en.title: A Thirst Only Jesus Can Satisfy
story: Most Jewish travellers avoided Samaria completely, taking a longer route to stay away from the Samaritans, whom they despised. But John says Jesus ‘had to go through Samaria’. He had an appointment to keep.

At noon, in the hottest part of the day, Jesus sat down by Jacob’s well, tired from the journey. A Samaritan woman came to draw water. Most women came in the cool of the morning, together. This woman came alone, at noon. She was probably avoiding the other women’s stares and whispers.

Jesus broke three rules at once: He, a Jewish man, spoke to a Samaritan woman in public and asked to drink from her jar. ‘Will you give me a drink?’ She was astonished. ‘How can you ask me for a drink?’

Jesus replied, ‘If you knew the gift of God and who it is that asks you for a drink, you would have asked Him and He would have given you living water.’ She thought He meant running water. But Jesus explained: ‘Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again, but whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst… it will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life.’

Then Jesus gently showed that He knew her life story: she had had five husbands, and the man she lived with now wasn’t her husband. She was used to being judged. But Jesus wasn’t exposing her to shame her. He was showing her that He knew everything and still offered her the gift of God.

She tried to change the subject to a religious argument, but Jesus brought it back to the heart: God is looking for people who worship Him ‘in Spirit and in truth’. Then He told her plainly, ‘I, the one speaking to you, am the Messiah.’

She left her water jar and ran into town: ‘Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Messiah?’ The woman who had been avoiding everyone became the first evangelist to her town, and many Samaritans believed.
Everyone is thirsty for something: love, acceptance, purpose. Only Jesus can truly satisfy that thirst.

verse.text: Whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst.

lessons: Jesus crosses every barrier to reach people.
Jesus knows everything about us and still offers us the gift of God.
Only Jesus can truly satisfy our deepest thirst.
questions: What three ‘rules’ did Jesus break by talking to the woman?
Why do you think she left her water jar behind?
What do people today try to ‘drink’ to satisfy their hearts?
en.listen: Be still and ask Jesus: ‘What am I thirsty for?’ Then ask, ‘How do you want to fill me?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, you know everything about me and still love me.
My heart is thirsty for…
Fill me with your living water.

mission.text: This week, reach out to someone who is often alone or avoided, as Jesus did at the well.

en.journal: Draw two cups: one labelled ‘things that never fully satisfy’ and one labelled ‘living water’. Fill each with words.

af.title: ’n Dors wat Net Jesus Kan Les
story: Die meeste Joodse reisigers het Samaria heeltemal vermy, en ’n langer roete gevat om weg te bly van die Samaritane, op wie hulle neergesien het. Maar Johannes sê Jesus ‘moes deur Samaria gaan’. Hy het ’n afspraak gehad om te hou.

Teen twaalfuur, die warmste deel van die dag, het Jesus by Jakob se put gaan sit, moeg van die reis. ’n Samaritaanse vrou het gekom om water te skep. Die meeste vroue het saam in die koelte van die oggend gekom. Hierdie vrou het alleen gekom, teen twaalfuur. Sy het waarskynlik die ander vroue se starende blikke en fluisterery vermy.

Jesus het drie reëls op een slag gebreek: Hy, ’n Joodse man, het in die openbaar met ’n Samaritaanse vrou gepraat en gevra om uit haar kruik te drink. ‘Sal jy vir My iets gee om te drink?’ Sy was verstom. ‘Hoe kan U my vir iets te drinke vra?’

Jesus het geantwoord: ‘As jy die gawe van God geken het en geweet het wie dit is wat vir jou vra om te drink, sou jy Hom gevra het en Hy sou jou lewende water gegee het.’ Sy het gedink Hy bedoel lopende water. Maar Jesus het verduidelik: ‘Elkeen wat van hierdie water drink, sal weer dors kry, maar wie van die water drink wat Ek hom sal gee, sal nooit weer dors kry nie… dit sal in hom ’n fontein word wat opborrel tot die ewige lewe.’

Toe het Jesus saggies gewys dat Hy haar lewensverhaal ken: sy het vyf mans gehad, en die man by wie sy nou bly, was nie haar man nie. Sy was gewoond daaraan om veroordeel te word. Maar Jesus het haar nie ontbloot om haar skaam te maak nie. Hy het haar gewys dat Hy alles weet en haar steeds die gawe van God aanbied.

Sy het probeer om die onderwerp na ’n godsdienstige argument te verander, maar Jesus het dit teruggebring na die hart: God soek mense wat Hom ‘in Gees en waarheid’ aanbid. Toe het Hy haar reguit gesê: ‘Ek wat met jou praat, is die Messias.’

Sy het haar waterkruik gelos en dorp toe gehardloop: ‘Kom kyk na ’n man wat my alles vertel het wat ek gedoen het. Kan Hy die Messias wees?’ Die vrou wat almal vermy het, het die eerste evangelis vir haar dorp geword, en baie Samaritane het geglo.
Almal is dors na iets: liefde, aanvaarding, ’n doel. Net Jesus kan daardie dors regtig les.

verse.text: Wie van die water drink wat Ek hom sal gee, sal nooit weer dors kry nie.

lessons: Jesus steek elke grens oor om mense te bereik.
Jesus weet alles van ons en bied ons steeds die gawe van God aan.
Net Jesus kan ons diepste dors regtig les.
questions: Watter drie ‘reëls’ het Jesus gebreek deur met die vrou te praat?
Hoekom dink jy het sy haar waterkruik agtergelaat?
Wat probeer mense vandag ‘drink’ om hulle harte tevrede te stel?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra Jesus: ‘Waarna is ek dors?’ Vra dan: ‘Hoe wil U my vul?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, U weet alles van my en het my steeds lief.
My hart is dors na…
Vul my met u lewende water.

mission.text: Reik hierdie week uit na iemand wat dikwels alleen is of vermy word, soos Jesus by die put gedoen het.

af.journal: Teken twee bekers: een met die naam ‘dinge wat nooit heeltemal tevrede stel nie’ en een met die naam ‘lewende water’. Vul elkeen met woorde.

en.title: Spirit and Truth
story: John 4 is the longest conversation Jesus has with any individual in the Gospels, and it is with a person almost everyone else would have ignored. She is a Samaritan, a woman and, by her community’s standards, a moral failure. Yet Jesus treats her as someone worth a serious conversation about God.
Notice how Jesus begins: by asking for help. ‘Will you give me a drink?’ He makes Himself the one in need. That small act of humility opens a door.

Then He offers her ‘living water’. In Hebrew thought, ‘living water’ meant fresh, flowing water from a spring, as opposed to still water in a cistern. The prophet Jeremiah used this image: God’s people had ‘forsaken me, the spring of living water, and have dug their own cisterns, broken cisterns that cannot hold water’. Jesus is presenting Himself as the spring that the human heart was made for.

When Jesus mentions her five husbands, He isn’t condemning her; He’s uncovering her thirst. She had looked for security and love in relationship after relationship, and each one had left her emptier. Many of us do the same with other things: popularity, achievement, possessions or screens. They are ‘broken cisterns’. They promise to satisfy, but they leak.

She deflects with a theological debate: Jews say worship in Jerusalem, Samaritans on Mount Gerizim; who is right? Jesus’ answer goes deeper than either side expected: ‘A time is coming and has now come when the true worshippers will worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth.’ Worship is no longer about a place but about a relationship with the Father, made possible by the Spirit and grounded in the truth revealed in Jesus.

Then comes Jesus’ clearest self-revelation in John so far: ‘I, the one speaking to you, am He’ (literally, ‘I am’, the divine name God gave Moses). And He reveals it to her, the outsider, before many of the religious leaders.

Her response is beautiful. She leaves her water jar, the symbol of her old daily routine of thirst, and becomes a witness. ‘Come, see.’ That is still the simplest way to share Jesus: tell people what He has done for you, and invite them to meet Him.

verse.text: True worshippers will worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth, for they are the kind of worshippers the Father seeks.

lessons: Jesus offers Himself as the spring that our hearts were made for.
Broken cisterns, the things we look to instead of God, never fully satisfy.
True worship is a relationship with the Father, in the Spirit and in truth.
questions: What ‘broken cisterns’ do people in your generation look to?
What does it mean to worship ‘in the Spirit and in truth’?
Why do you think Jesus revealed Himself so clearly to this particular woman?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Is there a broken cistern I keep going back to?’ Then ask Jesus to be your spring of living water. Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, you are the spring of living water.
I confess I often look to… to satisfy me.
Teach me to worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth.

mission.text: This week, take a break from one ‘broken cistern’ (a habit or app) and spend that time with Jesus instead.

en.journal: Write your own ‘Come, see’ story: what has Jesus done in your life that you could share with a friend?

af.title: Gees en Waarheid
story: Johannes 4 is die langste gesprek wat Jesus in die Evangelies met enige individu het, en dit is met iemand wat byna almal anders sou geïgnoreer het. Sy is ’n Samaritaan, ’n vrou en, volgens haar gemeenskap se standaarde, ’n morele mislukking. Tog behandel Jesus haar as iemand wat ’n ernstige gesprek oor God werd is.
Let op hoe Jesus begin: deur vir hulp te vra. ‘Sal jy vir My iets gee om te drink?’ Hy maak Homself die een in nood. Daardie klein daad van nederigheid maak ’n deur oop.

Dan bied Hy haar ‘lewende water’ aan. In Hebreeuse denke het ‘lewende water’ vars, vloeiende water uit ’n fontein beteken, teenoor stilstaande water in ’n opgaartenk. Die profeet Jeremia het hierdie beeld gebruik: God se volk het ‘My, die fontein van lewende water, verlaat en vir hulleself opgaartenks uitgekap, gebreekte tenks wat nie water kan hou nie’. Jesus stel Homself voor as die fontein waarvoor die menslike hart gemaak is.

Wanneer Jesus haar vyf mans noem, veroordeel Hy haar nie; Hy ontbloot haar dors. Sy het in verhouding ná verhouding na sekuriteit en liefde gesoek, en elkeen het haar leër gelaat. Baie van ons doen dieselfde met ander dinge: gewildheid, prestasie, besittings of skerms. Hulle is ‘gebreekte tenks’. Hulle belowe om tevrede te stel, maar hulle lek.

Sy keer dit af met ’n teologiese debat: Jode sê aanbid in Jerusalem, Samaritane op die berg Gerisim; wie is reg? Jesus se antwoord gaan dieper as wat enige kant verwag het: ‘Die tyd kom, en dit is nou al hier, dat die ware aanbidders die Vader in Gees en waarheid sal aanbid.’ Aanbidding gaan nie meer oor ’n plek nie, maar oor ’n verhouding met die Vader, moontlik gemaak deur die Gees en gegrond op die waarheid wat in Jesus geopenbaar is.

Dan kom Jesus se duidelikste selfopenbaring tot dusver in Johannes: ‘Ek wat met jou praat, is Hy’ (letterlik ‘Ek is’, die goddelike Naam wat God aan Moses gegee het). En Hy openbaar dit aan haar, die buitestaander, voor baie van die godsdienstige leiers.

Haar reaksie is pragtig. Sy los haar waterkruik, die simbool van haar ou daaglikse roetine van dors, en word ’n getuie. ‘Kom kyk.’ Dit is steeds die eenvoudigste manier om Jesus te deel: vertel mense wat Hy vir jou gedoen het, en nooi hulle om Hom te ontmoet.

verse.text: Die ware aanbidders sal die Vader in Gees en waarheid aanbid, want die Vader soek sulke aanbidders.

lessons: Jesus bied Homself aan as die fontein waarvoor ons harte gemaak is.
Gebreekte tenks, die dinge waarna ons kyk in plaas van God, stel nooit heeltemal tevrede nie.
Ware aanbidding is ’n verhouding met die Vader, in Gees en waarheid.
questions: Na watter ‘gebreekte tenks’ kyk mense in jou geslag?
Wat beteken dit om ‘in Gees en waarheid’ te aanbid?
Hoekom dink jy het Jesus Homself so duidelik aan hierdie spesifieke vrou geopenbaar?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra God: ‘Is daar ’n gebreekte tenk waarna ek aanhou teruggaan?’ Vra dan Jesus om jou fontein van lewende water te wees. Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, U is die fontein van lewende water.
Ek bely dat ek dikwels na… kyk om my tevrede te stel.
Leer my om die Vader in Gees en waarheid te aanbid.

mission.text: Neem hierdie week ’n blaaskans van een ‘gebreekte tenk’ (’n gewoonte of toep) en bring daardie tyd eerder saam met Jesus deur.

af.journal: Skryf jou eie ‘Kom kyk’-storie: wat het Jesus in jou lewe gedoen wat jy met ’n vriend kan deel?

en.title: Living Water
story: Jesus sat by a well. He was tired and thirsty.
A lady came to get water. Jesus asked, ‘Can I have a drink, please?’
Jesus told her, ‘I have special water. It’s called living water.’
‘When you have my water, your heart will never be thirsty again!’
Jesus fills my heart with His love.

verse.text: Whoever drinks the water I give will never be thirsty.

en.action: Take a sip of water and say: ‘Jesus fills my heart!’
lessons: Jesus fills my heart with His love.
questions: Are you thirsty? What do you like to drink?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
please fill my heart with your love. Amen.

af.title: Lewende Water
story: Jesus het by ’n put gesit. Hy was moeg en dors.
’n Vrou het gekom om water te skep. Jesus het gevra: ‘Kan Ek asseblief iets te drinke kry?’
Jesus het vir haar gesê: ‘Ek het spesiale water. Dit word lewende water genoem.’
‘As jy my water het, sal jou hart nooit weer dors wees nie!’
Jesus vul my hart met sy liefde.

verse.text: Wie die water drink wat Ek gee, sal nooit dors kry nie.

af.action: Drink ’n slukkie water en sê: ‘Jesus vul my hart!’
lessons: Jesus vul my hart met sy liefde.
questions: Is jy dors? Wat drink jy graag?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
vul asseblief my hart met u liefde. Amen.

en.title: The Woman at the Well
story: Jesus and His disciples were on a long walk through a place called Samaria. At lunchtime, Jesus sat down by an old well to rest, while His disciples went to buy food. It was hot, and Jesus was tired and thirsty.
A woman came to the well with her water jar. She came in the middle of the day, when no one else was there, because people were often unkind to her.
Jesus said, ‘Will you give me a drink?’ The woman was surprised! Jewish men didn’t usually talk to Samaritan women. But Jesus wasn’t like other people. He was kind to everyone.
Then Jesus said something amazing: ‘If you knew who I am, you would ask me, and I would give you living water. Whoever drinks the water I give will never be thirsty again.’

Jesus wasn’t talking about water for your tummy. He meant something for your heart. Everyone’s heart is thirsty for love, for friendship with God, and for life that lasts forever. Only Jesus can fill that thirst.

Jesus knew everything about the woman, even the sad things, and He still loved her. She was so happy that she left her water jar and ran to tell the whole town, ‘Come and meet a man who knows everything about me! Could He be the Saviour?’ And many people came and believed in Jesus.
Jesus offers His living water to you too.

verse.text: Whoever drinks the water I give them will never be thirsty.

lessons: Jesus satisfies my thirsty heart.
Jesus knows everything about me and still loves me.
When I meet Jesus, I want to tell others about Him.
questions: Why was the woman surprised that Jesus talked to her?
What do you think ‘living water’ is?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you for your living water.
Please fill my heart with your love
so that I never feel empty inside. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, be kind to someone others might not talk to, just like Jesus was.

af.title: Die Vrou by die Put
story: Jesus en sy dissipels was op ’n lang staptog deur ’n plek met die naam Samaria. Teen middagete het Jesus by ’n ou put gaan sit om te rus, terwyl sy dissipels kos gaan koop het. Dit was warm, en Jesus was moeg en dors.
’n Vrou het met haar waterkruik na die put gekom. Sy het in die middel van die dag gekom, as niemand anders daar was nie, want mense was dikwels onvriendelik met haar.

Jesus het gesê: ‘Sal jy vir My iets gee om te drink?’ Die vrou was verbaas! Joodse mans het gewoonlik nie met Samaritaanse vroue gepraat nie. Maar Jesus was nie soos ander mense nie. Hy was goed vir almal.
Toe sê Jesus iets wonderliks: ‘As jy geweet het wie Ek is, sou jy My gevra het, en Ek sou jou lewende water gegee het. Wie die water drink wat Ek gee, sal nooit weer dors kry nie.’

Jesus het nie van water vir jou maag gepraat nie. Hy het iets vir jou hart bedoel. Almal se harte is dors vir liefde, vir vriendskap met God, en vir lewe wat vir altyd hou. Net Jesus kan daardie dors les.

Jesus het alles van die vrou geweet, selfs die hartseer dinge, en Hy het haar steeds liefgehad. Sy was so bly dat sy haar waterkruik gelos en na die hele dorp gehardloop het om te vertel: ‘Kom ontmoet ’n man wat alles van my weet! Kan Hy die Verlosser wees?’ En baie mense het gekom en in Jesus geglo.
Jesus bied sy lewende water ook vir jou aan.

verse.text: Wie van die water drink wat Ek hom gee, sal nooit dors kry nie.

lessons: Jesus les my dors hart.
Jesus weet alles van my en het my steeds lief.
As ek Jesus ontmoet, wil ek ander van Hom vertel.
questions: Hoekom was die vrou verbaas dat Jesus met haar gepraat het?
Wat dink jy is ‘lewende water’?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie vir u lewende water.
Vul asseblief my hart met u liefde
sodat ek nooit leeg voel binne-in nie. Amen.

mission.text: Wees môre gaaf met iemand met wie ander dalk nie praat nie, net soos Jesus was.

af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy het die vrou haar waterkruik agtergelaat toe sy dorp toe gehardloop het?
af.journal: Teken ’n put met water wat uitvloei. Skryf: ‘Jesus gee lewende water.’

trait.en: Being with Jesus matters most
trait.af: Om by Jesus te wees, is die belangrikste

en.title: Distracted or Devoted?
story: Martha opened her home to Jesus. That was generous and brave, since Jesus travelled with a large group of disciples, and hosting them all was a lot of work. Martha loved Jesus and wanted everything to be perfect for Him.

Her sister Mary did something unusual. She ‘sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what He said’. In that culture, sitting at a teacher’s feet was the position of a disciple, a student learning from a rabbi. Women were rarely given that place. But Jesus welcomed Mary as His disciple.

Meanwhile, Luke says Martha was ‘distracted by all the preparations that had to be made’. The more she worked, the more frustrated she became, until she burst out, ‘Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!’
Notice that Martha’s complaint was really against Jesus Himself: ‘Don’t you care?’ When we are stressed and busy, we sometimes start to feel that God doesn’t care.

Jesus answered with love, saying her name twice: ‘Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things, but few things are needed, or indeed only one. Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.’
Jesus didn’t say serving was wrong. He said that time with Him comes first. Serving from a heart full of His presence is joyful. Serving from an empty, anxious heart leads to resentment.
Later, John tells us that Martha served at another dinner for Jesus, this time without complaint, while Mary poured expensive perfume on Jesus’ feet. Both sisters grew in their love for Jesus.
Are you more like Martha or Mary? Busy days come for everyone. But the ‘one thing needed’ is still time at Jesus’ feet.

verse.text: Come near to God and He will come near to you.

lessons: Time with Jesus comes before work for Jesus.
Being busy and stressed can make us feel God doesn’t care.
Jesus welcomes everyone as His disciple.
questions: What was good about Martha’s actions? What went wrong?
What did it mean that Mary sat at Jesus’ feet?
What things distract you from spending time with Jesus?
en.listen: Sit quietly, imagining yourself at Jesus’ feet like Mary. Ask Him: ‘What do you want to say to me today?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, I want to choose the better thing: time with you.
I am worried about…
Help me to serve from a heart full of your presence.

mission.text: This week, give Jesus your first five minutes after waking up, before screens or chores.

en.journal: Make two lists: ‘Things that make me a Martha’ and ‘Ways I can be a Mary’. Circle one thing you will change this week.

af.title: Afgelei of Toegewy?
story: Marta het haar huis vir Jesus oopgemaak. Dit was vrygewig en dapper, want Jesus het met ’n groot groep dissipels gereis, en om hulle almal te ontvang, was baie werk. Marta het Jesus liefgehad en wou hê alles moet vir Hom perfek wees.

Haar suster Maria het iets ongewoons gedoen. Sy het ‘by die Here se voete gesit en geluister na wat Hy sê’. In daardie kultuur was om by ’n leermeester se voete te sit die plek van ’n dissipel, ’n leerling wat by ’n rabbi leer. Vroue het selde daardie plek gekry. Maar Jesus het Maria as sy dissipel verwelkom.

Intussen sê Lukas dat Marta ‘afgelei was deur al die voorbereidings wat gedoen moes word’. Hoe meer sy gewerk het, hoe meer gefrustreerd het sy geword, totdat sy uitgebars het: ‘Here, gee U nie om dat my suster my alleen al die werk laat doen nie? Sê vir haar om my te help!’
Let op dat Marta se klagte eintlik teen Jesus self was: ‘Gee U nie om nie?’ As ons gestres en besig is, begin ons soms voel dat God nie omgee nie.

Jesus het met liefde geantwoord en haar naam twee keer gesê: ‘Marta, Marta, jy is bekommerd en ontsteld oor baie dinge, maar min dinge is nodig, of eintlik net een. Maria het die beste deel gekies, en dit sal nie van haar weggeneem word nie.’

Jesus het nie gesê om te dien is verkeerd nie. Hy het gesê dat tyd saam met Hom eerste kom. Om te dien uit ’n hart vol van sy teenwoordigheid, is vol vreugde. Om te dien uit ’n leë, angstige hart, lei tot bitterheid.

Later vertel Johannes ons dat Marta by ’n ander ete vir Jesus bedien het, hierdie keer sonder om te kla, terwyl Maria duur parfuum op Jesus se voete uitgegooi het. Albei susters het gegroei in hulle liefde vir Jesus.
Is jy meer soos Marta of Maria? Besige dae kom vir almal. Maar die ‘een ding wat nodig is’, is steeds tyd by Jesus se voete.

verse.text: Kom naby God, en Hy sal naby julle kom.

lessons: Tyd saam met Jesus kom voor werk vir Jesus.
Om besig en gestres te wees, kan ons laat voel dat God nie omgee nie.
Jesus verwelkom almal as sy dissipels.
questions: Wat was goed aan Marta se dade? Wat het skeefgeloop?
Wat het dit beteken dat Maria by Jesus se voete gesit het?
Watter dinge lei jou af om tyd saam met Jesus deur te bring?
af.listen: Sit stil, en stel jou voor jy sit soos Maria by Jesus se voete. Vra Hom: ‘Wat wil U vandag vir my sê?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, ek wil die beste deel kies: tyd saam met U.
Ek is bekommerd oor…
Help my om te dien uit ’n hart vol van u teenwoordigheid.

mission.text: Gee hierdie week jou eerste vyf minute nadat jy wakker word vir Jesus, voor skerms of take.

af.journal: Maak twee lyste: ‘Dinge wat my ’n Marta maak’ en ‘Maniere waarop ek ’n Maria kan wees’. Omkring een ding wat jy hierdie week sal verander.

en.title: The One Thing Needed
story: Luke places the story of Mary and Martha immediately after the parable of the Good Samaritan, and that is no accident. The Samaritan story teaches us to love our neighbour through action. The Bethany story teaches us to love God through attention. Together they answer the lawyer’s question about the greatest commandment: love God, and love your neighbour.

Martha does a good thing. She welcomes Jesus into her home, which was costly hospitality. But Luke uses a telling word: she was ‘distracted’ (literally ‘pulled in many directions’) by all the serving. Her activity for Jesus was pulling her away from Jesus.

Mary, meanwhile, takes the posture of a disciple. ‘Sitting at the feet’ of a rabbi was a technical phrase for being trained by him (Paul says he was brought up ‘at the feet of Gamaliel’). In a culture where women were generally excluded from formal religious instruction, Mary steps into a space reserved for men, and Jesus defends her right to be there.

Martha’s frustration boils over, and she even accuses Jesus: ‘Lord, don’t you care?’ Resentment often grows when we serve God without being nourished by Him. Jesus’ reply is tender, not harsh. The repeated name, ‘Martha, Martha’, is a sign of affection. He diagnoses her condition: ‘worried and upset about many things’. And He offers the cure: ‘only one thing is needed’.

What is that one thing? Being with Jesus. Listening to His word. Receiving from Him before we give to others. It isn’t passivity. Mary would later anoint Jesus extravagantly. Devotion leads to action, but action without devotion leads to burnout.

This matters especially in a busy, noisy world. Schoolwork, sport, activities, friends and screens can pull us in many directions. Even good things, including church activities, can crowd out the one thing needed. The question isn’t whether we serve, but whether our serving flows from time at His feet.
Jesus promises that what Mary chose ‘will not be taken away from her’. Achievements fade and activities end. Time with Jesus has eternal value.

verse.text: Few things are needed, or indeed only one. Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.

lessons: We love God through attention as well as action.
Activity for Jesus can pull us away from Jesus.
Devotion leads to healthy action; action without devotion leads to burnout.
questions: How do the Good Samaritan and the Mary and Martha stories fit together?
Why was it significant that Jesus welcomed Mary as a disciple?
What pulls you ‘in many directions’? What would it look like to choose the one thing needed?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Sit at Jesus’ feet in your imagination. Ask: ‘What are you saying to me today?’ Write it down, and also note any worries He is inviting you to let go of.
prayer: Jesus, I am often worried and upset about many things, like…
Today I choose the one thing needed: time with you.
Let my serving flow from being with you.

mission.text: This week, plan a daily ‘Mary time’ of at least ten minutes with Jesus, and protect it like an important appointment.

en.journal: Track how you spend one day this week. Afterwards, write honestly about where Jesus fits in, and what you want to change.

af.title: Die Een Ding wat Nodig Is
story: Lukas plaas die storie van Maria en Marta direk ná die gelykenis van die Barmhartige Samaritaan, en dit is nie toevallig nie. Die Samaritaan-storie leer ons om ons naaste deur dade lief te hê. Die Betanië-storie leer ons om God deur aandag lief te hê. Saam beantwoord hulle die wetsgeleerde se vraag oor die grootste gebod: het God lief, en het jou naaste lief.

Marta doen ’n goeie ding. Sy verwelkom Jesus in haar huis, wat duur gasvryheid was. Maar Lukas gebruik ’n veelseggende woord: sy was ‘afgelei’ (letterlik ‘in baie rigtings getrek’) deur al die bediening. Haar bedrywighede vir Jesus het haar van Jesus af weggetrek.

Maria, intussen, neem die houding van ’n dissipel in. ‘By die voete sit’ van ’n rabbi was ’n tegniese uitdrukking daarvoor om deur hom opgelei te word (Paulus sê hy is grootgemaak ‘aan die voete van Gamaliël’). In ’n kultuur waar vroue oor die algemeen van formele godsdienstige onderrig uitgesluit is, stap Maria in ’n ruimte wat vir mans bedoel was, en Jesus verdedig haar reg om daar te wees.

Marta se frustrasie kook oor, en sy beskuldig selfs vir Jesus: ‘Here, gee U nie om nie?’ Bitterheid groei dikwels wanneer ons God dien sonder om deur Hom gevoed te word. Jesus se antwoord is teer, nie hard nie. Die herhaalde naam, ‘Marta, Marta’, is ’n teken van liefde. Hy diagnoseer haar toestand: ‘bekommerd en ontsteld oor baie dinge’. En Hy bied die genesing: ‘net een ding is nodig’.

Wat is daardie een ding? Om by Jesus te wees. Om na sy woord te luister. Om van Hom te ontvang voordat ons aan ander gee. Dit is nie passiwiteit nie. Maria sou later Jesus kwistig salf. Toewyding lei tot dade, maar dade sonder toewyding lei tot uitbranding.

Dit maak veral saak in ’n besige, lawaaierige wêreld. Skoolwerk, sport, aktiwiteite, maats en skerms kan ons in baie rigtings trek. Selfs goeie dinge, ook kerkaktiwiteite, kan die een ding wat nodig is, uitdruk. Die vraag is nie of ons dien nie, maar of ons diens uit tyd by sy voete vloei.
Jesus belowe dat wat Maria gekies het, ‘nie van haar weggeneem sal word nie’. Prestasies vervaag en aktiwiteite eindig. Tyd saam met Jesus het ewige waarde.

verse.text: Min dinge is nodig, of eintlik net een. Maria het die beste deel gekies, en dit sal nie van haar weggeneem word nie.

lessons: Ons het God lief deur aandag sowel as dade.
Bedrywighede vir Jesus kan ons van Jesus af wegtrek.
Toewyding lei tot gesonde dade; dade sonder toewyding lei tot uitbranding.
questions: Hoe pas die Barmhartige Samaritaan en die Maria-en-Marta-stories inmekaar?
Hoekom was dit betekenisvol dat Jesus Maria as ’n dissipel verwelkom het?
Wat trek jou ‘in baie rigtings’? Hoe sou dit lyk om die een ding wat nodig is, te kies?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Sit in jou verbeelding by Jesus se voete. Vra: ‘Wat sê U vandag vir my?’ Skryf dit neer, en let ook op enige bekommernisse wat Hy jou nooi om te los.
prayer: Jesus, ek is dikwels bekommerd en ontsteld oor baie dinge, soos…
Vandag kies ek die een ding wat nodig is: tyd saam met U.
Laat my diens vloei uit om by U te wees.

mission.text: Beplan hierdie week ’n daaglikse ‘Maria-tyd’ van ten minste tien minute saam met Jesus, en beskerm dit soos ’n belangrike afspraak.

af.journal: Hou een dag hierdie week dop hoe jy jou tyd bestee. Skryf daarna eerlik oor waar Jesus inpas, en wat jy wil verander.

en.title: Sitting with Jesus
story: Jesus came to visit His friends Martha and Mary.
Martha was busy, busy, busy cooking and cleaning.
Mary sat down close to Jesus and listened to Him.
Jesus said, ‘Mary chose the best thing.’
Being with Jesus is the best!

verse.text: Come close to God, and He will come close to you.

en.action: Run around being ‘busy’, then stop, sit very still and whisper: ‘I’m with you, Jesus.’
lessons: Being with Jesus is the best thing.
questions: Can you sit very still for Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
I love being with you. Amen.

af.title: By Jesus Sit
story: Jesus het by sy vriendinne Marta en Maria kom kuier.
Marta was besig, besig, besig met kook en skoonmaak.
Maria het naby Jesus gaan sit en na Hom geluister.
Jesus het gesê: ‘Maria het die beste ding gekies.’
Om by Jesus te wees, is die beste!

verse.text: Kom naby God, en Hy sal naby jou kom.

af.action: Hardloop rond en wees ‘besig’, gaan staan dan, sit baie stil en fluister: ‘Ek is by U, Jesus.’
lessons: Om by Jesus te wees, is die beste ding.
questions: Kan jy baie stil sit vir Jesus?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
ek is lief daarvoor om by U te wees. Amen.

en.title: Martha, Mary and the Best Thing
story: Jesus had two good friends, sisters called Martha and Mary. They lived in a village called Bethany with their brother Lazarus. One day Jesus and His disciples came to visit.

Martha was so excited that she rushed off to get everything ready. There was bread to bake, food to cook, water to fetch and a table to set for all those guests! She hurried here and there, getting hotter and crosser.
But where was Mary? She was sitting on the floor at Jesus’ feet, listening to every word He said. She didn’t want to miss a thing!
Martha got cross. She marched up to Jesus and said, ‘Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do all the work? Tell her to help me!’
Jesus answered kindly, ‘Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things. But only one thing is really needed. Mary has chosen what is better, and it won’t be taken away from her.’
Jesus wasn’t saying that helping is bad. Helping is good! But being close to Jesus, listening to Him and enjoying Him is the most important thing of all.
Even on a busy day, you can stop and spend time with Jesus. He loves being with you.

verse.text: Come near to God and He will come near to you.

lessons: Being with Jesus matters most.
Jesus cares when I feel worried or upset.
Even on busy days, I can spend time with Jesus.
questions: What was Martha busy doing? What was Mary doing?
When is a good time for you to sit quietly with Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that you love being with me.
Help me to choose the best thing:
to spend time with you every day. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, choose a special ‘Mary moment’: sit quietly with Jesus for a few minutes and tell Him you love Him.

af.title: Marta, Maria en die Beste Ding
story: Jesus het twee goeie vriendinne gehad, susters met die name Marta en Maria. Hulle het in ’n dorpie met die naam Betanië gewoon saam met hulle broer Lasarus. Eendag het Jesus en sy dissipels kom kuier.

Marta was so opgewonde dat sy weggehardloop het om alles reg te kry. Daar was brood om te bak, kos om te kook, water om te skep en ’n tafel om te dek vir al daardie gaste! Sy het hiernatoe en daarnatoe gejaag, en al hoe warmer en kwater geword.
Maar waar was Maria? Sy het op die vloer by Jesus se voete gesit en na elke woord geluister wat Hy gesê het. Sy wou niks mis nie!
Marta het kwaad geword. Sy het na Jesus toe gestap en gesê: ‘Here, gee U nie om dat my suster my al die werk laat doen nie? Sê vir haar om my te help!’

Jesus het vriendelik geantwoord: ‘Marta, Marta, jy is bekommerd en ontsteld oor baie dinge. Maar net een ding is regtig nodig. Maria het die beste deel gekies, en dit sal nie van haar weggeneem word nie.’
Jesus het nie gesê helpe is sleg nie. Help is goed! Maar om naby Jesus te wees, na Hom te luister en Hom te geniet, is die belangrikste van alles.
Selfs op ’n besige dag kan jy stilstaan en tyd saam met Jesus deurbring. Hy is lief daarvoor om by jou te wees.

verse.text: Kom naby God, en Hy sal naby julle kom.

lessons: Om by Jesus te wees, is die belangrikste.
Jesus gee om as ek bekommerd of ontsteld voel.
Selfs op besige dae kan ek tyd saam met Jesus deurbring.
questions: Waarmee was Marta besig? Wat het Maria gedoen?
Wanneer is ’n goeie tyd vir jou om stil by Jesus te sit?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U daarvan hou om by my te wees.
Help my om die beste ding te kies:
om elke dag tyd saam met U deur te bring. Amen.

mission.text: Kies môre ’n spesiale ‘Maria-oomblik’: sit vir ’n paar minute stil by Jesus en sê vir Hom jy het Hom lief.

en.journal: Draw Mary sitting at Jesus’ feet. Write: ‘Being with Jesus is the best thing.’

af.fact: In Bybeltye het leerlinge by hulle onderwyser se voete gesit om te leer. Meisies is gewoonlik nie toegelaat om dit te doen nie, maar Jesus het Maria as sy leerling verwelkom!
af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy het Marta so kwaad geword?
af.journal: Teken Maria wat by Jesus se voete sit. Skryf: ‘Om by Jesus te wees, is die beste ding.’

trait.en: Jesus is the resurrection and the life
trait.af: Jesus is die opstanding en die lewe

en.title: I Am the Resurrection
story: When Lazarus fell ill, his sisters sent Jesus a simple message: ‘Lord, the one you love is sick.’ They didn’t tell Him what to do. They trusted His love.

John then writes something surprising: ‘Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. So when He heard that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was two more days.’ Because He loved them, He waited. Jesus knew He was about to do something far greater than a healing.

By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days. Martha met Him on the road: ‘Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But I know that even now God will give you whatever you ask.’

Jesus told her, ‘Your brother will rise again.’ Martha thought He meant at the end of time. Then Jesus said one of the greatest things ever spoken: ‘I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die; and whoever lives by believing in me will never die. Do you believe this?’ Martha answered, ‘Yes, Lord. I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God.’

When Mary came and fell at His feet weeping, and Jesus saw everyone crying, He was ‘deeply moved in spirit and troubled’. And then: ‘Jesus wept.’ The Son of God, who knew He would raise Lazarus in minutes, still cried with His friends. He doesn’t skip past our pain.

At the tomb Jesus said, ‘Take away the stone.’ Martha objected that there would be a bad smell. Jesus replied, ‘Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?’ He prayed aloud, then shouted, ‘Lazarus, come out!’ And the dead man came out, his hands and feet wrapped in strips of linen.
This sign pointed to something even bigger. A few weeks later, Jesus Himself would die and rise again, never to die again. Because He lives, all who believe in Him will live forever.

verse.text: I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die.

lessons: Jesus’ delays come from love, not from a lack of care.
Jesus weeps with us in our sorrow.
Jesus is the resurrection and the life; death is not the end for those who believe.
questions: Why do you think Jesus waited two days?
What does ‘Jesus wept’ tell you about Him?
How would you answer Jesus’ question to Martha: ‘Do you believe this?’
en.listen: Be still and bring Jesus any sadness you are carrying. Picture Him weeping with you. Then ask: ‘What hope do you want to give me?’ Write it down.
prayer: Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life.
Thank you that you understand my sadness about…
I believe that you are the Son of God.

mission.text: This week, be with someone who is sad. You don’t need the right words; just be kind and present, like Jesus.

en.journal: Write Jesus’ question, ‘Do you believe this?’, and write your own honest answer.

af.title: Ek Is die Opstanding
story: Toe Lasarus siek geword het, het sy susters vir Jesus ’n eenvoudige boodskap gestuur: ‘Here, die een vir wie U lief is, is siek.’ Hulle het Hom nie gesê wat om te doen nie. Hulle het sy liefde vertrou.

Johannes skryf dan iets verrassends: ‘Jesus het Marta en haar suster en Lasarus liefgehad. Toe Hy dus hoor dat Lasarus siek is, het Hy nog twee dae gebly waar Hy was.’ Omdat Hy hulle liefgehad het, het Hy gewag. Jesus het geweet Hy gaan iets baie groter as ’n genesing doen.

Teen die tyd dat Jesus aangekom het, was Lasarus al vier dae in die graf. Marta het Hom op die pad ontmoet: ‘Here, as U hier was, sou my broer nie gesterf het nie. Maar ek weet dat God U selfs nou sal gee wat U ook al vra.’

Jesus het vir haar gesê: ‘Jou broer sal opstaan.’ Marta het gedink Hy bedoel aan die einde van die tyd. Toe sê Jesus een van die grootste dinge wat nog ooit gesê is: ‘Ek is die opstanding en die lewe. Wie in My glo, sal lewe, al sterf hy ook; en elkeen wat lewe en in My glo, sal nooit sterf nie. Glo jy dit?’ Marta het geantwoord: ‘Ja, Here. Ek glo dat U die Messias is, die Seun van God.’

Toe Maria kom en huilend voor sy voete neerval, en Jesus almal sien huil, was Hy ‘diep in sy gees bewoë en ontroer’. En toe: ‘Jesus het gehuil.’ Die Seun van God, wat geweet het Hy sou Lasarus binne minute opwek, het steeds saam met sy vriende gehuil. Hy spring nie verby ons pyn nie.

By die graf het Jesus gesê: ‘Rol die klip weg.’ Marta het beswaar gemaak dat daar ’n slegte reuk sou wees. Jesus het geantwoord: ‘Het Ek jou nie gesê dat as jy glo, jy die heerlikheid van God sal sien nie?’ Hy het hardop gebid, en toe geroep: ‘Lasarus, kom uit!’ En die dooie man het uitgekom, sy hande en voete toegedraai met repe linne.
Hierdie teken het na iets nog groters gewys. ’n Paar weke later sou Jesus self sterf en weer opstaan, om nooit weer te sterf nie. Omdat Hy lewe, sal almal wat in Hom glo, vir altyd lewe.

verse.text: Ek is die opstanding en die lewe. Wie in My glo, sal lewe, al sterf hy ook.

lessons: Jesus se vertragings kom uit liefde, nie omdat Hy nie omgee nie.
Jesus huil saam met ons in ons hartseer.
Jesus is die opstanding en die lewe; die dood is nie die einde vir die wat glo nie.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Jesus twee dae gewag?
Wat vertel ‘Jesus het gehuil’ jou van Hom?
Hoe sou jy Jesus se vraag aan Marta beantwoord: ‘Glo jy dit?’
af.listen: Wees stil en bring vir Jesus enige hartseer wat jy dra. Sien in jou gedagtes hoe Hy saam met jou huil. Vra dan: ‘Watter hoop wil U my gee?’ Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Jesus, U is die opstanding en die lewe.
Dankie dat U my hartseer oor… verstaan.
Ek glo dat U die Seun van God is.

mission.text: Wees hierdie week by iemand wat hartseer is. Jy hoef nie die regte woorde te hê nie; wees net gaaf en daar, soos Jesus.

af.journal: Skryf Jesus se vraag, ‘Glo jy dit?’, en skryf jou eie eerlike antwoord.

en.title: The Seventh Sign
story: The raising of Lazarus is the seventh and greatest sign in John’s Gospel, and the turning point of the story. It shows Jesus’ power over death most dramatically, and it leads directly to the plot to kill Him.

The chapter begins with a puzzle. Jesus loves this family, yet when He hears Lazarus is sick, He deliberately stays away for two days. By the time He arrives, Lazarus has been dead four days. Some Jewish traditions held that the soul lingered near the body for three days; by the fourth, death was considered final. Jesus waited until there could be no doubt.

His conversations with the two sisters are different. With Martha, the practical one, He talks theology. She has solid faith in a future resurrection, but Jesus brings it into the present: ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’ Resurrection isn’t only an event at the end of history. It is a Person, and He is standing in front of her. Her confession, ‘You are the Messiah, the Son of God, who is to come into the world’, is one of the strongest in the Gospels.

With Mary, who says the same words through tears, Jesus doesn’t debate. He weeps. John uses a strong word for Jesus’ emotion: He was ‘deeply moved’, a word that can include indignation. Jesus is not only sad; He is angry at death itself, the enemy that tears families apart. Then He goes to confront it.

At the tomb, His prayer is said aloud ‘for the benefit of the people standing here, that they may believe that you sent me’. Then, ‘in a loud voice’: ‘Lazarus, come out!’ Someone once noted that if Jesus hadn’t used Lazarus’ name, every grave might have opened! The One who spoke creation into being speaks, and the dead obey.

Lazarus would eventually die again. This was a resuscitation, a return to ordinary life. But it pointed to the resurrection, Jesus’ own rising to a new, indestructible life. Because of His victory, Paul can write, ‘Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?’
Ironically, giving life to Lazarus would cost Jesus His own life. From that day the leaders plotted to kill Him. He gave life to others at the cost of His own, just as He would at the cross.

verse.text: Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?… Thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

lessons: Jesus is the resurrection and the life, here and now, not only at the end.
Jesus weeps with us and is angry at death, our enemy.
Jesus gave life to others at the cost of His own.
questions: Why do you think Jesus responded differently to Martha and to Mary?
What is the difference between Lazarus’ resuscitation and Jesus’ resurrection?
How does Jesus’ victory over death change the way you think about the future?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Read John 11:25–26 slowly. Ask Jesus: ‘What does it mean for my life now that you are the resurrection and the life?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life.
Thank you that you weep with me and are angry at what hurts me, like…
Thank you for giving your life so that I can live forever.

mission.text: This week, read 1 Corinthians 15:50–58 and share one verse of hope with someone who is grieving or afraid.

en.journal: Write about how Christian hope is different from wishful thinking. What makes our hope sure?

af.title: Die Sewende Teken
story: Die opwekking van Lasarus is die sewende en grootste teken in Johannes se Evangelie, en die keerpunt van die storie. Dit wys Jesus se mag oor die dood op die mees dramatiese manier, en dit lei direk tot die sameswering om Hom dood te maak.

Die hoofstuk begin met ’n raaisel. Jesus het hierdie familie lief, tog bly Hy doelbewus twee dae weg toe Hy hoor Lasarus is siek. Teen die tyd dat Hy aankom, is Lasarus al vier dae dood. Party Joodse tradisies het geglo dat die siel drie dae lank naby die liggaam bly; teen die vierde dag is die dood as finaal beskou. Jesus het gewag totdat daar geen twyfel kon wees nie.

Sy gesprekke met die twee susters is verskillend. Met Marta, die praktiese een, praat Hy teologie. Sy het ’n sterk geloof in ’n toekomstige opstanding, maar Jesus bring dit na die hede: ‘Ek is die opstanding en die lewe.’ Opstanding is nie net ’n gebeurtenis aan die einde van die geskiedenis nie. Dit is ’n Persoon, en Hy staan voor haar. Haar belydenis, ‘U is die Messias, die Seun van God, wat na die wêreld sou kom’, is een van die sterkstes in die Evangelies.

Met Maria, wat dieselfde woorde deur trane sê, debatteer Jesus nie. Hy huil. Johannes gebruik ’n sterk woord vir Jesus se emosie: Hy was ‘diep bewoë’, ’n woord wat verontwaardiging kan insluit. Jesus is nie net hartseer nie; Hy is kwaad vir die dood self, die vyand wat families uitmekaar skeur. Dan gaan Hy om dit te konfronteer.

By die graf word sy gebed hardop gebid ‘ter wille van die mense wat hier staan, sodat hulle kan glo dat U My gestuur het’. Dan, ‘met ’n harde stem’: ‘Lasarus, kom uit!’ Iemand het eens opgemerk dat as Jesus nie Lasarus se naam gebruik het nie, elke graf dalk oopgegaan het! Die Een wat die skepping tot stand gespreek het, spreek, en die dooies gehoorsaam.

Lasarus sou uiteindelik weer sterf. Dit was ’n terugkeer na die gewone lewe. Maar dit het gewys na die opstanding, Jesus se eie opstaan tot ’n nuwe, onvernietigbare lewe. Weens sy oorwinning kan Paulus skryf: ‘Dood, waar is jou oorwinning? Dood, waar is jou angel?’

Ironies genoeg sou die lewe wat Hy aan Lasarus gegee het, Jesus sy eie lewe kos. Van daardie dag af het die leiers beplan om Hom dood te maak. Hy het lewe aan ander gegee ten koste van sy eie, net soos Hy by die kruis sou doen.

verse.text: Dood, waar is jou oorwinning? Dood, waar is jou angel?… Maar God sy dank! Hy gee ons die oorwinning deur ons Here Jesus Christus.

lessons: Jesus is die opstanding en die lewe, hier en nou, nie net aan die einde nie.
Jesus huil saam met ons en is kwaad vir die dood, ons vyand.
Jesus het lewe aan ander gegee ten koste van sy eie.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Jesus verskillend op Marta en op Maria gereageer?
Wat is die verskil tussen Lasarus se terugkeer na die lewe en Jesus se opstanding?
Hoe verander Jesus se oorwinning oor die dood die manier waarop jy oor die toekoms dink?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Lees Johannes 11:25–26 stadig. Vra Jesus: ‘Wat beteken dit vir my lewe nou dat U die opstanding en die lewe is?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, U is die opstanding en die lewe.
Dankie dat U saam met my huil en kwaad is vir wat my seermaak, soos…
Dankie dat U u lewe gegee het sodat ek vir altyd kan lewe.

mission.text: Lees hierdie week 1 Korintiërs 15:50–58 en deel een vers van hoop met iemand wat treur of bang is.

af.journal: Skryf oor hoe Christelike hoop verskil van wensdenkery. Wat maak ons hoop seker?

en.title: Lazarus, Come Out!
story: Jesus’ friend Lazarus got sick and died.
Mary and Martha were very sad. Jesus cried with them.
Then Jesus went to the tomb and called, ‘Lazarus, come out!’
And out came Lazarus, alive!
Jesus is stronger than everything!

verse.text: Jesus said, ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’

en.action: Wrap yourself in a blanket like Lazarus, then jump out when someone says: ‘Come out!’
lessons: Jesus is stronger than everything.
questions: Can you jump out like Lazarus?
prayer: Thank you, Jesus,
you are so strong and you give life. Amen.

af.title: Lasarus, Kom Uit!
story: Jesus se vriend Lasarus het siek geword en gesterf.
Maria en Marta was baie hartseer. Jesus het saam met hulle gehuil.
Toe het Jesus na die graf gegaan en geroep: ‘Lasarus, kom uit!’
En Lasarus het uitgekom, lewendig!
Jesus is sterker as alles!

verse.text: Jesus het gesê: ‘Ek is die opstanding en die lewe.’

af.action: Draai jouself in ’n kombers toe soos Lasarus, en spring dan uit as iemand sê: ‘Kom uit!’
lessons: Jesus is sterker as alles.
questions: Kan jy uitspring soos Lasarus?
prayer: Dankie, Jesus,
U is so sterk en U gee lewe. Amen.

en.title: Jesus Wept, Then Jesus Called
story: Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, was one of Jesus’ good friends. One day Lazarus became very sick. His sisters sent a message to Jesus: ‘Lord, the one you love is sick.’
Jesus loved Lazarus and his sisters very much. But He waited two more days before He went. By the time He arrived in Bethany, Lazarus had died and had been in the tomb for four days.

Martha ran to meet Jesus. ‘Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.’ Jesus said to her, ‘I am the resurrection and the life. Anyone who believes in me will live, even though they die. Do you believe this?’ Martha said, ‘Yes, Lord, I believe you are the Son of God.’
When Jesus saw Mary and all their friends crying, He felt very sad too. And Jesus wept. Even though He knew what He was about to do, He cried with His friends.
Then Jesus went to the tomb, a cave with a big stone across the door. ‘Take away the stone,’ He said. Then He prayed and called in a loud voice, ‘Lazarus, come out!’
And out came Lazarus, still wrapped in the strips of cloth people used for burying! ‘Take off the cloths and let him go,’ said Jesus. What a happy day!
Jesus is sad when we are sad. And Jesus is stronger than death. He promises that everyone who believes in Him will live forever.

verse.text: I am the resurrection and the life. Anyone who believes in me will live.

lessons: Jesus is the resurrection and the life.
Jesus feels sad with us when we are sad.
Jesus is stronger than death.
questions: How did Jesus feel when He saw His friends crying?
What does it mean that Jesus is ‘the resurrection and the life’?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that you understand when I’m sad.
Thank you that you are stronger than death
and give life forever to those who believe in you. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, if someone is sad, sit with them and be kind, just like Jesus did.

af.title: Jesus het Gehuil, Toe het Jesus Geroep
story: Lasarus, die broer van Maria en Marta, was een van Jesus se goeie vriende. Eendag het Lasarus baie siek geword. Sy susters het ’n boodskap na Jesus gestuur: ‘Here, die een vir wie U lief is, is siek.’
Jesus was baie lief vir Lasarus en sy susters. Maar Hy het nog twee dae gewag voordat Hy gegaan het. Teen die tyd dat Hy in Betanië aangekom het, was Lasarus dood en al vier dae in die graf.

Marta het gehardloop om Jesus te ontmoet. ‘Here, as U hier was, sou my broer nie gesterf het nie.’ Jesus het vir haar gesê: ‘Ek is die opstanding en die lewe. Wie in My glo, sal lewe, al sterf hy ook. Glo jy dit?’ Marta het gesê: ‘Ja, Here, ek glo U is die Seun van God.’
Toe Jesus Maria en al hulle vriende sien huil, het Hy ook baie hartseer gevoel. En Jesus het gehuil. Al het Hy geweet wat Hy gaan doen, het Hy saam met sy vriende gehuil.
Toe het Jesus na die graf gegaan, ’n grot met ’n groot klip voor die deur. ‘Rol die klip weg,’ het Hy gesê. Toe het Hy gebid en hard geroep: ‘Lasarus, kom uit!’
En Lasarus het uitgekom, nog toegedraai in die repe lap wat mense gebruik het om te begrawe! ‘Haal die lappe af en laat hom gaan,’ het Jesus gesê. Wat ’n blye dag!
Jesus is hartseer as ons hartseer is. En Jesus is sterker as die dood. Hy belowe dat almal wat in Hom glo, vir altyd sal lewe.

verse.text: Ek is die opstanding en die lewe. Wie in My glo, sal lewe.

lessons: Jesus is die opstanding en die lewe.
Jesus voel hartseer saam met ons as ons hartseer is.
Jesus is sterker as die dood.
questions: Hoe het Jesus gevoel toe Hy sy vriende sien huil?
Wat beteken dit dat Jesus ‘die opstanding en die lewe’ is?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U verstaan as ek hartseer is.
Dankie dat U sterker is as die dood
en vir altyd lewe gee aan die wat in U glo. Amen.

mission.text: As iemand môre hartseer is, sit by hulle en wees gaaf, net soos Jesus gedoen het.
