af.deeper: Hoekom dink jy het Jesus gehuil, al het Hy geweet Hy gaan Lasarus weer lewendig maak?
af.journal: Teken die graf met die klip weggerol. Skryf Jesus se woorde: ‘Lasarus, kom uit!’

trait.en: Jesus serves, and teaches me to serve
trait.af: Jesus dien, en leer my om te dien

en.title: The Towel and the Basin
story: John begins this scene with a beautiful sentence: ‘Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the end.’ Jesus knew that in a few hours He would be arrested. He knew that Judas would betray Him and Peter would deny Him. And with all that ahead, He chose to spend His last evening showing His friends how much He loved them.

In that culture, roads were dusty and people wore sandals, so feet got filthy. Washing guests’ feet was the job of the lowest servant. Earlier that evening, according to Luke, the disciples had been arguing about which of them was the greatest. None of them was going to volunteer for the lowest job.

So Jesus did. He ‘got up from the meal, took off His outer clothing, and wrapped a towel around His waist. After that, He poured water into a basin and began to wash His disciples’ feet.’ The hands that had healed the sick, calmed storms and would soon be nailed to a cross scrubbed the dirt from their feet.

Peter protested: ‘You shall never wash my feet!’ He couldn’t accept his Lord serving him. Jesus said, ‘Unless I wash you, you have no part with me.’ We first need to let Jesus serve us, by cleansing us from sin, before we can truly serve others.
Jesus even washed the feet of Judas, who He knew would betray Him that night.

Afterwards Jesus said, ‘Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet. I have set you an example.’ And later that evening He added: ‘A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples.’
Greatness in God’s kingdom isn’t about being served. It is about serving, even in jobs no one else wants and even for people who might hurt us.

verse.text: As I have loved you, so you must love one another.

lessons: Jesus, the King of kings, chose to serve.
We first need to let Jesus serve us by cleansing us.
Greatness in God’s kingdom means serving others with love.
questions: Why didn’t any of the disciples offer to wash feet?
Why was it hard for Peter to let Jesus wash his feet?
What does it mean that Jesus washed Judas’ feet too?
en.listen: Be still and ask Jesus: ‘Who do you want me to serve this week, and how?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for loving me to the end.
Thank you for washing me clean.
Help me to serve… with love, even if nobody notices.

mission.text: This week, do the job nobody wants (at home, at school or in a group) without being asked and without telling anyone.

en.journal: Write about what ‘greatness’ means in the world and what it means in God’s kingdom. How are they different?

af.title: Die Handdoek en die Skottel
story: Johannes begin hierdie toneel met ’n pragtige sin: ‘Hy het sy eie mense in die wêreld liefgehad, en Hy het hulle tot die einde toe liefgehad.’ Jesus het geweet dat Hy oor ’n paar uur gevange geneem sou word. Hy het geweet dat Judas Hom sou verraai en Petrus Hom sou verloën. En met dit alles voor Hom, het Hy gekies om sy laaste aand te gebruik om sy vriende te wys hoe lief Hy hulle het.

In daardie kultuur was paaie stowwerig en het mense sandale gedra, so voete het vieslik vuil geword. Om gaste se voete te was, was die werk van die laagste bediende. Vroeër daardie aand, volgens Lukas, het die dissipels gestry oor wie van hulle die grootste is. Nie een van hulle sou aanbied om die laagste werk te doen nie.

Toe doen Jesus dit. Hy ‘het van die ete af opgestaan, sy boklere uitgetrek en ’n handdoek om sy middel vasgemaak. Daarna het Hy water in ’n skottel gegooi en begin om sy dissipels se voete te was.’ Die hande wat siekes genees het, storms stilgemaak het en binnekort aan ’n kruis vasgespyker sou word, het die vuilgoed van hulle voete afgeskrop.

Petrus het beswaar gemaak: ‘U sal nooit my voete was nie!’ Hy kon nie aanvaar dat sy Here hom bedien nie. Jesus het gesê: ‘As Ek jou nie was nie, het jy geen deel aan My nie.’ Ons moet eers vir Jesus toelaat om ons te dien, deur ons van sonde te reinig, voordat ons ander regtig kan dien.
Jesus het selfs die voete van Judas gewas, wat Hy geweet het Hom daardie nag sou verraai.

Daarna het Jesus gesê: ‘Noudat Ek, julle Here en Leermeester, julle voete gewas het, moet julle ook mekaar se voete was. Ek het vir julle ’n voorbeeld gegee.’ En later daardie aand het Hy bygevoeg: ‘Ek gee julle ’n nuwe gebod: Julle moet mekaar liefhê. Soos Ek julle liefgehad het, moet julle mekaar liefhê. Daaraan sal almal weet dat julle my dissipels is.’
Grootheid in God se koninkryk gaan nie daaroor om bedien te word nie. Dit gaan oor om te dien, selfs in werk wat niemand anders wil doen nie en selfs vir mense wat ons dalk kan seermaak.

verse.text: Soos Ek julle liefgehad het, moet julle mekaar liefhê.

lessons: Jesus, die Koning van die konings, het gekies om te dien.
Ons moet eers vir Jesus toelaat om ons te dien deur ons te reinig.
Grootheid in God se koninkryk beteken om ander in liefde te dien.
questions: Hoekom het nie een van die dissipels aangebied om voete te was nie?
Hoekom was dit vir Petrus moeilik om Jesus sy voete te laat was?
Wat beteken dit dat Jesus ook Judas se voete gewas het?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra Jesus: ‘Wie wil U hê moet ek hierdie week dien, en hoe?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U my tot die einde toe liefhet.
Dankie dat U my skoon was.
Help my om… in liefde te dien, selfs as niemand dit raaksien nie.

mission.text: Doen hierdie week die werk wat niemand wil doen nie (by die huis, by die skool of in ’n groep) sonder om gevra te word en sonder om vir enigiemand te vertel.

af.journal: Skryf oor wat ‘grootheid’ in die wêreld beteken en wat dit in God se koninkryk beteken. Hoe verskil hulle?

en.title: Love to the End
story: John 13 opens the second half of John’s Gospel, which focuses on Jesus’ final hours and His death and resurrection. The first verse sets the tone: ‘Jesus knew that the hour had come for Him to leave this world and go to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the end’, or ‘to the uttermost’.

Verse 3 is crucial: ‘Jesus knew that the Father had put all things under His power, and that He had come from God and was returning to God; so He got up from the meal… and wrapped a towel around His waist.’ Notice the ‘so’. Jesus washed feet not in spite of knowing who He was, but because He knew who He was. Secure people can serve. Those who are anxious about their status can’t afford to look small.

Each of Jesus’ actions mirrors something greater. He ‘took off His outer clothing’; Paul writes that Christ ‘made Himself nothing, taking the very nature of a servant’. He knelt to wash; Christ ‘humbled Himself by becoming obedient to death, even death on a cross’. Afterwards He ‘put on His clothes and returned to His place’; after the cross, God exalted Him to the highest place. The foot-washing is a living parable of the incarnation and the cross.

Peter’s objection reveals something about pride. He would rather serve Jesus than be served by Him. But Jesus insists: ‘Unless I wash you, you have no part with me.’ The gospel begins with receiving. We can’t earn a place with Jesus by our service; we receive cleansing as a gift. Then that grace overflows into service to others.

Jesus deliberately includes Judas. He knows exactly what Judas is about to do, yet He kneels and washes his feet too. Love that serves even the betrayer is love beyond ordinary human capacity. It is God’s love.

Then comes the ‘new command’: ‘As I have loved you, so you must love one another.’ The commandment to love wasn’t new; Leviticus already said, ‘Love your neighbour.’ What was new was the measure: ‘as I have loved you’. Self-giving, serving, cross-shaped love. And Jesus says this love will be the identifying mark of His followers: ‘By this everyone will know that you are my disciples.’

verse.text: In your relationships with one another, have the same mindset as Christ Jesus: who… made Himself nothing by taking the very nature of a servant.

lessons: Security in who we are in God frees us to serve.
The foot-washing is a picture of Jesus’ whole mission: humbling Himself to the cross.
We receive Jesus’ cleansing first; then His love overflows through us to others.
questions: How does knowing who He was free Jesus to serve? How might that apply to you?
How does the foot-washing mirror Philippians 2:5–11?
What makes Jesus’ command to love ‘new’?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Imagine Jesus kneeling to wash your feet. What do you feel? Then ask Him: ‘Whose feet do you want me to wash?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, you loved me to the uttermost.
I receive your cleansing for…
Give me a secure heart that is free to serve, even when it costs me.

mission.text: This week, serve someone you find difficult, in a practical, humble way.

en.journal: Write about pride. Where does it make it hard for you to receive help, or to serve others? What would change if you were secure in God’s love?

af.title: Liefde tot die Einde
story: Johannes 13 begin die tweede helfte van Johannes se Evangelie, wat fokus op Jesus se laaste ure en sy dood en opstanding. Die eerste vers stel die toon: ‘Jesus het geweet dat sy uur gekom het om uit hierdie wêreld na die Vader te gaan. Hy het sy eie mense in die wêreld liefgehad, en Hy het hulle tot die einde toe liefgehad’, of ‘ten volle’.

Vers 3 is deurslaggewend: ‘Jesus het geweet dat die Vader alles in sy hande gegee het, en dat Hy van God gekom het en na God teruggaan; daarom het Hy van die ete af opgestaan… en ’n handdoek om sy middel vasgemaak.’ Let op die ‘daarom’. Jesus het voete gewas nie ten spyte daarvan dat Hy geweet het wie Hy is nie, maar omdat Hy geweet het wie Hy is. Mense wat veilig is in wie hulle is, kan dien. Die wat angstig is oor hulle status, kan nie bekostig om klein te lyk nie.

Elkeen van Jesus se dade weerspieël iets groters. Hy het ‘sy boklere uitgetrek’; Paulus skryf dat Christus ‘Homself niks gemaak het deur die gestalte van ’n dienaar aan te neem’. Hy het gekniel om te was; Christus ‘het Homself verneder en gehoorsaam geword tot die dood, ja, tot die dood aan die kruis’. Daarna het Hy ‘sy klere aangetrek en teruggegaan na sy plek’; ná die kruis het God Hom tot die hoogste plek verhef. Die voetewassing is ’n lewende gelykenis van die menswording en die kruis.

Petrus se beswaar wys iets oor trots. Hy sal eerder Jesus dien as om deur Hom bedien te word. Maar Jesus hou vol: ‘As Ek jou nie was nie, het jy geen deel aan My nie.’ Die evangelie begin met ontvang. Ons kan nie ’n plek by Jesus verdien deur ons diens nie; ons ontvang reiniging as ’n geskenk. Dan loop daardie genade oor in diens aan ander.

Jesus sluit Judas doelbewus in. Hy weet presies wat Judas op die punt staan om te doen, tog kniel Hy en was ook sy voete. Liefde wat selfs die verraaier dien, is liefde verby gewone menslike vermoë. Dit is God se liefde.

Dan kom die ‘nuwe gebod’: ‘Soos Ek julle liefgehad het, moet julle mekaar liefhê.’ Die gebod om lief te hê was nie nuut nie; Levitikus het reeds gesê: ‘Jy moet jou naaste liefhê.’ Wat nuut was, was die maatstaf: ‘soos Ek julle liefgehad het’. Selfgewende, dienende, kruisvormige liefde. En Jesus sê hierdie liefde sal die kenmerk van sy volgelinge wees: ‘Daaraan sal almal weet dat julle my dissipels is.’

verse.text: Julle gesindheid teenoor mekaar moet dieselfde wees as dié van Christus Jesus: Hy… het Homself niks gemaak deur die gestalte van ’n dienaar aan te neem.

lessons: Om veilig te wees in wie ons in God is, maak ons vry om te dien.
Die voetewassing is ’n prentjie van Jesus se hele opdrag: Homself verneder tot by die kruis.
Ons ontvang eers Jesus se reiniging; dan loop sy liefde deur ons oor na ander.
questions: Hoe het om te weet wie Hy is, Jesus vry gemaak om te dien? Hoe kan dit op jou van toepassing wees?
Hoe weerspieël die voetewassing Filippense 2:5–11?
Wat maak Jesus se gebod om lief te hê ‘nuut’?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Stel jou voor Jesus kniel om jou voete te was. Wat voel jy? Vra Hom dan: ‘Wie se voete wil U hê moet ek was?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, U het my ten volle liefgehad.
Ek ontvang u reiniging vir…
Gee my ’n veilige hart wat vry is om te dien, selfs as dit my iets kos.

mission.text: Dien hierdie week iemand wat jy moeilik vind, op ’n praktiese, nederige manier.

af.journal: Skryf oor trots. Waar maak dit dit vir jou moeilik om hulp te ontvang, of om ander te dien? Wat sou verander as jy veilig was in God se liefde?

en.title: Jesus Helps
story: Jesus and His friends had dusty, dirty feet.
Jesus got a bowl of water and a towel.
He knelt down and washed His friends’ feet. Splish, splash!
Jesus said, ‘Help each other like I helped you.’
I can help others too!

verse.text: Serve one another with love.

en.action: Pretend to wash someone’s feet with a towel, then give them a big smile.
lessons: Jesus helps, and I can help too.
questions: Who can you help tomorrow?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
help me to help others. Amen.

af.title: Jesus Help
story: Jesus en sy vriende het stowwerige, vuil voete gehad.
Jesus het ’n skottel water en ’n handdoek gevat.
Hy het gekniel en sy vriende se voete gewas. Spat, spat!
Jesus het gesê: ‘Help mekaar soos Ek julle gehelp het.’
Ek kan ook ander help!

verse.text: Dien mekaar in liefde.

af.action: Maak of jy iemand se voete met ’n handdoek was, en gee hulle dan ’n groot glimlag.
lessons: Jesus help, en ek kan ook help.
questions: Wie kan jy môre help?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
help my om ander te help. Amen.

en.title: A Towel and a Basin
story: It was the night before Jesus died on the cross. He and His disciples were together for a special supper. Jesus knew it was His last meal with them, and He wanted to show them how much He loved them.

In those days people walked everywhere on dusty roads in sandals, so their feet got very dirty. Usually a servant washed the guests’ feet. But there was no servant at this supper, and none of the disciples wanted to do such a lowly job.

So Jesus got up from the table. He took off His outer robe, wrapped a towel around His waist and poured water into a basin. Then the King of kings knelt down and began to wash His disciples’ dirty feet, one by one, and dry them with the towel.
When Jesus came to Peter, Peter was shocked. ‘Lord, you will never wash my feet!’ But Jesus said, ‘Unless I wash you, you can’t be part of me.’ So Peter said, ‘Then wash my hands and my head too!’
When Jesus had finished, He sat down again and said, ‘I am your Lord and Teacher, and I have washed your feet. Now you should wash one another’s feet. I have given you an example to follow.’
Jesus is the greatest King of all, and He served others. He wants us to serve one another with love too, by helping, sharing and doing even the jobs nobody else wants to do.

verse.text: Serve one another humbly in love.

lessons: Jesus is a King who serves.
Jesus teaches me to serve others.
No job is too small when I do it with love.
questions: Why was Peter so shocked that Jesus wanted to wash his feet?
What is a job at home nobody wants to do that you could do with love?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you for being a King who serves.
Help me to serve others with love,
even when nobody is watching. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, secretly do a job at home that nobody wants to do, like tidying up shoes or wiping the table.

af.title: ’n Handdoek en ’n Skottel
story: Dit was die aand voordat Jesus aan die kruis gesterf het. Hy en sy dissipels was saam vir ’n spesiale aandete. Jesus het geweet dit was sy laaste ete saam met hulle, en Hy wou hulle wys hoe lief Hy hulle het.

In daardie dae het mense oral op stowwerige paaie in sandale geloop, so hulle voete het baie vuil geword. Gewoonlik het ’n bediende die gaste se voete gewas. Maar daar was geen bediende by hierdie ete nie, en nie een van die dissipels wou so ’n nederige werk doen nie.

Toe het Jesus van die tafel af opgestaan. Hy het sy boklere uitgetrek, ’n handdoek om sy middel gedraai en water in ’n skottel gegooi. Toe het die Koning van die konings gekniel en begin om sy dissipels se vuil voete een vir een te was, en met die handdoek af te droog.

Toe Jesus by Petrus kom, was Petrus geskok. ‘Here, U sal nooit my voete was nie!’ Maar Jesus het gesê: ‘As Ek jou nie was nie, kan jy nie deel van My wees nie.’ Toe sê Petrus: ‘Was dan my hande en my kop ook!’
Toe Jesus klaar was, het Hy weer gaan sit en gesê: ‘Ek is julle Here en Leermeester, en Ek het julle voete gewas. Nou moet julle mekaar se voete was. Ek het vir julle ’n voorbeeld gegee om te volg.’
Jesus is die grootste Koning van almal, en Hy het ander gedien. Hy wil hê ons moet mekaar ook in liefde dien, deur te help, te deel en selfs die werkies te doen wat niemand anders wil doen nie.

verse.text: Dien mekaar nederig in liefde.

lessons: Jesus is ’n Koning wat dien.
Jesus leer my om ander te dien.
Geen werk is te klein as ek dit met liefde doen nie.
questions: Hoekom was Petrus so geskok dat Jesus sy voete wou was?
Wat is ’n werkie by die huis wat niemand wil doen nie wat jy met liefde kan doen?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U ’n Koning is wat dien.
Help my om ander in liefde te dien,
selfs as niemand kyk nie. Amen.

mission.text: Doen môre in die geheim ’n werkie by die huis wat niemand wil doen nie, soos om skoene op te ruim of die tafel af te vee.

trait.en: I grow by staying close to Jesus
trait.af: Ek groei deur naby Jesus te bly

en.title: Remain in Me
story: On His last night, Jesus gave His disciples a picture they would never forget. Grapevines grew everywhere in Israel, and the vine was even a symbol of the nation. Jesus said, ‘I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener… I am the vine; you are the branches.’

Think about how a branch works. It doesn’t produce grapes by straining and trying harder. It simply stays connected to the vine, and the life of the vine (water, nutrients, sap) flows through it. Fruit grows naturally.

The key word in this passage is ‘remain’ (some Bibles say ‘abide’). Jesus uses it eleven times! ‘Remain in me, as I also remain in you. No branch can bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine. Neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in me.’

Then He says something humbling: ‘Apart from me you can do nothing.’ We can do lots of activities without Jesus, but nothing of eternal value. Real fruit, like love, joy, peace and changed lives, only grows through connection with Him.

Jesus also mentions pruning. A good gardener cuts back healthy branches so that they grow even more fruit. Sometimes God allows hard things or removes things from our lives, not to harm us, but to help us grow.

How do we remain in Jesus? Jesus Himself explains: through His words remaining in us (reading and remembering the Bible), through prayer (‘ask whatever you wish’), through obedience (‘If you keep my commands, you will remain in my love’) and through love for one another.

Notice that obedience flows from relationship. Jesus doesn’t say, ‘Obey me so that I will love you.’ He says, ‘As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Now remain in my love.’ We obey because we are loved, and we want to stay close.
And the result? ‘I have told you this so that my joy may be in you and that your joy may be complete.’

verse.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing.

lessons: Fruit grows by staying connected to Jesus, not by straining.
God sometimes prunes us so that we grow more.
Obedience flows from remaining in Jesus’ love, and leads to joy.
questions: How does a branch produce fruit? What does that teach us?
What are some ways we can ‘remain’ in Jesus?
What does ‘pruning’ look like in a person’s life?
en.listen: Be still and picture yourself as a branch connected to Jesus the vine. Ask: ‘Jesus, what do you want to grow in me?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, you are the vine and I am a branch.
I want to remain in you, especially when…
Grow your fruit in me, and fill me with your joy.

mission.text: This week, choose one verse from John 15 and read it every morning to ‘remain’ in Jesus’ words.

en.journal: Draw a vine with branches. On the vine, write ‘Jesus’. On the branches, write ways you stay connected. On the grapes, write fruit you hope to see.

af.title: Bly in My
story: Op sy laaste aand het Jesus sy dissipels ’n prentjie gegee wat hulle nooit sou vergeet nie. Wingerdstokke het oral in Israel gegroei, en die wingerdstok was selfs ’n simbool van die volk. Jesus het gesê: ‘Ek is die ware wingerdstok, en my Vader is die landbouer… Ek is die wingerdstok; julle is die lote.’

Dink aan hoe ’n loot werk. Dit dra nie druiwe deur te sukkel en harder te probeer nie. Dit bly net aan die stok verbind, en die lewe van die stok (water, voedingstowwe, sap) vloei daardeur. Vrugte groei natuurlik.

Die sleutelwoord in hierdie gedeelte is ‘bly’. Jesus gebruik dit elf keer! ‘Bly in My, soos Ek ook in julle bly. Geen loot kan op sy eie vrugte dra nie; dit moet aan die wingerdstok bly. Julle ook nie, tensy julle in My bly nie.’

Dan sê Hy iets wat ons nederig maak: ‘Sonder My kan julle niks doen nie.’ Ons kan baie bedrywighede sonder Jesus doen, maar niks van ewige waarde nie. Regte vrugte, soos liefde, vreugde, vrede en veranderde lewens, groei net deur verbinding met Hom.

Jesus noem ook snoei. ’n Goeie landbouer sny gesonde lote terug sodat hulle nog meer vrugte dra. Soms laat God moeilike dinge toe of verwyder Hy dinge uit ons lewe, nie om ons seer te maak nie, maar om ons te help groei.

Hoe bly ons in Jesus? Jesus self verduidelik: deur sy woorde wat in ons bly (die Bybel lees en onthou), deur gebed (‘vra wat julle wil’), deur gehoorsaamheid (‘As julle my gebooie gehoorsaam, sal julle in my liefde bly’) en deur liefde vir mekaar.

Let op dat gehoorsaamheid uit verhouding vloei. Jesus sê nie: ‘Gehoorsaam My sodat Ek julle sal liefhê nie.’ Hy sê: ‘Soos die Vader My liefgehad het, het Ek julle liefgehad. Bly nou in my liefde.’ Ons gehoorsaam omdat ons liefgehê word, en ons wil naby bly.
En die gevolg? ‘Ek het dit vir julle gesê sodat my blydskap in julle kan wees en julle blydskap volkome kan wees.’

verse.text: Ek is die wingerdstok; julle is die lote. Wie in My bly en Ek in hom, dra baie vrugte; sonder My kan julle niks doen nie.

lessons: Vrugte groei deur aan Jesus verbind te bly, nie deur te sukkel nie.
God snoei ons soms sodat ons meer groei.
Gehoorsaamheid vloei uit om in Jesus se liefde te bly, en lei tot vreugde.
questions: Hoe dra ’n loot vrugte? Wat leer dit ons?
Wat is party maniere waarop ons in Jesus kan ‘bly’?
Hoe lyk ‘snoei’ in ’n mens se lewe?
af.listen: Wees stil en sien jouself as ’n loot wat aan Jesus, die wingerdstok, verbind is. Vra: ‘Jesus, wat wil U in my laat groei?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, U is die wingerdstok en ek is ’n loot.
Ek wil in U bly, veral wanneer…
Laat u vrugte in my groei, en vul my met u vreugde.

mission.text: Kies hierdie week een vers uit Johannes 15 en lees dit elke oggend om in Jesus se woorde te ‘bly’.

af.journal: Teken ’n wingerdstok met lote. Skryf ‘Jesus’ op die stok. Skryf op die lote maniere waarop jy verbind bly. Skryf op die druiwe vrugte wat jy hoop om te sien.

en.title: Abiding, Not Striving
story: When Jesus said, ‘I am the true vine’, His disciples would have caught the reference. In the Old Testament, Israel was often pictured as God’s vine. Isaiah 5 contains a sad ‘song of the vineyard’: God planted a choice vine, cared for it, and ‘looked for a crop of good grapes, but it yielded only bad fruit’. Israel had failed to produce the justice and righteousness God desired.

So when Jesus calls Himself the ‘true vine’, He is claiming to be what Israel was meant to be, the faithful Son who bears the fruit God always wanted. And now people become part of God’s vine by being connected to Him.

The central command is ‘remain in me’ (‘abide’ in older translations), used eleven times in the passage. It is a relationship word. It describes ongoing, intimate, dependent connection. It isn’t a one-time decision but a daily way of life.

This is radically different from the way many people think about the Christian life. We often picture it as striving: trying harder to be good, to pray more and to do more. But branches don’t strive. They receive. Fruit is the natural result of connection, not the product of effort. That doesn’t mean we do nothing. Abiding takes intention. But our main focus is on staying close to Jesus, and fruit follows.
Jesus says ‘apart from me you can do nothing’. That doesn’t mean we can’t do anything; non-Christians accomplish many things. It means nothing of lasting, eternal fruit comes from our own resources.

Pruning is another important idea. The Father ‘prunes’ fruitful branches so that they become more fruitful. Pruning can be painful: disappointments, losses, the removal of things we were attached to. But in God’s hands, it isn’t punishment; it is preparation for greater fruitfulness.

Notice how love and obedience connect: ‘If you keep my commands, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commands and remain in His love.’ This isn’t earning love. Jesus’ obedience to the Father flowed from their love relationship, and so does ours. Then Jesus calls His disciples something astonishing: ‘I no longer call you servants… Instead, I have called you friends.’ Abiding means living as Jesus’ friend.

verse.text: As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Now remain in my love.

lessons: Jesus is the true vine, the faithful Son who bears the fruit God desired.
The Christian life is abiding, not striving: fruit flows from connection.
Obedience flows from love, and Jesus calls us His friends.
questions: How does Isaiah 5 help you understand Jesus’ claim to be the ‘true vine’?
What is the difference between abiding and striving? Which describes your faith more?
How have you experienced ‘pruning’, and what did God grow through it?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Don’t ask for anything; simply rest in Jesus’ love, as a branch rests in the vine. Then write down what you noticed.
prayer: Jesus, you are the true vine, and I want to remain in you.
Forgive me for striving in my own strength, especially in…
Thank you for calling me your friend.

mission.text: This week, practise ‘abiding’: start each day by sitting quietly with Jesus before asking Him for anything.

en.journal: Write a short essay: ‘What it means to be a branch.’ Include the vine, abiding, pruning, fruit and friendship.

af.title: Bly, Nie Sukkel Nie
story: Toe Jesus gesê het: ‘Ek is die ware wingerdstok’, sou sy dissipels die verwysing raakgevat het. In die Ou Testament is Israel dikwels as God se wingerdstok voorgestel. Jesaja 5 bevat ’n hartseer ‘lied van die wingerd’: God het ’n uitgesoekte wingerdstok geplant, dit versorg, en ‘verwag dat dit goeie druiwe sou dra, maar dit het net slegte druiwe gedra’. Israel het nie die geregtigheid en reg gedra wat God begeer het nie.

So wanneer Jesus Homself die ‘ware wingerdstok’ noem, beweer Hy dat Hy is wat Israel veronderstel was om te wees, die getroue Seun wat die vrugte dra wat God nog altyd wou hê. En nou word mense deel van God se wingerdstok deur aan Hom verbind te wees.

Die sentrale bevel is ‘bly in My’, elf keer in die gedeelte gebruik. Dit is ’n verhoudingswoord. Dit beskryf voortdurende, intieme, afhanklike verbinding. Dit is nie ’n eenmalige besluit nie, maar ’n daaglikse leefwyse.

Dit is radikaal anders as die manier waarop baie mense oor die Christelike lewe dink. Ons sien dit dikwels as sukkel: harder probeer om goed te wees, meer te bid en meer te doen. Maar lote sukkel nie. Hulle ontvang. Vrugte is die natuurlike gevolg van verbinding, nie die produk van inspanning nie. Dit beteken nie ons doen niks nie. Om te bly vra doelbewustheid. Maar ons hooffokus is om naby Jesus te bly, en vrugte volg.
Jesus sê ‘sonder My kan julle niks doen nie’. Dit beteken nie ons kan niks doen nie; nie-Christene bereik baie dinge. Dit beteken niks van blywende, ewige vrugte kom uit ons eie hulpbronne nie.

Snoei is nog ’n belangrike idee. Die Vader ‘snoei’ lote wat vrugte dra sodat hulle nog meer vrugte dra. Snoei kan pynlik wees: teleurstellings, verliese, die verwydering van dinge waaraan ons geheg was. Maar in God se hande is dit nie straf nie; dit is voorbereiding vir groter vrugbaarheid.

Let op hoe liefde en gehoorsaamheid verbind is: ‘As julle my gebooie gehoorsaam, sal julle in my liefde bly, net soos Ek my Vader se gebooie gehoorsaam het en in sy liefde bly.’ Dit is nie om liefde te verdien nie. Jesus se gehoorsaamheid aan die Vader het uit hulle liefdesverhouding gevloei, en ons s’n ook. Dan noem Jesus sy dissipels iets verbasends: ‘Ek noem julle nie meer diensknegte nie… Ek noem julle vriende.’ Om in Hom te bly, beteken om as Jesus se vriend te lewe.

verse.text: Soos die Vader My liefgehad het, het Ek julle liefgehad. Bly nou in my liefde.

lessons: Jesus is die ware wingerdstok, die getroue Seun wat die vrugte dra wat God begeer het.
Die Christelike lewe is om te bly, nie om te sukkel nie: vrugte vloei uit verbinding.
Gehoorsaamheid vloei uit liefde, en Jesus noem ons sy vriende.
questions: Hoe help Jesaja 5 jou om Jesus se aanspraak om die ‘ware wingerdstok’ te wees, te verstaan?
Wat is die verskil tussen bly en sukkel? Watter een beskryf jou geloof meer?
Hoe het jy al ‘snoei’ ervaar, en wat het God daardeur laat groei?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Moenie vir iets vra nie; rus net in Jesus se liefde, soos ’n loot in die stok rus. Skryf daarna neer wat jy agtergekom het.
prayer: Jesus, U is die ware wingerdstok, en ek wil in U bly.
Vergewe my dat ek in my eie krag sukkel, veral in…
Dankie dat U my u vriend noem.

mission.text: Oefen hierdie week om te ‘bly’: begin elke dag deur stil by Jesus te sit voordat jy Hom vir iets vra.

af.journal: Skryf ’n kort opstel: ‘Wat dit beteken om ’n loot te wees.’ Sluit die wingerdstok, bly, snoei, vrugte en vriendskap in.

en.title: Stay Close to Jesus
story: Jesus said, ‘I am like a grapevine.’
‘You are like the little branches.’
Branches that stay on the vine grow yummy grapes!
When I stay close to Jesus, I grow good things too.
I want to stay close to Jesus!

verse.text: Stay close to me, and you will grow good fruit.

en.action: Hold hands with someone like a vine and its branches, and say: ‘I stay close to Jesus!’
lessons: I grow when I stay close to Jesus.
questions: Do you like grapes?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
I want to stay close to you. Amen.

af.title: Bly Naby Jesus
story: Jesus het gesê: ‘Ek is soos ’n wingerdstok.’
‘Julle is soos die klein lote.’
Lote wat aan die stok bly, kry lekker druiwe!
As ek naby Jesus bly, groei daar ook goeie dinge in my.
Ek wil naby Jesus bly!

verse.text: Bly naby My, en julle sal goeie vrugte dra.

af.action: Hou iemand se hand vas soos ’n stok en sy loot, en sê: ‘Ek bly naby Jesus!’
lessons: Ek groei as ek naby Jesus bly.
questions: Hou jy van druiwe?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
ek wil naby U bly. Amen.

en.title: The Vine and the Branches
story: On the way to the garden where He would pray on His last night, Jesus may have walked past grapevines with His disciples. He used them to teach something very important.
‘I am the vine,’ Jesus said, ‘and you are the branches.’

Have you ever seen a grapevine? It has a thick, strong trunk called the vine, and lots of thinner branches growing out of it. The branches get water and food from the vine. That’s how they grow leaves and juicy bunches of grapes.
But what happens if a branch is broken off the vine? It can’t grow anything. It dries up. ‘Apart from me you can do nothing,’ Jesus said.
Jesus was telling His friends: ‘Stay close to me, and I will stay close to you. If you stay close to me, you will grow lots of good fruit.’

What kind of fruit? Not apples or grapes! Jesus meant good things growing in our lives, like love, joy, kindness and patience. We don’t make that fruit by trying really hard on our own. It grows when we stay connected to Jesus.
How do we stay close to Jesus? By talking to Him, listening to Him, reading His Word and loving Him every day, just like we do on our Lantern Trail. ‘Remain in my love,’ Jesus said.

verse.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. If you stay in me, you will bear much fruit.

lessons: I grow by staying close to Jesus.
Good things grow in me when I am connected to Jesus.
I can stay close to Jesus by talking and listening to Him every day.
questions: What happens to a branch that is broken off the vine?
What helps you stay close to Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
you are the vine and I am a branch.
Help me stay close to you every day,
so that good fruit grows in my life. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, talk to Jesus three times: in the morning, at lunchtime and before bed.

af.title: Die Wingerdstok en die Lote
story: Op pad na die tuin waar Hy op sy laaste aand sou bid, het Jesus dalk saam met sy dissipels by wingerdstokke verbygeloop. Hy het hulle gebruik om iets baie belangriks te leer.
‘Ek is die wingerdstok,’ het Jesus gesê, ‘en julle is die lote.’

Het jy al ’n wingerdstok gesien? Dit het ’n dik, sterk stam wat die stok genoem word, en baie dunner lote wat daaruit groei. Die lote kry water en kos van die stok af. Dit is hoe hulle blare en sappige trosse druiwe kry.
Maar wat gebeur as ’n loot van die stok afgebreek word? Dit kan niks laat groei nie. Dit droog uit. ‘Sonder My kan julle niks doen nie,’ het Jesus gesê.
Jesus het vir sy vriende gesê: ‘Bly naby My, en Ek sal naby julle bly. As julle naby My bly, sal julle baie goeie vrugte dra.’

Watter soort vrugte? Nie appels of druiwe nie! Jesus het goeie dinge bedoel wat in ons lewe groei, soos liefde, vreugde, goedheid en geduld. Ons maak nie daardie vrugte deur op ons eie baie hard te probeer nie. Dit groei as ons aan Jesus verbind bly.
Hoe bly ons naby Jesus? Deur met Hom te praat, na Hom te luister, sy Woord te lees en Hom elke dag lief te hê, net soos ons op ons Lanternpad doen. ‘Bly in my liefde,’ het Jesus gesê.

verse.text: Ek is die wingerdstok; julle is die lote. As julle in My bly, sal julle baie vrugte dra.

lessons: Ek groei deur naby Jesus te bly.
Goeie dinge groei in my as ek aan Jesus verbind is.
Ek kan naby Jesus bly deur elke dag met Hom te praat en na Hom te luister.
questions: Wat gebeur met ’n loot wat van die stok afgebreek is?
Wat help jou om naby Jesus te bly?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
U is die wingerdstok en ek is ’n loot.
Help my om elke dag naby U te bly,
sodat goeie vrugte in my lewe groei. Amen.

mission.text: Praat môre drie keer met Jesus: in die oggend, teen middagete en voor slaaptyd.

en.title: The Vine and the Branches
story: On the way to the garden where He would pray on His last night, Jesus may have walked past grapevines with His disciples. He used them to teach something very important.
‘I am the vine,’ Jesus said, ‘and you are the branches.’

Have you ever seen a grapevine? It has a thick, strong trunk called the vine, and lots of thinner branches growing out of it. The branches get water and food from the vine. That’s how they grow leaves and juicy bunches of grapes.
But what happens if a branch is broken off the vine? It can’t grow anything. It dries up. ‘Apart from me you can do nothing,’ Jesus said.
Jesus was telling His friends: ‘Stay close to me, and I will stay close to you. If you stay close to me, you will grow lots of good fruit.’

What kind of fruit? Not apples or grapes! Jesus meant good things growing in our lives, like love, joy, kindness and patience. We don’t make that fruit by trying really hard on our own. It grows when we stay connected to Jesus.
How do we stay close to Jesus? By talking to Him, listening to Him, reading His Word and loving Him every day, just like we do on our Lantern Trail. ‘Remain in my love,’ Jesus said.

verse.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. If you stay in me, you will bear much fruit.

lessons: I grow by staying close to Jesus.
Good things grow in me when I am connected to Jesus.
I can stay close to Jesus by talking and listening to Him every day.
questions: What happens to a branch that is broken off the vine?
What helps you stay close to Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
you are the vine and I am a branch.
Help me stay close to you every day,
so that good fruit grows in my life. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, talk to Jesus three times: in the morning, at lunchtime and before bed.

en.fact: Gardeners prune grapevines, cutting off some parts so that the vine grows even more grapes. Jesus said God, the gardener, prunes us too, so that we grow even more good fruit.
en.deeper: What ‘fruit’ would you like to see growing in your life?
en.journal: Draw a vine with branches and bunches of grapes. On each grape, write a good thing that grows when we stay close to Jesus.

af.title: Die Wingerdstok en die Lote
story: Op pad na die tuin waar Hy op sy laaste aand sou bid, het Jesus dalk saam met sy dissipels by wingerdstokke verbygeloop. Hy het hulle gebruik om iets baie belangriks te leer.
‘Ek is die wingerdstok,’ het Jesus gesê, ‘en julle is die lote.’

Het jy al ’n wingerdstok gesien? Dit het ’n dik, sterk stam wat die stok genoem word, en baie dunner lote wat daaruit groei. Die lote kry water en kos van die stok af. Dit is hoe hulle blare en sappige trosse druiwe kry.
Maar wat gebeur as ’n loot van die stok afgebreek word? Dit kan niks laat groei nie. Dit droog uit. ‘Sonder My kan julle niks doen nie,’ het Jesus gesê.
Jesus het vir sy vriende gesê: ‘Bly naby My, en Ek sal naby julle bly. As julle naby My bly, sal julle baie goeie vrugte dra.’

Watter soort vrugte? Nie appels of druiwe nie! Jesus het goeie dinge bedoel wat in ons lewe groei, soos liefde, vreugde, goedheid en geduld. Ons maak nie daardie vrugte deur op ons eie baie hard te probeer nie. Dit groei as ons aan Jesus verbind bly.
Hoe bly ons naby Jesus? Deur met Hom te praat, na Hom te luister, sy Woord te lees en Hom elke dag lief te hê, net soos ons op ons Lanternpad doen. ‘Bly in my liefde,’ het Jesus gesê.

verse.text: Ek is die wingerdstok; julle is die lote. As julle in My bly, sal julle baie vrugte dra.

lessons: Ek groei deur naby Jesus te bly.
Goeie dinge groei in my as ek aan Jesus verbind is.
Ek kan naby Jesus bly deur elke dag met Hom te praat en na Hom te luister.
questions: Wat gebeur met ’n loot wat van die stok afgebreek is?
Wat help jou om naby Jesus te bly?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
U is die wingerdstok en ek is ’n loot.
Help my om elke dag naby U te bly,
sodat goeie vrugte in my lewe groei. Amen.

mission.text: Praat môre drie keer met Jesus: in die oggend, teen middagete en voor slaaptyd.

af.fact: Tuiniers snoei wingerdstokke, en sny party dele af sodat die stok nog meer druiwe dra. Jesus het gesê God, die tuinier, snoei ons ook, sodat ons nog meer goeie vrugte dra.
af.deeper: Watter ‘vrugte’ wil jy graag in jou lewe sien groei?
af.journal: Teken ’n wingerdstok met lote en trosse druiwe. Skryf op elke druif ’n goeie ding wat groei as ons naby Jesus bly.

trait.en: Jesus prays for me
trait.af: Jesus bid vir my

en.title: Jesus Prayed for You
story: After the Last Supper, before walking to the Garden of Gethsemane where He would be arrested, Jesus looked up to heaven and prayed. John recorded the whole prayer, and it is the longest prayer of Jesus in the Bible. It is like being allowed to listen in on a conversation between the Son and the Father.

Jesus prayed in three circles. First, for Himself: ‘Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may glorify you.’ He also gave a beautiful definition of eternal life: ‘Now this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.’ Eternal life isn’t just living forever. It is knowing God, a relationship that begins now.

Second, Jesus prayed for His disciples. ‘Holy Father, protect them by the power of your name… so that they may be one as we are one.’ He didn’t ask God to take them out of the world, but to protect them from the evil one while they lived in it. ‘Sanctify them by the truth; your word is truth.’

Third, Jesus widened the circle: ‘My prayer is not for them alone. I pray also for those who will believe in me through their message.’ That includes every Christian who has ever lived, including you! The disciples told others, who told others, who told others, all the way down to you.

What did Jesus pray for you? ‘That all of them may be one, Father, just as you are in me and I am in you.’ He prayed that you would be united with other believers in love. He prayed that the world would see that love and believe. And finally, ‘Father, I want those you have given me to be with me where I am, and to see my glory.’ Jesus wants you with Him forever.
And Jesus’ prayers didn’t stop that night. Hebrews says that He ‘always lives to intercede’ for us. Right now, He is praying for you.

verse.text: Now this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.

lessons: Eternal life means knowing God, a relationship that begins now.
Jesus prayed for everyone who would believe, including you.
Jesus wants His followers to be one in love and to be with Him forever.
questions: What are the three ‘circles’ of Jesus’ prayer?
How does John 17:3 describe eternal life?
How does it feel to know Jesus prayed for you by name, long before you were born?
en.listen: Read John 17:20–24 slowly, putting your own name in where it says ‘those who will believe’. Ask Jesus: ‘What are you praying for me today?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for praying for me.
I want to know you more, especially…
Help me to love other Christians, so that the world can see your love.

mission.text: This week, pray for Christians in another church or another country, asking God to make us one in love.

en.journal: Write down a family tree of faith: who told you about Jesus? Who told them? Then write one person you would like to tell.

af.title: Jesus het vir Jou Gebid
story: Ná die Laaste Avondmaal, voordat Hy na die tuin van Getsemane geloop het waar Hy gevange geneem sou word, het Jesus na die hemel opgekyk en gebid. Johannes het die hele gebed opgeskryf, en dit is die langste gebed van Jesus in die Bybel. Dit is soos om toegelaat te word om in te luister op ’n gesprek tussen die Seun en die Vader.

Jesus het in drie kringe gebid. Eerstens vir Homself: ‘Vader, die uur het gekom. Verheerlik u Seun, sodat u Seun U kan verheerlik.’ Hy het ook ’n pragtige beskrywing van die ewige lewe gegee: ‘Dit is die ewige lewe: dat hulle U ken, die enigste ware God, en Jesus Christus, wat U gestuur het.’ Ewige lewe is nie net om vir altyd te lewe nie. Dit is om God te ken, ’n verhouding wat nou begin.

Tweedens het Jesus vir sy dissipels gebid. ‘Heilige Vader, beskerm hulle deur die krag van u Naam… sodat hulle een kan wees soos Ons een is.’ Hy het nie God gevra om hulle uit die wêreld uit te haal nie, maar om hulle teen die Bose te beskerm terwyl hulle daarin lewe. ‘Heilig hulle deur die waarheid; u woord is die waarheid.’

Derdens het Jesus die kring groter gemaak: ‘Ek bid nie net vir hulle nie. Ek bid ook vir die wat deur hulle boodskap in My sal glo.’ Dit sluit elke Christen in wat nog ooit gelewe het, ook jy! Die dissipels het ander vertel, wat ander vertel het, wat ander vertel het, tot by jou.

Wat het Jesus vir jou gebid? ‘Dat hulle almal een mag wees, Vader, net soos U in My is en Ek in U.’ Hy het gebid dat jy in liefde met ander gelowiges verenig sal wees. Hy het gebid dat die wêreld daardie liefde sal sien en glo. En laastens: ‘Vader, Ek wil hê dat die wat U My gegee het, by My moet wees waar Ek is, en my heerlikheid moet sien.’ Jesus wil jou vir altyd by Hom hê.
En Jesus se gebede het nie daardie aand opgehou nie. Hebreërs sê dat Hy ‘altyd lewe om vir ons in te tree’. Op die oomblik bid Hy vir jou.

verse.text: Dit is die ewige lewe: dat hulle U ken, die enigste ware God, en Jesus Christus, wat U gestuur het.

lessons: Ewige lewe beteken om God te ken, ’n verhouding wat nou begin.
Jesus het gebid vir almal wat sou glo, ook vir jou.
Jesus wil hê sy volgelinge moet een wees in liefde en vir altyd by Hom wees.
questions: Wat is die drie ‘kringe’ van Jesus se gebed?
Hoe beskryf Johannes 17:3 die ewige lewe?
Hoe voel dit om te weet Jesus het vir jou gebid, lank voordat jy gebore is?
af.listen: Lees Johannes 17:20–24 stadig, en sit jou eie naam in waar dit sê ‘die wat sal glo’. Vra Jesus: ‘Waarvoor bid U vandag vir my?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U vir my gebid het.
Ek wil U beter leer ken, veral…
Help my om ander Christene lief te hê, sodat die wêreld u liefde kan sien.

mission.text: Bid hierdie week vir Christene in ’n ander kerk of ’n ander land, en vra God om ons een te maak in liefde.

af.journal: Skryf ’n geloofstamboom neer: wie het jou van Jesus vertel? Wie het hulle vertel? Skryf dan een persoon neer vir wie jy graag wil vertel.

en.title: That They May Be One
story: John 17 has been called the ‘holy of holies’ of the Gospels. It is Jesus’ longest recorded prayer, prayed aloud on the night before His crucifixion. Some call it His ‘High Priestly Prayer’, because in it Jesus does what the high priest did: He intercedes for God’s people and prepares to offer a sacrifice, Himself.

The prayer opens with the hour of glory. For John, Jesus’ ‘glory’ is revealed most fully not in power but at the cross, where the depth of God’s love is displayed. Jesus asks the Father to glorify Him ‘with the glory I had with you before the world began’, a clear statement of His eternal existence with the Father.

Verse 3 defines eternal life: ‘that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent’. The word ‘know’ here means personal, relational knowledge, not just information. Eternal life is first a quality of life, a relationship with the Triune God, and it begins the moment we believe.

For His disciples, Jesus asks for protection, joy and sanctification (being set apart for God) ‘by the truth; your word is truth’. He asks not that they be taken out of the world, but kept from the evil one in it. Christians are called to be ‘in the world but not of the world’: engaged, present and loving, but not shaped by its values.

Then Jesus prays for all future believers, and His central request is unity: ‘that all of them may be one, Father, just as you are in me and I am in you’. The model for Christian unity is the relationship within the Trinity itself. And the purpose is mission: ‘so that the world may believe that you have sent me’. When Christians are divided, the world struggles to believe. When we love one another across our differences, the world sees something of God.

Unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Christians have different traditions, styles and even some different views. But we share one Father, one Lord, one Spirit and one hope. Jesus prayed for that unity, and so should we.
Finally, Hebrews tells us that Jesus’ prayers continue: ‘He always lives to intercede for them.’ The Son of God, at the Father’s right hand, is praying for you by name.

verse.text: Therefore He is able to save completely those who come to God through Him, because He always lives to intercede for them.

lessons: Eternal life is knowing God personally, and it begins now.
Christians are called to be in the world but not shaped by it.
Jesus prays for the unity of believers so that the world may believe, and He still intercedes for us.
questions: What does John 17:5 tell us about who Jesus is?
What does ‘in the world but not of the world’ look like in your daily life?
Why is unity among Christians so important to Jesus? Where do you see disunity, and how could you help?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Picture Jesus at the Father’s right hand, praying for you. Ask: ‘What are you praying for me right now?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you always live to intercede for me.
Keep me from the evil one, and set me apart by your truth, especially in…
Make your people one, and help me build unity, not division.

mission.text: This week, do something to build unity: encourage a Christian from a different church, or make peace in a group that is divided.

en.journal: Write about how Christians can be united while still having differences. What should we agree on, and where can we give each other freedom?

af.title: Sodat Hulle Een Kan Wees
story: Johannes 17 is al die ‘allerheiligste’ van die Evangelies genoem. Dit is Jesus se langste opgetekende gebed, hardop gebid die aand voor sy kruisiging. Party noem dit sy ‘Hoëpriesterlike Gebed’, omdat Jesus daarin doen wat die hoëpriester gedoen het: Hy tree in vir God se mense en berei Hom voor om ’n offer te bring, Homself.

Die gebed begin met die uur van heerlikheid. Vir Johannes word Jesus se ‘heerlikheid’ die volste geopenbaar nie in mag nie, maar by die kruis, waar die diepte van God se liefde gewys word. Jesus vra die Vader om Hom te verheerlik ‘met die heerlikheid wat Ek by U gehad het voordat die wêreld begin het’, ’n duidelike stelling van sy ewige bestaan by die Vader.

Vers 3 beskryf die ewige lewe: ‘dat hulle U ken, die enigste ware God, en Jesus Christus, wat U gestuur het’. Die woord ‘ken’ beteken hier persoonlike kennis in ’n verhouding, nie net inligting nie. Ewige lewe is eerstens ’n kwaliteit van lewe, ’n verhouding met die Drie-enige God, en dit begin die oomblik dat ons glo.

Vir sy dissipels vra Jesus beskerming, vreugde en heiliging (om vir God afgesonder te word) ‘deur die waarheid; u woord is die waarheid’. Hy vra nie dat hulle uit die wêreld weggeneem word nie, maar dat hulle daarin teen die Bose bewaar word. Christene word geroep om ‘in die wêreld, maar nie van die wêreld nie’ te wees: betrokke, teenwoordig en liefdevol, maar nie gevorm deur sy waardes nie.

Dan bid Jesus vir alle toekomstige gelowiges, en sy sentrale versoek is eenheid: ‘dat hulle almal een mag wees, Vader, net soos U in My is en Ek in U’. Die voorbeeld vir Christelike eenheid is die verhouding binne die Drie-eenheid self. En die doel is sending: ‘sodat die wêreld kan glo dat U My gestuur het’. As Christene verdeeld is, sukkel die wêreld om te glo. As ons mekaar oor ons verskille heen liefhet, sien die wêreld iets van God.

Eenheid beteken nie eenvormigheid nie. Christene het verskillende tradisies, style en selfs party verskillende sienings. Maar ons deel een Vader, een Here, een Gees en een hoop. Jesus het vir daardie eenheid gebid, en ons moet ook.
Laastens vertel Hebreërs ons dat Jesus se gebede voortgaan: ‘Hy lewe altyd om vir hulle in te tree.’ Die Seun van God, aan die Vader se regterhand, bid op jou naam vir jou.

verse.text: Daarom kan Hy die wat deur Hom na God kom, volkome red, omdat Hy altyd lewe om vir hulle in te tree.

lessons: Ewige lewe is om God persoonlik te ken, en dit begin nou.
Christene word geroep om in die wêreld te wees, maar nie daardeur gevorm te word nie.
Jesus bid vir die eenheid van gelowiges sodat die wêreld kan glo, en Hy tree steeds vir ons in.
questions: Wat vertel Johannes 17:5 ons oor wie Jesus is?
Hoe lyk ‘in die wêreld, maar nie van die wêreld nie’ in jou daaglikse lewe?
Hoekom is eenheid tussen Christene so belangrik vir Jesus? Waar sien jy verdeeldheid, en hoe kan jy help?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Sien in jou gedagtes hoe Jesus aan die Vader se regterhand vir jou bid. Vra: ‘Waarvoor bid U nou vir my?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U altyd lewe om vir my in te tree.
Bewaar my teen die Bose, en sonder my af deur u waarheid, veral in…
Maak u volk een, en help my om eenheid te bou, nie verdeeldheid nie.

mission.text: Doen hierdie week iets om eenheid te bou: bemoedig ’n Christen van ’n ander kerk, of maak vrede in ’n groep wat verdeeld is.

af.journal: Skryf oor hoe Christene verenig kan wees terwyl hulle steeds verskille het. Waaroor moet ons saamstem, en waar kan ons mekaar vryheid gee?

en.title: Jesus Prays for Me
story: Before Jesus went to the cross, He prayed.
He prayed for His friends.
And guess what? He prayed for you too!
Jesus asked God to keep you safe and to help you love each other.
Jesus prays for me!

verse.text: Jesus prays for us.

en.action: Put your hand on your heart and say: ‘Jesus prays for me!’
lessons: Jesus prays for me.
questions: Who would you like to pray for?
prayer: Thank you, Jesus,
for praying for me. Amen.

af.title: Jesus Bid vir My
story: Voordat Jesus na die kruis gegaan het, het Hy gebid.
Hy het vir sy vriende gebid.
En raai wat? Hy het ook vir jou gebid!
Jesus het God gevra om jou veilig te hou en jou te help om mekaar lief te hê.
Jesus bid vir my!

verse.text: Jesus bid vir ons.

af.action: Sit jou hand op jou hart en sê: ‘Jesus bid vir my!’
lessons: Jesus bid vir my.
questions: Vir wie wil jy graag bid?
prayer: Dankie, Jesus,
dat U vir my bid. Amen.

en.title: The Prayer Jesus Prayed for You
story: On His last night before the cross, after supper, Jesus looked up to heaven and prayed a long, beautiful prayer. His disciples heard every word.
First Jesus prayed for Himself: ‘Father, the time has come. Bring glory to your Son, so that your Son can bring glory to you.’ Jesus was ready to do what His Father had sent Him to do.
Then Jesus prayed for His disciples. ‘Father, I have told them all about you. Now please protect them. Keep them safe from the evil one. Help them to be one, just as we are one.’
And then Jesus said something wonderful: ‘I am not praying only for them. I am also praying for everyone who will believe in me because of their message.’

Do you know who that is? It’s you! Long, long ago, Jesus was already praying for you. He asked His Father to keep you close, to fill you with joy, to help God’s children love each other, and that one day you would be with Him and see His glory.
And Jesus didn’t stop praying. The Bible says that right now, Jesus is in heaven, praying for us. When you go to sleep tonight, you can remember: Jesus is praying for me.

verse.text: Christ Jesus… is at the right hand of God and is praying for us.

lessons: Jesus prays for me.
Jesus wants God’s children to love each other and be one.
Jesus wants me to be with Him forever.
questions: What did Jesus ask His Father to do for His friends?
How does it make you feel that Jesus prays for you?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that you prayed for me long ago,
and that you are praying for me now.
Help me to love your family. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, pray for three people in God’s family, just like Jesus prays for you.

af.title: Die Gebed wat Jesus vir Jou Gebid Het
story: Op sy laaste aand voor die kruis, ná ete, het Jesus na die hemel opgekyk en ’n lang, pragtige gebed gebid. Sy dissipels het elke woord gehoor.
Eers het Jesus vir Homself gebid: ‘Vader, die tyd het gekom. Verheerlik u Seun, sodat u Seun U kan verheerlik.’ Jesus was gereed om te doen waarvoor sy Vader Hom gestuur het.
Toe het Jesus vir sy dissipels gebid. ‘Vader, Ek het hulle alles van U vertel. Beskerm hulle nou asseblief. Hou hulle veilig teen die Bose. Help hulle om een te wees, net soos Ons een is.’
En toe het Jesus iets wonderliks gesê: ‘Ek bid nie net vir hulle nie. Ek bid ook vir almal wat deur hulle boodskap in My sal glo.’

Weet jy wie dit is? Dit is jy! Lank, lank gelede het Jesus al vir jou gebid. Hy het sy Vader gevra om jou naby te hou, jou met vreugde te vul, God se kinders te help om mekaar lief te hê, en dat jy eendag by Hom sal wees en sy heerlikheid sal sien.
En Jesus het nie opgehou bid nie. Die Bybel sê dat Jesus nou in die hemel is en vir ons bid. As jy vanaand gaan slaap, kan jy onthou: Jesus bid vir my.

verse.text: Christus Jesus… is aan die regterhand van God en bid vir ons.

lessons: Jesus bid vir my.
Jesus wil hê God se kinders moet mekaar liefhê en een wees.
Jesus wil hê ek moet vir altyd by Hom wees.
questions: Wat het Jesus sy Vader gevra om vir sy vriende te doen?
Hoe laat dit jou voel dat Jesus vir jou bid?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U lank gelede vir my gebid het,
en dat U nou vir my bid.
Help my om u familie lief te hê. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre vir drie mense in God se familie, net soos Jesus vir jou bid.

en.journal: Write ‘Jesus prays for me’ in the middle of a page. Around it, write the names of people you will pray for.

en.title: Campfire Night: The Living Water
story: Welcome to the fifth campfire of the Trail of the Living Water! This week brought you to the heart of the whole trail. At Jacob’s well, Jesus offered a thirsty woman living water. In Bethany, Mary chose the one thing needed, and Lazarus walked out of his tomb. In the upper room, Jesus washed His friends’ feet. On the way to the garden, He called Himself the vine and us the branches. And He prayed for you. Jesus is the spring our hearts were made for. When we remain in Him, His life flows through us.
en.game: Living water relay: set up six cups, one for each story this week. Take turns pouring water into a cup and naming what Jesus gives in that story (living water, His presence, life, cleansing, fruit, His prayers).

en.title: What I Do Have, I Give You
story: After Jesus rose from the dead and returned to heaven, He sent the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, just as He had promised. The disciples, who had been hiding in fear, became bold witnesses. Three thousand people believed in a single day! And the church kept growing.

One afternoon at three o’clock, the hour of prayer, Peter and John walked up to the temple. At the gate called Beautiful sat a man who had been lame from birth. He was over forty years old. Every day people carried him there to beg from the crowds going in to worship.

When he asked Peter and John for money, Peter looked straight at him and said, ‘Look at us!’ The man looked up, expecting coins. Then Peter said, ‘Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.’

Peter took him by the right hand and helped him up, and instantly his feet and ankles became strong. He jumped to his feet, began to walk, and went into the temple courts with them, ‘walking and jumping, and praising God’.

A crowd gathered, astonished. Peter used the moment to tell them about Jesus: ‘Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk?… By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know was made strong.’
Peter and John were ordinary fishermen. They had no money, no education and no special status. But they had the name of Jesus and the power of the Holy Spirit, and that was more than enough.

The same is true for you. You may not have much to give in the world’s eyes. But if you belong to Jesus, you carry His name and His Spirit. ‘What I do have, I give you’: kindness, prayer, the good news and the love of Jesus.

verse.text: Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.

lessons: There is power in the name of Jesus.
The Holy Spirit makes ordinary people bold.
We may not have much, but what we have in Jesus is worth sharing.
questions: What did the man expect, and what did he receive?
Why did Peter make sure everyone knew it wasn’t their own power?
What do you have in Jesus that you could give to someone else?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘What do I have from you that I can give to someone this week?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for the power of your name.
Holy Spirit, make me bold to share…
Use the little I have to bless others.

mission.text: This week, give someone something money can’t buy: a prayer, encouragement or your time.

en.journal: Write ‘Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you’. Then list what you ‘do have’ in Jesus.

af.title: Wat Ek Het, Gee Ek vir Jou
story: Nadat Jesus uit die dood opgestaan het en na die hemel teruggekeer het, het Hy op die Pinksterdag die Heilige Gees gestuur, net soos Hy belowe het. Die dissipels, wat van vrees weggekruip het, het dapper getuies geword. Drieduisend mense het op een dag geglo! En die kerk het aangehou groei.

Een middag om drie-uur, die uur van gebed, het Petrus en Johannes na die tempel opgegaan. By die poort wat die Mooipoort genoem is, het ’n man gesit wat van sy geboorte af lam was. Hy was meer as veertig jaar oud. Elke dag het mense hom daarheen gedra om te bedel by die skare wat ingegaan het om te aanbid.

Toe hy Petrus en Johannes vir geld vra, het Petrus reguit na hom gekyk en gesê: ‘Kyk na ons!’ Die man het opgekyk en muntstukke verwag. Toe sê Petrus: ‘Silwer of goud het ek nie, maar wat ek het, gee ek vir jou. In die Naam van Jesus Christus van Nasaret, loop.’

Petrus het hom aan die regterhand gevat en gehelp om op te staan, en dadelik het sy voete en enkels sterk geword. Hy het opgespring, begin loop, en saam met hulle die tempelvoorhowe ingegaan, ‘terwyl hy loop en spring en God prys’.

’n Skare het bymekaargekom, verstom. Petrus het die oomblik gebruik om hulle van Jesus te vertel: ‘Hoekom staar julle na ons asof ons deur ons eie krag of godsvrug hierdie man laat loop het?… Deur geloof in die Naam van Jesus is hierdie man, wat julle sien en ken, sterk gemaak.’

Petrus en Johannes was gewone vissers. Hulle het geen geld, geen opleiding en geen spesiale status gehad nie. Maar hulle het die Naam van Jesus en die krag van die Heilige Gees gehad, en dit was meer as genoeg.

Dieselfde is waar vir jou. Jy het dalk nie veel om te gee in die wêreld se oë nie. Maar as jy aan Jesus behoort, dra jy sy Naam en sy Gees. ‘Wat ek het, gee ek vir jou’: goedheid, gebed, die goeie nuus en die liefde van Jesus.

verse.text: Silwer of goud het ek nie, maar wat ek het, gee ek vir jou. In die Naam van Jesus Christus van Nasaret, loop.

lessons: Daar is krag in die Naam van Jesus.
Die Heilige Gees maak gewone mense dapper.
Ons het dalk nie veel nie, maar wat ons in Jesus het, is die moeite werd om te deel.
questions: Wat het die man verwag, en wat het hy ontvang?
Hoekom het Petrus seker gemaak almal weet dit was nie hulle eie krag nie?
Wat het jy in Jesus wat jy vir iemand anders kan gee?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Wat het ek van U wat ek hierdie week vir iemand kan gee?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, dankie vir die krag van u Naam.
Heilige Gees, maak my dapper om… te deel.
Gebruik die bietjie wat ek het om ander te seën.

mission.text: Gee hierdie week vir iemand iets wat geld nie kan koop nie: ’n gebed, bemoediging of jou tyd.

af.journal: Skryf ‘Silwer of goud het ek nie, maar wat ek het, gee ek vir jou’. Lys dan wat jy in Jesus ‘het’.

en.title: The Power of the Name
story: The book of Acts could be called ‘The Acts of the Holy Spirit through the Apostles’. Luke, its author, tells us his first book (the Gospel of Luke) was about ‘all that Jesus began to do and to teach’. Acts is the continuation: what the risen Jesus kept on doing through His Spirit-filled people.

Acts 3 gives us the first detailed miracle after Pentecost, and it is carefully chosen. The man at the Beautiful Gate was a living symbol of human helplessness: lame from birth, over forty years old, dependent on others and stuck outside the place of worship. The law barred some people with disabilities from serving in parts of the temple, and he sat at the threshold, unable to enter.

Peter’s words are famous: ‘Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.’ In the ancient world, a ‘name’ represented a person’s authority and character. To act ‘in the name of Jesus’ is to act on His authority, as His representative. It isn’t a magic formula; it is a relationship of delegated power.

The healing is complete and immediate, and the man goes where he couldn’t go before, into the temple, ‘walking and jumping, and praising God’. Isaiah had prophesied that in the Messiah’s day ‘the lame will leap like a deer’. The prophecy was being fulfilled.

Peter immediately redirects the attention: ‘Why do you stare at us?’ Then he preaches Jesus: the one they rejected, whom ‘God raised from the dead’. He calls them to ‘repent… and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out, that times of refreshing may come from the Lord’.

The result? Peter and John were arrested. But when they stood before the same council that had condemned Jesus, Peter, ‘filled with the Holy Spirit’, declared: ‘Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.’ The leaders ‘were astonished and they took note that these men had been with Jesus’.
That is the secret: ordinary people who have been with Jesus, filled with His Spirit, acting in His name.

verse.text: Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.

lessons: Acts is the continuing story of what Jesus does through His Spirit-filled people.
Acting ‘in Jesus’ name’ means acting on His authority, not using a formula.
People notice when ordinary believers have ‘been with Jesus’.
questions: What does it mean to act ‘in the name of Jesus’?
Why is it significant that the healed man could now enter the temple?
What would it look like for people to notice that you ‘have been with Jesus’?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask the Holy Spirit: ‘Where do you want to act through me in Jesus’ name?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, there is no other name by which we are saved.
Holy Spirit, fill me and make me bold in…
Let people see that I have been with Jesus.

mission.text: This week, offer to pray for someone who is sick or struggling, in Jesus’ name, and trust Him with the result.

en.journal: Write about Acts 4:13. What do you think made the leaders notice that Peter and John had been with Jesus?

af.title: Die Krag van die Naam
story: Die boek Handelinge kan ‘Die Handelinge van die Heilige Gees deur die Apostels’ genoem word. Lukas, die skrywer, vertel ons sy eerste boek (die Evangelie van Lukas) het gegaan oor ‘alles wat Jesus begin doen en leer het’. Handelinge is die voortsetting: wat die opgestane Jesus aangehou doen het deur sy mense wat met die Gees gevul is.

Handelinge 3 gee ons die eerste gedetailleerde wonderwerk ná Pinkster, en dit is versigtig gekies. Die man by die Mooipoort was ’n lewende simbool van menslike hulpeloosheid: van geboorte af lam, meer as veertig jaar oud, afhanklik van ander en vasgevang buite die plek van aanbidding. Hy het by die drumpel gesit, nie in staat om in te gaan nie.

Petrus se woorde is bekend: ‘Silwer of goud het ek nie, maar wat ek het, gee ek vir jou. In die Naam van Jesus Christus van Nasaret, loop.’ In die antieke wêreld het ’n ‘naam’ ’n persoon se gesag en karakter verteenwoordig. Om ‘in die Naam van Jesus’ op te tree, is om op sy gesag op te tree, as sy verteenwoordiger. Dit is nie ’n towerformule nie; dit is ’n verhouding van gedelegeerde krag.

Die genesing is volkome en onmiddellik, en die man gaan waar hy voorheen nie kon gaan nie, die tempel in, ‘terwyl hy loop en spring en God prys’. Jesaja het geprofeteer dat in die dag van die Messias ‘die lammes soos ’n takbok sal spring’. Die profesie is vervul.

Petrus stuur dadelik die aandag weg van hulle af: ‘Hoekom staar julle na ons?’ Dan preek hy Jesus: die een wat hulle verwerp het, wat ‘God uit die dood opgewek het’. Hy roep hulle op om ‘julle te bekeer… en na God te draai, sodat julle sondes uitgewis kan word, sodat tye van verkwikking van die Here kan kom’.

Die gevolg? Petrus en Johannes is gevange geneem. Maar toe hulle voor dieselfde raad staan wat Jesus veroordeel het, het Petrus, ‘vol van die Heilige Gees’, verklaar: ‘Daar is in niemand anders redding nie, want daar is onder die hemel geen ander naam aan die mense gegee waardeur ons gered moet word nie.’ Die leiers ‘was verbaas en het opgemerk dat hierdie manne by Jesus was’.
Dit is die geheim: gewone mense wat by Jesus was, vol van sy Gees, wat in sy Naam optree.

verse.text: Daar is in niemand anders redding nie, want daar is onder die hemel geen ander naam aan die mense gegee waardeur ons gered moet word nie.

lessons: Handelinge is die voortgaande storie van wat Jesus doen deur sy mense wat met die Gees gevul is.
Om ‘in Jesus se Naam’ op te tree, beteken om op sy gesag op te tree, nie om ’n formule te gebruik nie.
Mense merk op as gewone gelowiges ‘by Jesus was’.
questions: Wat beteken dit om ‘in die Naam van Jesus’ op te tree?
Hoekom is dit betekenisvol dat die genese man nou die tempel kon binnegaan?
Hoe sou dit lyk as mense opmerk dat jy ‘by Jesus was’?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra die Heilige Gees: ‘Waar wil U in Jesus se Naam deur my optree?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, daar is geen ander naam waardeur ons gered word nie.
Heilige Gees, vul my en maak my dapper in…
Laat mense sien dat ek by Jesus was.

mission.text: Bied hierdie week aan om vir iemand wat siek is of sukkel, in Jesus se Naam te bid, en vertrou Hom met die uitkoms.

af.journal: Skryf oor Handelinge 4:13. Wat dink jy het die leiers laat opmerk dat Petrus en Johannes by Jesus was?

en.title: Walking and Jumping!
story: A man sat by a big gate. His legs couldn’t walk.
Peter and John came by. ‘We don’t have money,’ said Peter.
‘But in Jesus’ name, get up and walk!’
The man stood up! He walked and jumped and praised God!
There is power in Jesus’ name!

verse.text: In the name of Jesus, get up and walk!

en.action: Sit down, then stand up and jump around shouting: ‘Praise God!’
lessons: There is power in Jesus’ name.
questions: How high can you jump?
prayer: Thank you, Jesus,
your name is so powerful! Amen.

af.title: Loop en Spring!
story: ’n Man het by ’n groot poort gesit. Sy bene kon nie loop nie.
Petrus en Johannes het verbygekom. ‘Ons het nie geld nie,’ het Petrus gesê.
‘Maar in die Naam van Jesus, staan op en loop!’
Die man het opgestaan! Hy het geloop en gespring en God geprys!
Daar is krag in Jesus se Naam!

verse.text: In die Naam van Jesus, staan op en loop!

af.action: Sit, staan dan op en spring rond en roep: ‘Prys God!’
lessons: Daar is krag in Jesus se Naam.
questions: Hoe hoog kan jy spring?
prayer: Dankie, Jesus,
u Naam is so kragtig! Amen.

en.title: Silver, Gold and Something Better
story: After Jesus went back to heaven, He sent the Holy Spirit to His friends, just as He had promised. Now the disciples were full of God’s power, and they told everyone about Jesus.

One afternoon, Peter and John were going to the temple to pray. At the gate called Beautiful sat a man who had never been able to walk, not even once in his whole life. Every day his friends carried him there so that he could beg for money.
‘Please, can you give me some money?’ he asked Peter and John.

Peter looked straight at him and said, ‘Look at us!’ The man looked up, hoping to get some coins. But Peter said, ‘I don’t have silver or gold. But what I do have, I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!’

Peter took his hand and helped him up. Straight away, the man’s feet and ankles became strong! He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went into the temple with them, walking and jumping and praising God!
Everyone who saw him was amazed. ‘Isn’t that the man who used to sit by the gate?’ they said. Peter told them, ‘It wasn’t our power that did this. It was the name of Jesus!’
Jesus is alive, and there is still power in His name today.

verse.text: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!

lessons: There is power in the name of Jesus.
Jesus is alive and still works through His people.
Jesus can give something better than money.
questions: What did the man ask for? What did Peter give him instead?
How do you think the man felt when he could walk and jump?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that your name is powerful.
Thank you that you are alive
and still help people today. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you pray, finish ‘in Jesus’ name’, and remember how powerful His name is.

af.title: Silwer, Goud en Iets Beters
story: Nadat Jesus teruggegaan het hemel toe, het Hy die Heilige Gees na sy vriende gestuur, net soos Hy belowe het. Nou was die dissipels vol van God se krag, en hulle het vir almal van Jesus vertel.

Een middag was Petrus en Johannes op pad na die tempel om te bid. By die poort wat die Mooipoort genoem is, het ’n man gesit wat nog nooit kon loop nie, nie eers een keer in sy hele lewe nie. Elke dag het sy vriende hom daarheen gedra sodat hy vir geld kon bedel.
‘Kan julle my asseblief ’n bietjie geld gee?’ het hy vir Petrus en Johannes gevra.

Petrus het reguit na hom gekyk en gesê: ‘Kyk na ons!’ Die man het opgekyk, en gehoop om ’n paar muntstukke te kry. Maar Petrus het gesê: ‘Ek het nie silwer of goud nie. Maar wat ek het, gee ek vir jou. In die Naam van Jesus Christus van Nasaret, loop!’

Petrus het sy hand gevat en hom gehelp om op te staan. Dadelik het die man se voete en enkels sterk geword! Hy het opgespring en begin loop. Toe het hy saam met hulle die tempel ingegaan, en geloop en gespring en God geprys!

Almal wat hom gesien het, was verbaas. ‘Is dit nie die man wat altyd by die poort gesit het nie?’ het hulle gesê. Petrus het vir hulle gesê: ‘Dit was nie ons krag wat dit gedoen het nie. Dit was die Naam van Jesus!’
Jesus leef, en daar is vandag nog krag in sy Naam.

verse.text: In die Naam van Jesus Christus van Nasaret, loop!

lessons: Daar is krag in die Naam van Jesus.
Jesus leef en werk steeds deur sy mense.
Jesus kan iets gee wat beter is as geld.
questions: Waarvoor het die man gevra? Wat het Petrus hom eerder gegee?
Hoe dink jy het die man gevoel toe hy kon loop en spring?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat u Naam kragtig is.
Dankie dat U leef
en vandag nog mense help. Amen.

mission.text: As jy môre bid, eindig ‘in Jesus se Naam’, en onthou hoe kragtig sy Naam is.

en.title: Silver, Gold and Something Better
story: After Jesus went back to heaven, He sent the Holy Spirit to His friends, just as He had promised. Now the disciples were full of God’s power, and they told everyone about Jesus.

One afternoon, Peter and John were going to the temple to pray. At the gate called Beautiful sat a man who had never been able to walk, not even once in his whole life. Every day his friends carried him there so that he could beg for money.
‘Please, can you give me some money?’ he asked Peter and John.

Peter looked straight at him and said, ‘Look at us!’ The man looked up, hoping to get some coins. But Peter said, ‘I don’t have silver or gold. But what I do have, I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!’

Peter took his hand and helped him up. Straight away, the man’s feet and ankles became strong! He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went into the temple with them, walking and jumping and praising God!
Everyone who saw him was amazed. ‘Isn’t that the man who used to sit by the gate?’ they said. Peter told them, ‘It wasn’t our power that did this. It was the name of Jesus!’
Jesus is alive, and there is still power in His name today.

verse.text: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!

lessons: There is power in the name of Jesus.
Jesus is alive and still works through His people.
Jesus can give something better than money.
questions: What did the man ask for? What did Peter give him instead?
How do you think the man felt when he could walk and jump?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that your name is powerful.
Thank you that you are alive
and still help people today. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you pray, finish ‘in Jesus’ name’, and remember how powerful His name is.

en.fact: The man was over forty years old and had never walked. Muscles that have never been used are usually very weak, so it was a double miracle that he could jump straight away!
en.deeper: Why do you think Peter said, ‘Look at us’?
en.journal: Draw the man jumping at the Beautiful Gate. Write: ‘In Jesus’ name, walk!’
